News.title: Reform vows to ban foreign graduates who fail to repay student loans from UK
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

International graduates owing student loan debts would face entry bans to the UK unless they settle their balances under new proposals put forward by Reform UK.

The party further stated that visas held by foreign students currently residing in the UK would be cancelled if they fall behind on their repayments.

According to Reform’s figures, European Union citizens residing overseas have failed to pay approximately £360 million over the past 12 months.

Party data indicates that out of 103,400 EU citizens abroad earning above the repayment threshold, 43,700 (42%) made no single repayment.

Reform claims that total unrecovered debts from overseas students could eventually exceed £1.5 billion.

At present, around 172,000 EU students hold £6.23 billion in outstanding UK loans.

Criticising previous administrations, Reform’s home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf said: "Tory and Labour governments have helped foreign nationals scam British taxpayers.

"British people will rightly be furious to learn foreign students have come here using loans funded by British taxpayers, only to flee.

"This scam has already cost the British taxpayer £360 million.

"Reform will end the scam.

"No more taxpayer-funded loans for foreign students, and those failing to make the repayments will be banned from entering Britain.

"We will stand up for British people."

The political party previously committed to completely barring non-UK students from receiving state-backed student finance, proposing instead to reallocate those funds towards establishing 600,000 apprenticeships.

While standard international students are not eligible for public loans, EU citizens who secured settled status following Brexit retain eligibility.

News.title: Elon Musk’s government funding for SpaceX is on the line, top Democrat warns
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A top Democrat warned Elon Musk that “every” U.S. government contract with SpaceX has been called into question, the latest sign that congressional Democrats are preparing to investigate Donald Trump’s administration officials and his allies.

Connecticut Rep. Jim Himes, who is poised to lead the House Intelligence Committee in January, issued the warning in a letter to the SpaceX CEO Friday, demanding answers about last month’s disruptions in Ukraine to Starshield, a U.S. government-purchased service that uses SpaceX’s Starlink satellite network.

Musk acknowledged in an October post on X that the company intentionally restricted its Starlink service in Ukraine, hindering military efforts to combat Russia. He claimed Ukraine violated Starlink’s terms by using the civilian commercial service for “offensive drone strikes.” Starshield, he added, is controlled by the U.S. government.

“I write to formally request that senior SpaceX officials meet with me to explain the Starshield service disruptions in Ukraine in October 2026,” Himes wrote in his letter. “My committee staff have requested this briefing on multiple occasions but have received no substantive response from your company.”

Himes said Starshield’s reliance on Starlink satellites — more than 10,000 of which are in orbit — does not give SpaceX the right to make “unilateral” changes to the government-contracted service.

open image in gallery A top Democrat warned Elon Musk that ‘every’ U.S. government contract with SpaceX has been called into question following service disruptions in Ukraine last month ( Getty Images )

“My view, which I have conveyed to senior Administration officials, is that SpaceX’s potentially unilateral modification of a U.S. Government contract, combined with its lack of responsiveness to congressional oversight, calls into question every contract the U.S. Government has with SpaceX,” he wrote.

“For that reason, it is difficult for me to continue supporting the authorization of funding for ... SpaceX-developed, government-owned systems until I receive satisfactory answers,” he added.

SpaceX, which went public in June, had about $22 billion in government contracts as of last February.

“SpaceX has done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth BY FAR,” Musk wrote on X last month. “That said, I have nothing but UTTER CONTEMPT for the virtue-signaling evil warmongers who push for endless slaughter and offer no realistic solution to the conflict.”

The war in Ukraine, which began with Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, has dragged on for more than four years, claiming hundreds of thousands of lives. Repeated efforts by the Trump administration to broker a peace deal have so far failed.

The Independent has contacted the company for comment.

open image in gallery More than 10,000 Starlink satellites are currently in orbit. Pictured: SpaceX Starship Flight 14 launches from its launch pad at Boca Chica Beach on September 28 in Boca Chica Beach, Texas ( Getty Images )

Himes’ letter is the latest sign that Democrats plan to probe Trump administration officials and allies when they take control of Congress in January following their midterm election victories.

Asked about Musk last week, House Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries vowed to investigate “everyone” involved in the “MAGA extremist movement.” Musk, who spearheaded DOGE and donated millions to Republicans, recently declared he is “not MAGA” despite campaigning for the president in his signature black MAGA hat.

Also last week, Rep. Robert Garcia, the Oversight Committee’s top Democrat, wrote letters to a dozen administration officials and others in Trump’s orbit, requesting that they preserve documents, signaling an investigation could be forthcoming.

Among those who received letters were President Donald Trump’s eldest sons, Vice President JD Vance and Attorney General Todd Blanche.

In an apparent bid to thwart Democratic investigations, the White House has instructed federal officials and government contractors to obtain permission before testifying on Capitol Hill.

Blanche has said the Department of Justice will cooperate with Congress but insisted “we will not back down” from Trump’s agenda.

News.title: 24 dead after boat carrying mourners to funeral capsizes in Nigeria
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

At least 24 have died after a boat carrying mourners to a funeral capsized in southern Nigeria.

Up to 300 people are believed to have been on the vessel when it sank on Friday in Bayelsa State in the country's South South region.

The boat was travelling between communities for a burial service at the time, and search and rescue operations remained underway on Saturday, according to Manzo Ezeki, spokesman for Nigeria's National Emergency Management Agency. He did not clarify how many passengers are still missing.

Police spokesman Musa Mohammed said on Friday that 24 people were rescued and required medical care. The boat, travelling between the villages of Ayama and Ukubie, appeared to have suffered a mechanical failure and capsized at about 1000 GMT, Mohammed said.

Passengers reportedly asked the operator to direct the vessel toward land but he allegedly refused, according to Mohammed. The operator then fled the area and the manager of the boat was taken into custody.

Earlier reports had indicated that two adults and two children died in the accident, while 19 survivors were treated at a local clinic and five others were transferred to a hospital in Yenagoa, the state capital.

Marine police, local divers and other emergency responders continue to search for additional victims.

Sophie Igoniwari, a witness, described chaotic boarding and overcrowding before the boat left Ayama. Igoniwari said that several victims were brought ashore after the boat capsized shortly after departure.

Boat accidents are common on Nigeria's inland waterways, especially in riverine communities where overcrowding is widespread and safety regulations are often ignored. Faulty boats without life jackets sometimes operate in the country due to a lack of enforcement of safety requirements.

The Bayelsa state government responded to the tragedy by urging boat operators and passengers to adhere to safety regulations.

“Overloading, speeding, recklessness and traveling without life jackets must stop. No journey is worth a life,” Bayelsa Commissioner for Information Ebiuwou Koku-Obiyai said in a statement on Saturday.

News.title: Jodie Foster reveals her favorite film ‘ever’ that she’s watched ‘over 100 times’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Jodie Foster has confessed that her favorite movie of all-time isn’t a comedy or a thriller, but rather a Disney animated classic.

The Oscar-winning Silence of the Lambs actor recently revealed that she’s seen The Lion King “way over a hundred times.”

“Gosh, because I had two sons during the whole animation fever, so I’ve seen every animated movie you could ever imagine in my era,” she told People on the red carpet for her new Disney animated movie Hexed.

“But Lion King is my favorite movie ever,” she said.

Foster, 64, has lent her own voice to Disney’s Hexed. The film follows teenager Billie (Hailee Steinfeld) who discovers that she and her mother, Alive (Rashida Jones), are witches with the ability to travel to a magical realm. Foster voices Queen Celeste, the witches’ evil ruler.

open image in gallery Jodie Foster said her favorite movie is ‘The Lion King’ ( Getty )

Speaking about playing the villainous role, she told People that it was “totally fun.”

“It’s always fun playing a villain because they’re honest people,” Foster continued. “They’re honestly bad and they’re unashamed of living up to their destiny as villains. There’s something about that honestly that’s always really compelling where you’re just like, ‘Ooh, I can’t believe she said that.’”

To prepare for the red carpet premiere of Hexed, Foster participated in one of her lucky rituals. She told People she is sure to “always wear a certain perfume,” adding that she never wears perfume “pretty much ever, except when I go to a movie premiere.”

“It’s vetiver,” Foster said of the scent.

open image in gallery Foster said she’s seen ‘The Lion King’ ‘way over a hundred times’ ( Getty )

“Beyond that though, I think it’s more just make sure you have the right underclothes,” she added of her preparation for big events.

Foster added that she’s often trying to manifest good outcomes, saying that she’s become “a little more superstitious as I get older.”

“I feel like I have many superstitions,”the Taxi Driver star said. “I don’t know if it’s superstitions, but I do things to ensure a good outcome. If it doesn’t work, I don’t care, but I just want to make sure that I put my finger on the scale a little bit.”

“So, I have lucky things, I do, I suppose, and it seems to get more and more as I get older. I get a little more superstitious as I get older,” she continues. “You would think it would be the opposite, but it’s getting worse.”

News.title: Princess of Wales shares emotional hug with children in new cancer documentary
News.content:
The Princess of Wales shared a poignant moment with her children in a trailer for a new documentary in which she reflects on her cancer diagnosis.

Heal will follow Kate as she undertakes the Three Peaks Challenge – climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours.

The princess is seen hugging her husband, the Prince of Wales, and their children George, Charlotte and Louis at the end of the challenge.

Kate says in the trailer: “Cancer does change you. It changes your body. It changes you physically.

“But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.”

Heal will premiere on the BBC in the UK on November 29. All funds received through the documentary’s distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, Kensington Palace said.

News.title: South Africa coaching staff deny Rassie Erasmus contact during Ireland defeat
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

South Africa’s coaching staff denied suggestions they were receiving instructions from suspended head coach Rassie Erasmus during Saturday’s 20-17 defeat to Ireland in Dublin.

Erasmus, who was barred from any having any involvement in matchday activity as part of his six-game ban from World Rugby, hosted a live watch-along from the team’s hotel.

The 54-year-old was muted for large spells of the online event but could be seen speaking to an unknown party while wearing earbuds and covering his mouth.

open image in gallery Mzwandile Stick stood in for Rassie Erasmus at the Aviva Stadium ( PA )

Asked if Erasmus was passing on messages, Springboks assistant coach Felix Jones said: “I’ve no idea, we were busy with a Test match.”

Fellow assistant coach Mzwandile Stick added: “Maybe he was communicating with his followers on that party that he was having, but with us we were just in the game.”

Build-up to the heavyweight contest at the Aviva Stadium was dominated by Erasmus being sanctioned after questioning the integrity of match officials following his side’s 21-19 defeat to France.

Jones said the situation was not a distraction as the Springboks slipped to a second successive loss before questions on Erasmus were quickly shut down by the team’s media officer.

Ireland head coach Andy Farrell savoured a “big night for everyone who’s Irish” and a major stepping stone in his side’s journey towards next year’s World Cup.

open image in gallery Andy Farrell hailed a great performance from Ireland ( PA )

Robert Baloucoune claimed two first-half tries and Ronan Kelleher added another, with a long-range penalty from Sam Prendergast ultimately proving decisive amid a colossal defensive effort.

“It’s something that we’ve been looking forward to and tried to challenge ourselves with about delivering when it matters against top line sides,” said Farrell.

“We knew that this fixture was coming, playing against the world’s best – world’s best by a stretch at this moment in time, I would have thought so.

“It was a game that we wanted to challenge ourselves and see how we went and obviously fronting up and showing the character that we did and coming out the right side of the win is a big night for everyone who’s Irish.”

South Africa ensured a pulsating encounter remained tantalisingly poised until the final whistle thanks to scores from Morne van den Berg and Malcolm Marx, plus seven points from the boot of Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu.

“I think we’ve taken a step forward and that was the aim,” said Farrell.

“This game mattered to us in how we prepped for it. We didn’t shy away from that and we took it on for what it was, which was a top of the tree game.

“We were able to perform. It wasn’t perfect but we managed to come out with a win. The World Cup, it’s all about stepping stones and this is a big one that’s for sure.”

Despite their defeat, South Africa progressed to the Nations Championship final at Twickenham after picking up a losing bonus point.

Ireland will likely contest the fifth-place final against either Argentina or Australia.

open image in gallery Ireland players celebrate (Brian Lawless/PA)

Asked about Erasmus, Farrell said: “Rassie is his own man and he’s a smart guy. He does things for a reason.

“There’s always going to be a plan or whatever. I don’t know the ins and outs of it.

“The South African boys are in our dressing room having a beer and it’s an unspoken rule that you just leave it alone really I would have thought. It is what it is.”

PA

News.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to have proved Riemann hypothesis with help of Claude
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A mathematician working for the AI company Anthropic claims to have proved the Riemann hypothesis – the most famous unsolved problem in the mathematical world – using the large language model Claude.

The hypothesis, first proposed in 1859 by Germany’s Bernhard Riemann, claims that the location of prime numbers along the number line are not random, but are instead determined by a meaningful order.

It is of importance to mathematicians because it links the distribution of prime numbers to a precise pattern.

The hypothesis was identified by influential mathematician David Hilbert in 1900 as one of his 23 mathematical challenges for the 20th century.

In 2000, the Clay Mathematics Institute offered a $1 million reward for anyone who could prove the hypothesis.

Anthropic’s Dr Levent Alpöge claimed the breakthrough in a statement posted to his website on Friday.

Dr Levent Alpöge, right, pictured with fellow mathematician Bernard Saint-Donat, claims to have proved the Riemann hypothesis ( Getty )

“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” he wrote.

“It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.”

Dr Alpöge has released a version of the proof which is written in the computer code Lean, which is used to verify the mathematical correctness of arguments.

Experts will now need to examine whether the work is properly coded and if the hypothesis has, indeed, been proved.

Dr Alpöge, who holds dual United States and Turkish citizenship, has an MA from Harvard, a Master of Advanced Studies from the University of Cambridge, and a PhD from Princeton.

In July, he made headlines when he posted a counterexample to the famous Jacobian conjecture, a well-known problem in the field of algebraic geometry.

Like his work on the Riemann hypothesis, he had used Claude to make the discovery.

“hello there the jacobian conjecture is false thanx to my close friend akhil for asking about it and my other close friend fable for working during the world cup final,” he posted on X (formerly Twitter).

Dr Alpöge’s statement on the Riemann hypothesis on Friday was slightly longer and more erudite.

“I hope the argument provides a glimpse towards the miracles that lie ahead, and shows us the joy and wonder we are about to find in the simplest things,” he wrote.

News.title: Arsenal arrogance is their downfall but Madueke rescues point at Newcastle
News.content:
Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “My feeling is that we lost two points today. I think we were exceptional in the first half. At every level. Our intensity, the clarity that we have, how to attack the jumps of Newcastle every time they wanted to go man-to-man, the composure that we have, the way we use our relationship to break their press. And it should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up, clear.

“But it wasn’t. And when it wasn’t, then we expected in the second half that we have to again raise the level because the opponent is going to have a reaction. And the opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. And then we gave them belief.

“And I say we give them belief because we give them a goal, we give them a throw-in that we just give them the ball. We have no structure to control the opposite winger. We concede a goal and it’s game on. And from that it became a very chaotic game. Every set-piece, we know that they are exceptional at it and we concede from a set piece.

“And then you have to react. And then we went back to the team that the exceptional team that we were in the first half again for another 25 minutes and we scored a great goal. We create infinity of openings to create and score the third goal, but we lack some time or to be precise, to make that count.”

News.title: ‘Remarkable’ Ireland deliver perfect riposte to Erasmus mind games
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Ireland vs South Africa from the Nations Championship in Dublin, with both teams harbouring hopes of finishing the day at the top of their respective tables.

Ireland and South Africa have both won four of their five games in the group phase of this year’s inaugural Nations Championship, and come into their last match before next weekend’s finals still in contention for the overall title.

Andy Farrell’s men begin the afternoon in third in the Northern Hemisphere table, but level on points with second-placed England, who are currently hosting New Zealand, and just one point behind leaders France, who take on Argentina this evening.

The reigning world champions, meanwhile, are guaranteed to at least remain in second in the Southern Hemisphere table, but are just one point behind the All Blacks at the top of the group, so will be hoping for a favour from Steve Borthwick’s men at Twickenham.

The Springboks will be without head coach Rassie Erasmus for today’s contest in the Irish capital, with the 54-year-old facing a six-match ban because of his criticism of officials following his team’s narrow defeat by France last weekend, including asking whether they were “match-fixing”.

“He’s been hands-on with our team, and we’re in a good space,” assistant coach Mzwandile Stick said of Erasmus on Friday. “Irrespective of what has happened, we love him, we appreciate him, and no one is going to break us. I can tell you that for sure.”

In the same press conference, Erasmus predicted that Sam Prendergast would be cleared to play after being cited for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji. The Ireland fly-half escaped punishment from the independent panel and starts for Farrell’s side this afternoon.

News.title: Alonso heckled as Chelsea are humiliated by Leeds
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

“(We need) the whole team for that,” said Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

“It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

“We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his new-look group.

“There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a big shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

“It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

News.title: England obliterate All Blacks in record win
News.content:
A nearly perfect half for England was ruined just two minutes before half-time when Ben Earl gave up a penalty from the restart, immediately after scoring the home side’s third try. New Zealand kicked to the corner and Ethan de Groot plunged over to give the All Blacks a lifeline they scarcely deserve.

Until that point, this was as dominant a half against top-tier opposition that we have ever seen from Steve Borthwick’s team. Much like they did against Australia, England have strangled the life out of New Zealand and have enjoyed a preposterous 78 per cent territory.

They have also repeatedly cut New Zealand open in midfield. The interplay between Fin Smith, Seb Atkinson and the regal George Furbank has been sumptuous to watch. England have struggled to break New Zealand down in the red zone but still have three tries to show for their efforts. Smith’s cute little poke through was grounded by Henry Slade after five minutes and then scrum half Jack van Poortvliet did his best Superman impression by diving over the top of a ruck for England’s second try.

Earl also went route one, picking off the back of a scrum and through Cam Roigard’s tackle to put England in dreamland. Not every department has functioned perfectly. New Zealand have been on top of the scrum and have stopped the English maul in its tracks, but the All Blacks have been dominated physically. When was the last time we said that about an England team?

The De Groot try has taken the wind out of England’s sails a little but a similar setback took place in the Australia game just before half-time and Borthwick’s team responded with an emphatic second-half performance.

England need to see this out too, otherwise they’ll be kicking themselves all the way through to the World Cup.

News.title: England lose to ‘Australia B team’ in thriller
News.content:
England’s white-ball tour of Australia continues as a five-match T20 series between kicks off in Melbourne at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground, with the sandpapergate saga rumbling on. The first part of the tour went England’s way, as they came from 1-0 down to win the ODI series 2-1, following wins in Adelaide and Hobart. All of that action on the field has taken place whilst there has been plenty of “he said, she said” as some, like Cameron Bancroft, David Warner and Usman Khawaja say that everyone knew about the use of sandpaper whilst Pat Cummins has categorically denied that.

The last time these sides met in a T20 series back in September 2024, the three-match series ended in a 1-1 draw, with the final match abandoned. England won the last series played down under in October 2022, claiming a 2-0 series victory. Therefore, England are unbeaten in their past three bilateral mens’s T20I series against Australia. England are currently top of the ICC T20 rankings, with Australia third.

England were last in T20 action back in September, when they beat Sri Lanka 3-0. They have won all but two completed T20Is in 2026, with their last defeat coming in the World Cup semi-finals against India in March. They have decided to rest a number of the seamers who played in the ODI series including Jofra Archer and Gus Atkinson, whilst Josh Tongue is out injured. With those seamers absent, it will likely present opportunities for Henry Crocombe and Eddie Jack. Jacob Bethell remains out with a knee injury that he is still struggling with whilst Jos Buttler continues to recover from an hamstring injury.

Australia bombed out of the T20 World Cup in the group stages earlier this year, the first time that has happened since 2009. They did though win their most recent T20 series, beating Bangladesh 3-0 in June. Australia’s fast-bowling trio of Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood have all been rested for England’s white-ball tour, something that was planned long before the 2018 sandpapergate was reignited. Not only are that trio not involved but the likes of Nathan Ellis and Xavier Bartlett will also not play, therefore it will be a relatively inexperienced bowling attack for the hosts.

They will give a debut to wicketkeeper Sam Harper, who was named player of the tournament in the most recent edition of the Big Bash with the Melbourne Stars, with Josh Inglis being rested ahead of Australia’s upcoming busy Test schedule. Inglis is not the only player to sit out this series having played in the ODIs, with the likes of Travis Head, Matt Renshaw, Cameron Green and Cooper Connolly also not participating.

Play from the MCG gets under way from 8.15am GMT.

News.title: Anthropic plunges as Wall Street suffers AI sell-off
News.content:
Anthropic’s share price slump triggered a sharp sell-off on Wall Street with tech stocks closing down more than 5pc.

More than $163bn was wiped off the value of the AI giant on Friday, just a day after it touched a $2tn valuation on its stock market debut.

The decline prompted a wider flight from AI shares, with the tech-focused Nasdaq 100 down 5.6pc. It means the index has now erased all its gains year to date.

The S&P 500 fell 3.7pc at close, putting it on course for its worst week since Donald Trump’s ‘liberation day’ tariffs last year, and into correction territory.

Anthropic has endured a hugely volatile introduction to public markets, surging as much as 39pc on the Nasdaq on Thursday, before closing the day 17pc higher.

However, it fell by as much as 14pc to $83.16 on Friday, just above where it started trading on Thursday.

It started the day at $97, less than 24 hours after it hit a high of $115.

The latest sell-off has fuelled fears that the company’s record-breaking float, which raised $87bn, is not enough to dispel lingering concerns over the AI bubble.

It comes after a series of threats to the investment boom.

That includes anti-data centre Democrats taking control of Congress, the downfall of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang and tighter export controls on chips to China.

The Philadelphia semiconductor index, a grouping of the major US chip companies, dropped by as much as 9pc on Friday.

AI-linked companies dragged the Nasdaq lower, with the likes of semiconductor maker ARM losing 14pc.

CoreWeave also weighed on the Nasdaq, with its shares down 12pc.

European shares were also on track for their worst week since March amid investor concern over an AI bubble.

In a day of volatile swings on Wall Street, Nvidia also slipped behind Google parent Alphabet to become the fourth-most valuable US company.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “It’s been another hectic and negative week and one where even positive news is struggling to help the market stabilise.”

Pressure on stocks also rose after Donald Trump on Friday threatened to ban technology companies from building data centres outside of the US.

In a White House press conference, Mr Trump warned there would be “tremendous penalties” on US companies that tried to build data centres in foreign countries.

He said: “We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centres outside of our country. We’re not going to allow that to happen.”

He added: “We’re going to fight very hard for the data centres because we’re not going to let China [overtake us].”

The ban threat will raise questions for AI developers who are spending hundreds of billions of pounds building data facilities in the UK, Europe and across Asia.

It is not clear whether Mr Trump’s ban would apply to all data centre developers or just the most advanced facilities.

The sell-off came as Anthropic’s approach to copyright was slammed by news publishers, who said the company lacks “a basic moral compass”.

The News Media Association (NMA), which represents titles including The Telegraph, The Times and The Guardian, attacked the company for its policy on journalism.

Anthropic told investors it could not guarantee it would adhere to measures that prevented journalism from being used to train AI models.

The Claude maker said it took steps to abide by paywalls but that this “may not always be successful”.

News.title: New case of bird flu confirmed in US dairy farm worker
News.content:
Another person in the US has contracted H5N1, bringing the number of confirmed cases in the country this year to four.

The patient, whose identity has not been released, works on a dairy farm in the US state of Oregon, local health officials confirmed on Thursday.

Their symptoms are reportedly mild, and they do not require hospitalisation.

All four of the H5N1 cases recorded in the US this year – one of whom died – have been in dairy workers who have had close contact with sick cattle.

The virus, which experts have long warned could trigger the next human pandemic, has become endemic in US dairy cattle after ‘jumping’ from birds to cows in late 2023.

Since then, it has been detected on nearly 1,000 dairy farms across dozens of states.

The US has reported 74 human cases of bird flu since 2024, nearly all of which have been from close contact with poultry or cows.

Earlier this month, United Farm Workers (UFW), a union which represents thousands of workers across the US, released a statement on X that said many farmers were experiencing symptoms of H5N1 and were not being tested for the virus.

They said the workers’ symptoms ranged from “very mild to very severe” and that surveillance on farms had been poor.

News.title: Violence and mistrust hamper Ebola response
News.content:
Six months after the deadly Bundibugyo Ebola virus flared in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the outbreak is far from under control.

Scores of new cases of the deadly haemorrhagic fever are being recorded every day and half of those diagnosed go on to die.

The official toll of 11,000 cases and more than 5,400 deaths is likely to be a vast underestimate and the outbreak is more than halfway to becoming the largest ever recorded.

Beyond the bare figures, aid agencies and emergency responders are also increasingly warning about the chaos, disorganisation and violence hampering the response.

Among the most worrying markers is that with 400 to 500 new cases reported every week, some two-thirds of deaths are occurring outside Ebola treatment centres.

Epidemiologists warn that figure is a sure sign cases are spreading undetected and that the tracking and quarantining of suspected patients is not working.

The outbreak has become like a deadly game of whack-a-mole, with new hotspots emerging just as responders manage to gain control over some of the early epicentres.

“Progress in some places is not control of the outbreak as a whole,” Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director general of the World Health Organization (WHO), warned this week.

FURIOUS Cole Palmer snubbed the home fans and even appeared to have an angry exchange with Joao Pedro after their 4-1 defeat to Leeds.

Furious fans booed their side at half-time and the final whistle, with Palmer refusing to applaud them after being asked to by staff.



The Blues took the lead against Daniel Farke’s side, Emmanuel Emegha scoring his first goal for the club.

But after losing Moises Caicedo to injury, and Leeds creating chances, the hosts collapsed to suffer their third defeat in four Premier League games.



Noah Okafor scored twice, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson also getting a goal each.

At full time, Chelsea players went to applaud those fans who had stayed until the end but Palmer can be spotted seething as he exited the West London pitch.

Careful to mask his words with his hand, Palmer strutted up to team-mate Pedro with a furrowed brow obviously exasperated by the result as Chelsea slipped to eighth.

The Brazilian seemingly has no explanation for Palmer, who sidled off in a huff back to changing rooms while Pedro continued to try and talk it out.

Having been bullied by Sunderland before the international break, this was another difficult defeat for Alonso & Co so early in his tenure – his fifth Premier League loss in 11.

Sports.title: Bayern Munich slammed for ‘putting pressure’ on Jamal Musiala with ‘deeply concerning’ comments about his health
Sports.content:
Next

FIFPRO are “deeply concerned” with Bayern Munich’s comments on Jamal Musiala’s ongoing health problems.

The Germany international, 23, revealed in August he was being treated for a “neurological dysfunction” after fainting in successive pre-season games.



He returned to play for Bayern early in the season but a subsequent muscle injury has limited him to five games.

Musiala, who spent time in Chelsea’s academy, played for the first time since September with 20 minutes off the bench against Cologne on Friday.



Speaking after the 1-1 draw, which saw Harry Kane forced off with an ankle injury that required surgery, Bayern board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge admitted the club are assessing Musiala’s future.

Musiala signed a contract extension last year until 2030, which is understood to have made him one of Bayern’s highest-paid players.



Rummenigge said: “He has a health-related issue. It’s also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money.

“As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. What we know unfortunately suggests it will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has often shown here.

“These sums of money, with all due respect, are no longer feasible. I cannot imagine that Jamal wants to leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions.”

FIFPro, the world footballers’ union, said they were “deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from Bayern Munich’s leadership”.



They added: “In FIFPRO’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.

“Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player’s future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

“Making Musiala’s health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.”

The champions gifted Newcastle an equaliser as Harvey Barnes levelled.

Sports.title: Newcastle 2 Arsenal 2: Noni Madueke rescues point for Gunners after Toon’s thrilling second-half fightback
Sports.content:
Next

THERE was a huge groan around St James’ Park when it was announced that there would be NINE minutes of stoppage time.

But unlike last season, when Arsenal stole three points with Gabriel Magalhaes snatching a 96th minute winner, there was no Newcastle collapse.



And for the first time this season, Mikel Arteta’s champions have drawn a game.

Arsenal, in control for the fist half, conceded goals number six and seven of the season within 13 minutes of each other.



And on the day defender Wlliam Saliba returned to the matchday squad from injury, there was the worrying sight of keeper David Raya leaving the pitch with what appeared to be a shoulder injury.

For Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, his team did well after a lamentable first half and in the end, they were the most likely to score.

Yet things were looking straightforward for Arsenal when Eberechi Eze scored his first Premier League goal of the season after a mistake by Lewis Hall.

Harvey Barnes grabbed his 100th career goal and Newcastle breached Arsenel’s defence again with Malick Thiaw scrambling the second.

But after losing keeper Raya after he ran into Will Osula, the champions grabbed a point, Noni Madueke scoring the leveller although Newcastle no 1 Lukas Horniceck was at fault.

By the time of Arsenal’s second goal, Bruno Guimaraes, pantomime villain of the day, was off the pitch.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

When you consider he lifted the Carabao Cup for Newcastle in 2025, Guimaraes was always going to get some stick, even though he has repeatedly declared his love for the club and was respectful.

Yet there will never be some pleasing fans. Nevertheless, Guimaraes was booed as he stepped off the team coach, jeered when he kicked off and this treatment continued with each touch.

Equally, it was nothing like the sort of abuse Alexander Isak received when he returned here with Liverpool earlier in the season.



There was a moment in the first half when the Brazilian would have broken a few hearts, and to make matters worse it was in front of the Gallowgate End, when he made a dash into the box and stuck out a boot to reach Declan Rice’s far post cross but he could not make a proper connection.

That followed Noni Madueke firing a shot against the outside of the post and Kai Havertz sent an effort which flashed wide.

So an Arsenal goal always looked likely but on this occasion, it was completely avoidable. Hall attempted to control Ezri Konsa’s clipped pass with his chest when he should have headed clear.

Yet Havertz was breathing down Hall’s neck and the German nicked the ball before playing a brilliant pass behind Amar Dedic and Eze dispatched a first-time shot past the exposed Hornicek.

Hall was clearly thinking about that mistake as he was caught sleeping while attempting to let the ball go out for a throw. Madueke took possession and attempted to beat Hornicek at his near post but he read what the English international was trying to do.



At least Hall ended the half with a goal-saving tackle to deny Madueke. At half-time, Jaissle made a triple substitution with Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey introduced

And Jaissle got the perfect response as his team seized on some sloppy play by Arsenal. Arteta’s team normally score from dead ball situations rather than concede but Riccardo Calafiori’s throw led to a miskick by Odegaard who was under pressure from Joe Willock but that is still no excuse.

William Osula pounced and threaded a ball for Barnes who was never going to miss from around the penalty spot for his third Premier League goal of the season.



Subdued for all of the game, the home crowd came to life and it felt like the sort of occasion we had so many times under Eddie Howe.

And Arteta will have hoped to weather the storm before making his changes but Newcastle kept pushing and were rewarded again.

Arteta will be annoyed that Burn peeled away and was left unmarked to head Hall’s corner towards the goal. While Willock accidentally block the ball on the line, it felt perfectly for Thiaw.

Arsenal were forced into a triple sub and that included Guimaraes, who was given a final jeer, Eze and keeper Raya who was replaced by Kepa.

Finally, Arsenal woke up threatened. Odegaard found Madueke and he was given far too much space by the home defence although Hornicek should have save the shot as it was straight at him.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Yet Arsenal never looked like grabbing a third and it was Newcastle’s players who left to a standing ovation.

As for Arteta, his main concern will be the injury bulletin from his medical team regarding Raya.

Sports.title: England stars in furious bust-up during Newcastle vs Arsenal as tensions boil over after Dan Burn challenge

ENGLAND stars Dan Burn and Noni Madueke clashed as tensions boiled over in the closing stages of Newcastle’s 2-2 draw at home to Arsenal.

Malick Thiaw got the Geordies dancing in the 62nd minute after finding the back of the net, only for Noni Madueke to drag the Gunners to 2-2.

But minutes after the goal, Jurrien Timber went down on the edge of the pitch after Dan Burn held little back.



Madueke rushed Burn in a rage, squaring up to the 6ft 7in Blyth-born defender.

Declan Rice also appeared to have stepped into the melee, before it was stopped from breaking into a massive brawl around the 80-minute mark.

While both Burn and Madueke featured at this summer’s World Cup in North America, they were involved in zero minutes together.

The closest they got to playing together was the quarter-finals against Norway



But Madueke came off around the hour mark, while Burn was subbed on for the last ten minutes.

Both Burn and Madueke received bookings as the game was thrown into disarray, having already seen Arsenal shot-stopper David Raya come off clutching his shoulder.

The Spain international was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga, while former Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes was also taken off.

Both sides battled to find another goal in the remaining time but even with nine minutes of injury time, the tense clash ended in a draw.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta has given Man Utd the perfect blueprint - but INEOS have to completely change
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has given Man Utd the perfect blueprint - but INEOS have to completely change

Mauricio Pochettino has now started work at Manchester United and if he's in need of any inspiration when it comes to turning a club's fortunes around, he should look no further than his old PSG team-mate Mikel Arteta

View 3 Images

Anfield feels an entirely fitting venue to uncover the size of the task Mauricio Pochettino has on his hands. It's a bear pit at the best of times - not least when there's an opportunity to inflict early misery upon a brand-new Manchester United manager.

‌



‌



For Liverpool, chances as good as this do not come around often. Sleep-deprived Poch heads to Merseyside with a blank canvas for a match poised to underline the importance of patience.

‌



Just ask the 54-year-old's former Paris Saint-Germain team-mate, Mikel Arteta. The Spaniard recently masterminded Arsenal's first Premier League victory at Anfield since 2012, when he was a player.

‌



However, it was also a landmark triumph that stretched far beyond three crucial and priceless top-flight points. That's because it also symbolised the Gunners' growth and ascension into a red-hot, rock-solid established force.

The champions are not everyone's cup of tea but under Arteta they have gone from a laughing stock to a serious outfit, capable of going toe-to-toe with just about any team on the planet.

They were thrashed 7-1 on aggregate across his first two league visits to Liverpool as Arsenal manager but after three defeats and three draws, Arsenal finally silenced The Kop on November 1 - without conceding a single shot on target.

‌



Some 25 years ago - during an 18-month loan spell with PSG - fresh-faced teenager Arteta did everything within his power to learn from Pochettino in the French capital.

Now the tables have turned because despite his respectable coaching pedigree, Poch simply has to try and emulate what Arteta has created, sculpted and gradually built at the Emirates - which has not happened overnight.

‌



It won't be a universally popular take, but the Basque is currently the gold-standard Premier League coach.

Having tinkered, controlled and overseen the seismic transformation of a big prestigious football club - while regularly competing with iconic managerial juggernauts such as Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp - Arteta has undeniably set the benchmark where rebuilds are concerned.

‌



View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has worked wonders at Arsenal but he needed significant backing from upstairs to turn the club's fortunes around (Image: Pavel Lebeda/Soccrates/Getty Images)

The great irony of it all is that Arsenal genuinely gave some consideration to offering Pochettino the job, ahead of Arteta, back in 2019.

‌



Whether he would have taken it, on the back of his love affair with Tottenham, is a question we will never truly know the answer to but ultimately, there is no guarantee he would have had the same level of success as the title-winning Men's Coach of the Year nominee.

Equally, Arteta couldn't have done it without significant backing. He flirted with the sack in August 2021 following a 5-0 drubbing at Manchester City but dared to be great by slowly discarding the club's top-earners such as Mesut Ozil and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, respectively.

‌



Pochettino, who has long been eyeing the keys to the kingdom at Old Trafford, knows a thing or two about squad-building having fired Spurs to the Champions League final seven-and-a-half years ago.

The United is an entirely different beast, however. In many respects, it has been a poisoned chalice since the departure of Sir Alex Ferguson back in 2013.

‌



The Argentine needs time to implement his ideas but with INEOS under greater scrutiny than ever following a series of high-profile mistakes, he's entering a pressure-cooker environment that has eaten up so many of his predecessors.

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first Manchester United match this weekend (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Given United are currently languishing in the relegation zone, swift results also feel somewhat imperative because commercially, the club needs Champions League football to flex their muscles in the transfer market.

Then there's an entirely separate argument that Pochettino is already handicapped by the faulty regime working above him.

‌



It's been claimed the Glazers overruled Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada in signing off the hire. Should that be true, the lack of alignment is a huge issue in itself while player recruitment under director of football Wilcox has been dismal.

On the back of a top-five finish under Michael Carrick, United needed to be efficient and clinical in the market. Instead, they burned cash and the team regressed.

‌



Pochettino is also the fourth head coach in situ in the past three years under Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

There is still no identity, no direction - it's chalk and cheese when compared with Arteta's working conditions at Arsenal - and until bold changes are made, the same problems will remain.

Sports.title: Newcastle and Arsenal play out thrilling draw as new Gunners concern emerges
Sports.content:
Newcastle United and Arsenal both had to settle for a point after a rollercoaster Premier League clash ended 2-2.

Eberechi Eze put the Gunners in front, before Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw turned the game on its head after the break. But Noni Madueke's goal was enough to secure Arsenal the point which moved them six clear at the top.

The Gunners quickly assumed control in front of a Newcastle crowd which was struggling to warm to new manager Matthias Jaissle.

After a tepid opening 45, Jaissle made a triple change and that sparked an immediate transformation with Barnes scoring the equaliser, before Thiaw put them in front just after the hour mark.

Arsenal suffer brutal injury blow as David Raya leaves the pitch in agony vs Newcastle READ MORE :

Arsenal and Newcastle given detested new kick-off time for Premier League clash READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The visitors' night got even worse when David Raya was forced to leave the pitch with a worrying injury to his shoulder. But with Newcastle in the ascendancy, Arsenal showed their resilience to restore parity through Madueke.

Both sides pushed for a winner, but even with nine minutes added on, neither side were able to nick all three points.. Here's what we learned from an enthralling tie at St James' Park.

ARSENAL MISS THEIR CHANCE

Nobody of an Arsenal persuasion wanted to admit it, but when they were leading, dominating and about to go eight points clear at the top, they must have thought it. Could we be heading towards a title procession?

Manchester City - ignoring the obvious elephant in the courtroom - look miles off the pace, while Liverpool have their own issues. Brighton are a good story and have looked brilliant, but it still feels unlikely they can match Arsenal over a 38-game season.

And while they still have a very healthy lead, this is a slight dent to the feeling of inevitability that would have accompanied a sixth straight win.

BRUNO'S UNHAPPY RETURN

Newcastle fans started their Premier League season by giving Alexander Isak an exceptionally hostile return to St James’ Park. That was to be expected, given the manner of the Swede’s exit and his antics before sealing a move to Liverpool.

Bruno Guimaraes may have been hoping for a more pleasant reunion with the supporters that once adored him. After all, as recently as September, the Brazilian goaded Sunderland following his winning goal on Wearside

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes returned to Newcastle for the first time since his move to Arsenal

But if that was an attempt to curry favour with the Toon Army, it didn’t have much impact. He was roundly booed as he came off the Arsenal bus, but that was nothing compared to the reception each and every time he touched the ball.

The cauldron created for Isak’s return helped the home team get a result and while not as vitriolic as that afternoon, the atmosphere played a huge part again.

Guimaraes didn't have his best evening in an Arsenal shirt and Arteta’s decision to withdraw the midfielder as they chased an equaliser brought a cheer as loud as either goal.

SEASON-DEFINING CHANGE

Jaissle needed something. While it hasn’t been a disastrous start to his tenure in the Toon dugout, supporters remained firmly unconvinced.

After watching back-to-back home defeats, a lifeless first half did little to win over any doubters. But the 15 minutes following the first 45 could be the period that completely changes the narrative on Tyneside.

View 4 Images Matthias Jaissle got the reaction he wanted after ringing the changes at half time

For just the second time this season a Premier League manager made three changes at the break, such was the level of their first-half display. Fair to say it had an impact.

The comeback didn’t appear on the cards. Until it was. Newcastle looked like a team reborn in the second half and although it was only good enough for a point, the comeback offered a glimpse of what Jaissle’s team could really become.

RAYA CONCERN

The sight of David Raya going down in the Arsenal penalty area isn't an uncommon one. After shaking off a collision to the head, when he went down holding his shoulder many assumed the Spaniard had gone down for tactical reasons rather than anything more serious.

View 4 Images David Raya left the game with an injury

But after lengthy treatment, Raya trudged off the pitch in agony with what appeared to be a shoulder injury. It can't be emphasised enough just how important the World Cup winner is to Arsenal's mean defence.

Kepa is a capable deputy, but a long period without their number one, after finally seeing William Saliba return to fitness would be a bitter blow for Arteta to swallow.

Sports.title: Arsenal suffer brutal injury blow as David Raya leaves the pitch in agony vs Newcastle
Sports.content:
Arsenal suffer brutal injury blow as David Raya leaves the pitch in agony vs Newcastle

David Raya was forced off injured in the second half against Newcastle, and Mikel Arteta will be fearing the worst after his keeper looked in real pain as he trudged off the pitch

View 3 Images David Raya looked to be in real discomfort as the Arsenal star was forced off vs Newcastle

David Raya has handed Arsenal a huge injury worry after being forced off in the second half against Newcastle. The Arsenal goalkeeper fought back tears as he appeared to collide innocuously with William Osula when he looked to distribute the ball before having to go off, clutching his arm.

‌



Raya immediately went down despite replays showing minimal contact. However, Mikel Arteta had to turn to Kepa Arrizabalaga, with his No. 1 looking to be in real discomfort as he left the pitch with an Arsenal physio.

The 31-year-old, who is an integral part of Arsenal's team, having kept seven clean sheets in the opening ten Premier League matches of the season, was treated on the pitch before heading off and now looks set to spend some time on the sidelines.

Xabi Alonso speaks out as Chelsea fans turn on manager after Leeds thrashing READ MORE :

Enzo Maresca reveals exactly what Erling Haaland said during Man City VAR controversy READ MORE :

The Spaniard's injury occurred in the 69th minute, with the home side leading 2-1 after a spirited fightback. Eberechi Eze had given the Gunners the lead after a superbly weighted pass from Kai Havertz, with Newcastle heading into the break to a chorus of boos.

However, the match flipped on its head after Matthias Jaissle's men came firing out of the blocks in the second half, equalising through Harvey Barnes in the 49th minute before Malick Thiaw bundled home from point-blank range to put them in front.

St James' Park had to face a nervous wait with VAR checking a handball before awarding Thiaw's goal. Minutes later, Raya went down after colliding with Osula. The incident happened shortly after another challenge between him and Joe Willock.

View 3 Images Raya received treatment on the pitch before being substituted (Image: Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The distressed-looking Raya caused some surprise as he headed off the pitch, and even received an apology from Sky Sports commentator Bill Leslie, who speculated that there might be some play-acting going on.

"David Raya does indeed look in some discomfort. Apologies if I did him a disservice there because it really didn’t look like significant contact with Osula," he said.

Chris Sutton added: "Raya is holding his arm; it looks like there’s some sort of sprain. He is in a lot of pain. It really did look innocuous, didn’t it, the coming together."

Kepa, who had only played one Carabao Cup match this season before Sunday, was then called upon for the final 20 minutes. With the Premier League leaders chasing, Arteta also turned to his bench again moments later, bringing on Christos Tzolis and Myles Lewis-Skelly for scorer Eberechi Eze and Bruno Guimaraes, who was given a tough reception all afternoon by the boo boys at his former club.

View 3 Images Noni Madueke earned a point for Arsenal with a late strike in the second half (Image: Getty Images)

The substitutes weren't involved, but Arteta got the response he was hoping for in the 78th minute, with Noni Madueke getting the better of Lukas Hornicek with a low deflected shot after being teed up by Martin Odegaard.

With title rivals Manchester City slipping up earlier in the day, drawing 1-1 with Fulham, Arteta would've been keen to claim all three points to extend their lead at the top even further, but was made to settle for a point, leaving them six points above Brighton, having played a game more.

However, the injury to Raya will be a huge cause of concern for the Spanish boss and Arsenal fans, with the champions taking on City next weekend, before crunch fixtures against the likes of Real Madrid, Tottenham and Manchester United before Christmas.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso speaks out as Chelsea fans turn on manager after Leeds thrashing
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso speaks out as Chelsea fans turn on manager after Leeds thrashing

Chelsea were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, with Xabi Alonso already under pressure just 11 games into his tenure as manager

View 2 Images Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso during his side's 4-1 defeat to Leeds

Xabi Alonso admits his Chelsea side are struggling in all aspects of the game after their painful home defeat to Leeds.

‌



‌



After taking the lead through Emmanuel Emegha, Chelsea capitulated, eventually losing 4-1 to Daniel Farke’s impressive Leeds side.

‌



Chelsea - who have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches - were loudly booed off by the home fans who have now seen home defeats to Tottenham and Leeds in the last month.

‌



A section of the Stamford Bridge crowd turned on Alonso, chanting ‘you don’t know what you’re doing’ during the Leeds onslaught in the second half.

And Alonso accepts that there are serious issues with his side, claiming there is a fragility which is impacting everything else.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"We are disappointed and sad. It was tough to deal with the defeat and we're in a fragile moment,” he told BBC Sport.

‌



"We have lost a bit of the confidence which we were playing with. It's a delicate moment but we have to go through it together and find solutions.

"The first half an hour was good but we conceded the equaliser and weren't too comfortable and lost some momentum. We could have done more in the second half but we didn't regain the confidence to have a real go and couldn't push hard enough to score one goal, which would have changed the momentum."

‌



View 2 Images Leeds ran riot at Stamford Bridge to beat Chelsea

Asked to pinpoint Chelsea’s biggest issue, Alonso added: "Everything is related. It's the confidence, this fragility at the moment, the demand of the game, the physicality - everything is related."

‌



It was a different story for Farke, who masterminded Leeds’ first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999 to move his charges just one point off the top four.

"We came here to win the game. We spoke the whole week about this and wanted to make this our game where we play on the front foot. We didn't want to allow Chelsea to control the mood,” Farke explained.

Article continues below

"We need to have good fitness levels and I have smart players who understand how we want to press and play. We have to be more concentrated to execute what we want to do. Desire is second to none, and we are competitive in the best league in the world."

Sports.title: Ismaila Sarr opens up on failed Liverpool transfer and reveals fresh talks
Sports.content:
Ismaila Sarr opens up on failed Liverpool transfer and reveals fresh talks

Liverpool saw a £50million bid for Ismaila Sarr rejected by Crystal Palace in the summer transfer window before the Reds eventually moved on to their top target, Bradley Barcola

View 2 Images Crystal Palace want to give Ismaila Sarr a new contract (Image: Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)

Ismaila Sarr has confirmed that he's in talks over a new contract with Crystal Palace after putting Liverpool's interest 'behind him'. Sarr, 28, was keen on a move to Anfield before Palace turned down Liverpool's £50million bid.

‌



‌



The Reds were looking for alternatives to Bradley Barcola before ultimately coughing up Paris Saint-Germain's £123m asking price. Despite the disappointment, the Senegal international maintains that he's happy at Palace and is open to extending his stay.

‌



Sarr told BBC Sport: "Liverpool is one of the biggest clubs in world football and, when a club like that shows an interest in you, of course it's something you take seriously.

‌



"I don't think any player would be indifferent to that kind of opportunity. It was an interesting possibility, and naturally, I considered what it could mean for my career.

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"Today, that chapter is behind me. I've always believed that you can't move forward if you're constantly looking in the rear-view mirror.

"I'm a Crystal Palace player, I'm proud of what we've achieved together, and my focus is on getting back on the pitch and helping the team."

‌



On his future at Selhurst Park, the ex-Watford star added: "Yes, there have been discussions with the club. For now, I prefer to let those conversations happen privately and concentrate on football."

Sarr will have a new manager when he returns from a groin injury, as Thomas Frank has replaced Pierre Sage. Frank's reign begins away to Coventry on Saturday, and Sarr is confident that the former Brentford and Tottenham boss can change Palace's fortunes.

‌



Should Liverpool go back in for Ismaila Sarr? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Ismaila Sarr is willing to commit his future to Crystal Palace (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

‌



"Of course, it's a difficult moment for everyone at the club," the winger acknowledged. "After everything we achieved last season, nobody expected us to be in this position.

"But I know the quality of this squad. We have very good players, a strong group and the ability to turn things around. The arrival of Thomas Frank is an opportunity for a fresh start, new energy and a different approach.

Article continues below

"We all have to take responsibility, work together and fight for every point. I'm confident we can overcome this difficult period and achieve our objectives this season."

Sports.title: Antonio Conte fires back after Man Utd snub with 'frightened of winning' jibe
Sports.content:
Antonio Conte fires back after Man Utd snub with 'frightened of winning' jibe

Antonio Conte was tipped to become Manchester United's new boss after the sacking of Michael Carrick, but the club had reservations about his demanding style of management

View 2 Images Antonio Conte staunchly defended his 'method' (Image: Cronache di spogliatoio)

Antonio Conte has suggested that Manchester United are 'frightened of winning' after he was snubbed for the manager's job in favour of Mauricio Pochettino. It's understood that Conte was put forward as a candidate by United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, but other prominent figures at the club weren't convinced.

‌



‌



The Italian has a reputation of being extremely demanding of his players, explosive in the media and he doesn't tend to last more than two seasons at a club. But Conte also boasts a trophy cabinet that the likes of Pochettino and other candidates such as Eddie Howe can only dream of.

‌



With one Premier League and three Serie A titles to his name along with six cups, the ex-Chelsea and Tottenham manager says that it'd be 'strange' if United decided not to hire him based on his 'method'. In an interview on an Italian podcast, Cronache di spogliatoio, Conte also revealed that he once spent a day with legendary former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson.

‌



"First, let me address the question of my method," the 57-year-old began. "If anyone is frightened by my method, then they are frightened of winning, because that methodology leads to victory. That is my answer.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"Manchester United has such a significant history that I find it strange to imagine anyone could be afraid of an approach aimed at restoring the club to its true stature."

Conte went on to say: "[United] last won the league in 2013, under Ferguson. I have immense respect for Sir Alex Ferguson. I've read his book, and when I was in London, I was fortunate enough to visit his home, and spend a day with him. [His Scottish accent was] a bit difficult to understand.

‌



Should Manchester United have appointed Antonio Conte? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Antonio Conte has won 11 trophies as a manager (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



"Through his own methodology and approach, he made Manchester United great. That is why I find certain remarks almost offensive towards United; it's as if someone were placing a veto on the club's return to its own history.

"A method is what's needed to achieve major results. And if you're suggesting that this method requires hard work, well, yes, it does. Everyone has to work hard, not just the players."

Article continues below

United instead opted for Pochettino, handing him a two-and-a-half-year contract. The Argentine has only won three trophies in his 17-year managerial career, all of which came at Paris Saint-Germain.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino wants to scrap Man Utd system from Michael Carrick reign
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino wants to scrap Man Utd system from Michael Carrick reign

Mauricio Pochettino takes on Liverpool in his first game as Manchester United boss

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino is preparing for his first game as Man United boss (Image: Getty)

Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to make a change to their social media output to prevent fan confusion.

‌



‌



During Michael Carrick's stint as boss this season, the Red Devils have announced their line-ups in numerical order rather than by position, leaving supporters scratching their heads over the formation.

‌



Speaking on MUTV, Pochettino urged the social media team to implement this change, saying: "Different way, no?" But whether United honour the manager's request for the Liverpool clash remains to be seen.

‌



Pochettino took over from Carrick during the international break, and will be eyeing a dream debut by snatching all three points at Anfield.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



But he has inherited something of a mess at Old Trafford, with the club registering just a single Premier League win all season. As a result, United find themselves mired in the relegation zone, with their campaign blighted by player unrest and widespread discontent among supporters.

Pochettino's appointment has injected a fresh burst of optimism into the club. A victory over Liverpool could dramatically shift the atmosphere around Old Trafford, though taking three points from Anfield is no mean feat.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick was sacked with Man United in the relegation zone (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

Speaking at his inaugural press conference on Friday, Pochettino said: "We are so excited to be here, and I think it's an amazing club. We are happy, but at the same time, so busy. I think it's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool.

‌



"We arrive with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy with the way we love to work. We have found supportive people in the club.

"But at the same time, we need to improve our players and find a way to perform. The identity and the culture of the club are very clear; it's a historic club with years as one of the best in the world."

When asked about his objectives, Pochettino responded: "My first target is to sleep! But I cannot sleep, only three or four hours a day. The target is to get to know the people, the staff, the players, and try to have an impact from the beginning, a positive one."

Sports.title: Arsenal's winning run ended by Newcastle in thrilling draw
Sports.content:
Arsenal's four-game winning Premier League run without conceding was ended by Newcastle in a frantic 2-2 draw.

For 45 minutes, this looked like another routine victory for Mikel Arteta's winning machine. Arsenal were dominant, controlling the tempo and suffocating Newcastle with their relentless pressure as Eberechi Eze's opener was exactly what the league leaders deserved.

But football showed yet again it's a game of two halves as Matthias Jaissle produced a tactical masterstroke to change the momentum of the game.

The Newcastle boss made a triple substitution that completely transformed the contest. Suddenly, Newcastle were bolder, braver and playing with intensity.

Harvey Barnes sparked the comeback before Malick Thiaw completed a spectacular turnaround on a night when Bruno Guimaraes returned to St James' Park as an Arsenal player but was withdrawn in the second half after a quiet performance. The first Newcastle captain to lift a trophy in 56 years following their historic 2025 Carabao Cup triumph, he was cheered at full-time when he completed a lap of the pitch.

Image: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes applauds the Newcastle fans after the whistle

Arsenal were rattled after falling behind. And their afternoon took another worrying turn when goalkeeper David Raya was forced off with a shoulder injury.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said: "Unfortunately, he had to come off which is never good news. He will get assessed now and probably he will have an MRI tomorrow [Sunday] to see what it is exactly because at the moment I don't know. It was a knock.

"I don't know how it happened and what the injury is at the moment, so we have to wait and see tomorrow."

But champions find a way to respond and Noni Madueke delivered the equaliser to ensure they escaped Tyneside with a point that extended their lead at the top of the table to six points over second-placed Brighton, who could halve the deficit at Hull on Sunday.

The key moments from St James' Park...

33: GOAL! Eze fires Arsenal ahead as their first-half superiority pays off after a mistake by Lewis Hall.

Eze fires Arsenal ahead as their first-half superiority pays off after a mistake by Lewis Hall. 46: SECOND HALF! Jaissle makes a triple substitution, bringing on Anthony Elanga, Jacob Ramsey and Tino Livramento transforming Newcastle's approach and attacking intent.

Jaissle makes a triple substitution, bringing on Anthony Elanga, Jacob Ramsey and Tino Livramento transforming Newcastle's approach and attacking intent. 49: GOAL! Barnes equalises after Martin Odegaard's error as the momentum swings dramatically.

Barnes equalises after Martin Odegaard's error as the momentum swings dramatically. 62: GOAL! Thiaw completes a stunning turnaround, firing Newcastle into a 2-1 lead.

Thiaw completes a stunning turnaround, firing Newcastle into a 2-1 lead. 67: INJURY! Arsenal suffer another setback as Raya departs with a worrying shoulder injury.

Arsenal suffer another setback as Raya departs with a worrying shoulder injury. 78: GOAL! Madueke rescues Arsenal with an equaliser to make it 2-2.

Arteta: We lost two points after 'exceptional' first half

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to Sky Sports:

"My feeling is that we lost two points today. We were exceptional in the first half. At every level. Our intensity, the clarity that we have, how to attack the jumps of Newcastle every time they wanted to go man-to-man, the composure that we have, the way we use our relationship to break their press. And it should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up, clear.

"But it wasn't. And when it wasn't, then we expected in the second half that we have to again raise the level because the opponent is going to have a reaction. And the opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. And then we gave them belief.

"And I say we give them belief because we give them a goal, we give them a throw-in that we just give them the ball. We have no structure to control the opposite winger. We concede a goal and it's game on.

"From that it became a very chaotic game. Every set-piece, we know that they are exceptional at it and we concede from a set-piece.

"Then you have to react. And then we went back to the exceptional team that we were in the first half again for another 25 minutes and we scored a great goal. We create infinity of openings to create and score the third goal, but we lack some time or to be precise, to make that count."

Jaissle: Our comeback gave me goosebumps

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle:

"A big, big point. When you feel the momentum in the second half, then you're almost feeling it's two points lost. But staying humble and seeing the big picture over 90 minutes, I think it's a fair result and something we can carry on and build on.

"We tried to encourage the players. Tactically, it was not too much of a difference. Honestly, it's just about believing in being front-footed, being aggressive, doing the last steps and believing also in your teammates. We need to use the momentum and that's what the lads did in the second half playing really vertical and using the gaps and the space and that was done with success.

"You see what's possible, especially at home with our fans - an unbelievable atmosphere, the energy was giving me goosebumps.

"This needs to be the standard. This unity, players and the fans and then the playing style. It's how we want to do that. The synergy should thrive us and give us confidence that we can do much better in the future."
