Sports.title: Erasmus runs risk of breaching World Rugby ban with watchalong
Sports.content:
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus went ahead with an online watchalong during Ireland's victory over his team in the Nations Championship on Saturday.

Erasmus is serving a six-match suspension handed down by World Rugby following extraordinary claims, questioning whether "match-fixing" and "manipulation" was occurring in rugby after his side's defeat to France in Paris last week.

The 54-year-old was suspended for "public criticism of match officials, undermining the integrity of individuals or the sport, and fuelling online abuse".

Erasmus organised a free watchalong for anyone to sign up and view him react to the Test match as he watched it unfold from his Dublin hotel.

After a brief welcome, Erasmus kept himself on mute during both halves of the match, where he could be seen clapping at times, gazing intently at a TV, apparently shouting into what presumably was a phone and thumping his table in frustration when Ireland won 20-17.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player South Africa head coach Erasmus' planned online watchalong could risk breaching the terms of his six-Test ban

But he did come off mute at half-time to outline what he thought would be under discussion in the break. He said: "We've not been playing perfect.

"If we step it up I think we'll be in this match. I think they've been really clinical but I'd have been much more worried if we'd played perfect and we're not currently playing perfect and we shouldn't just play to get one bonus point.

"I think will be the gist of what's happening at half-time."

Erasmus' ban covers the following:

"The suspension applies with immediate effect, applies to international matches, and includes any matchday involvement including coaching, direct or indirect contact with team management or players on matchdays; entering the stadium, coaches' box, playing enclosure, technical area, approaching and/or communicating with match officials on matchday; engaging in any 'feedback' process with match officials; and engaging in media duties during the suspension."

Regarding the "direct or indirect contact with team management or players on matchdays" element of his suspension, Sky Sports sought guidance on the potential for one of South Africa's coaching staff or management set-up signing up, listening to and watching the reactions and comments of their suspended head coach during the contest.

While this specific scenario is not covered by the guidelines, Sky Sports understands Erasmus' plan could be considered a breach by rugby's governing body.

There was, though, a short delay to the broadcast feed Erasmus was using.

South Africa Rugby released a statement requesting a full misconduct hearing in an immediate response to the sanction, but it is understood formal confirmation of an intention to appeal is yet to be received at World Rugby.

Image: Erasmus questioned whether TMOs and referees were 'match-fixing' or whether there was 'manipulation of the game or result'

Erasmus has now been suspended three times in five years for these sorts of incidents.

During the 2021 British and Irish Lions series in South Africa, after the Springboks lost the first Test, Erasmus broadcast an hour-long critique of Australian referee Nic Berry, and was eventually handed a two-month ban from all rugby activity and a 10-month matchday ban.

In 2022 he received a two-Test ban after sarcastic social media posts following back-to-back South Africa defeats to Ireland and France. A video critical of referee Wayne Barnes led to the official revealing he and his family had received death threats.

On Wednesday, SA Rugby released a statement "condemning the online abuse of officials" following confirmation of Erasmus' ban.

Sports.title: Frick enjoys winning start with Aberdeen with victory at Kilmarnock
Sports.content:
Mario Frick enjoyed a dream start to life as Aberdeen boss by edging a six-goal thriller with a 4-2 win over Kilmarnock.

Kevin Nisbet's double, coupled with Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall strikes, secured three priceless Scottish Premiership points to leave the Rugby Park side rooted to the bottom.

The visitors climbed to eighth spot after a remarkable afternoon where they hit a much-needed scoring streak.

The Dons opted to dispense with the services of boss Stephen Robinson after a run of only one win from seven which saw them sink to second-bottom and Frick was appointed as his replacement last Sunday.

It should have been advantage to the hosts in the seventh minute as Greg Kiltie picked out Joe Hugill and the striker went one-on-one with Marius Muller but could only rattle his shot into the body of the Dons 'keeper. They were made to pay moments later.

Image: Aberdeen's Kevin Nisbet scored twice at Kilmarnock

Another slick Aberdeen attack had skipper Nisbet taking full advantage of some familiar hesitancy in the Killie defence to sidefoot a shot into Nico Mantl's bottom left-hand corner and Frick's reign was off and running in emphatic style.

It would get better in the 10th minute as Ieuan Owen was booked for a cynical foul on Nicky Devlin and Nisbet stepped up to brilliantly curl his 20-yard free-kick low past Mantl via post for his 15th goal of the season.

As the Red Army celebrated an astonishing reversal of fortunes, Hicham Mahou rattled a shot in from distance which sailed inches wide of the target as Killie struggled to regroup from the double-whammy but the pulled one back in the 20th minute.

It was a much-needed response as Greg Kiltie reacted first to a loose ball to drive a low shot past Muller and at a stroke the contest was back in the balance.

Image: Neil McCann's Kilmarnock remain bottom of the table

That would shift again on the half-hour mark as the Dons made it three with Lyons running onto a Nesta Guinness-Walker cross from the left to bury a header past Mantl as the goal-fest continued.

Killie almost reduced the deficit moments after the restart as Michael Schjonning-Larsen's strike was superbly turned away by Muller as the Rugby Park side looked to launch a rescue act.

Manti then blocked a Nisbet shot with his legs as the Scotland international went in search of his hat-trick in the 52nd minute but Kilie were still in the fight and they threw themselves a lifeline five minutes later as Muller gifted possession to Tyreece John-Jules who gratefully accepted by clipping his finish high into the net.

Image: Aberdeen's Findlay Marshall (L) celebrates scoring to make it 4-2

Jamie Brandon squandered a terrific chance to square the game in the 73rd when he blazed a shot over the bar from 16 yards with the goal gaping and with that the Dons held on to see out a contest which allows Frisk to get off to a winning start as the last word went to Marshall who drilled in a fourth three minutes from time.

What the managers said...

Mario Frick predicted Kevin Nisbet would get his name on the scoresheet:

"I spoke to Kevin during the week and told him he would score and he scored twice, so he showed how dangerous he is inside the box. He could have scored three but I was very happy for him.

"I can enjoy it now but during the game it was difficult. We were lucky as well as Killie played very well, especially in the second half.

"We had some difficulties but in the end it was a deserved victory. We can defend better as we were lucky, We struggled in the first five or six minutes but after taking the lead we played well. But it was a bit chaotic and I was surprised.

"I told the players to play the way they did when they were young and they didn't think about mistakes or any negatives and played only to win for fun. I told them to play as they did as young players. Watching the third goal was beautiful, it's only the start and a beginning as we need to improve."

Killie boss Neil McCann admitted their winless run has to end, quickly:

"We are just conceding cheap goals and the boys are working so hard in training but when it comes into a game then that's when you really need to execute as that's when it matters most.

"When we managed to get ourselves back into the game at 2-1 I felt that we would go on and create more chances and then we conceded a third.

"In the second half we changed things around a bit as well as some personnel and adjusted how we were playing and I felt from the start of the second half onwards we were the better side.

"We were done on the counter-attack for the fourth goal and when you strip it all down I probably sound like a broken record. but the amount of chances we created and didn't take them....

"It's a sore one as we have worked so hard but it's in games where it matters most and every game is a chance to arrest that."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Ireland hold on for huge win over South Africa
Sports.content:
Ireland 20-17 South Africa: Springboks downed as Andy Farrell's side hold on for big victory in Nations Championship

Robert Baloucoune scored twice to help Ireland seal victory against South Africa

Robert Baloucoune's brace of tries saw Ireland seal a huge 20-17 victory against South Africa in the Nations Championship.

The bonus point for losing within seven points of Ireland tied the Springboks with New Zealand at the top of the southern hemisphere standings, but a huge points differential separated them.

The world champion Springboks will face England or France in the final next Saturday at Twickenham but will go in with consecutive defeats for the first time in four years.

After losing to Six Nations champion France 21-19 last weekend, South Africa was expected to overpower Ireland as they did with embarrassing ease a year ago in Dublin.

Ronan Kelleher scored just before half-time to give Ireland the lead at the break

But while the forwards set up both tries for South Africa, the backline attack was poor, as it was in Paris. The Springboks lost the aerial battle, struggled with Ireland's defensive line speed, and were flattered in the end to lose by only three points. The Boks led for only four minutes in the game.

They surged late into the match, with Malcolm Marx crossing on 58 minutes to set up a tense finish.

Despite a barrage of South Africa attacks, Ireland's defence was resolute, with Farrell's side moving above France to second in the northern hemisphere standings, with Les Bleus playing Argentina later on Saturday.

Farrell dubbed the victory "remarkable" and hailed his team for their performance against the world champions.

"These boys have done a lot of exceptional things over the years, but certainly in the last 12 months [this is the best]," the Ireland head coach said.

Ireland will likely play either Australia or New Zealand in the Nations Championship finals

"You always want to test yourself against the best. They are world champions, and not only that, they are the world No 1, and rightly so.

"This was always a challenge we were going to look forward to, and see if we could front up. These games matter.

"The game wasn't perfect, but it was never going to be. Most of the games at the top level aren't."

O'Driscoll: 'Outstanding' Ireland the better attacking team

Former Ireland captain Brian O'Driscoll said to ITV:

"We've been treated to a number of these big days in the last 10 years in Dublin, but this one is right up there.

"I said before the game, South Africa are completely the best team in the world, with the consistency they've shown.

"Ireland today were outstanding. You have to credit Ireland rather than saying where it went wrong for South Africa.

"Ireland looked the better attacking team, and they won the battle in the air.

Brian O'Driscoll believes Ireland outplayed South Africa on Saturday

"We've all been querying, where are we [Ireland]? This was the litmus test and you really discover where you're at.

"With all the hype this week, they did their talking on the pitch.

"The scoreline might even have flattered South Africa. Ireland showed most of the attacking threat."

Sports.title: Alonso: Chelsea are fragile and need to be tougher
Sports.content:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said his side are "fragile" and need to be "tougher" after being embarrassed by Leeds United.

Noah Okafor's double helped Leeds to a stunning 4-1 victory, their first at Stamford Bridge since 1999, increasing the pressure on Alonso, whose team have lost three of their last four Premier League matches and slipped to eighth.

Chelsea took the lead through Emmanuel Emegha after Moises Caicedo went off injured, but once Leeds deservedly equalised through Noah Okafor, the home side never looked likely to recover.

"We are in a fragile moment mentally," said Alonso. "When we receive a punch, we didn't recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling."

He added: "After the equaliser, after the change (Caicedo), we lost the momentum completely," said Alonso. "Until then, we were doing OK. We were creating, playing a lot on the pitch, we were coming out from the pressure, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing and it changed totally.

"And after that, we never got the good feeling mentality in any moment, and we were not able to cope with the pressure, and we didn't get close to the goal, so it completely changed it.

"We need to find solutions for sure because there will be setbacks during any game and to be tougher and to be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition."

Image: Noah Okafor of Leeds United celebrates scoring his team’s first goal with Gabriel Gudmundsson, Jayden Bogle and Dominic Calvert-Lewin

Calvert-Lewin said Chelsea "couldn't handle" Leeds' intensity with the visitors outrunning their opponents by 6km, putting in more high-speed runs and further sprinting distance.

"I try to find football solutions as well," said Alonso when asked how he will attempt to fix being bullied by teams.

"That's our job, to try to find solutions, to work on that, to create that, to have bad experiences like today and hopefully we will have good ones when we can overcome, even during the game, a difficult moment because this is football and for sure that will happen.

"But in the progression, in the process that I often talk about, this is a very, very important topic."

Chelsea won more duels but Leeds' press won them possession nine times in the final third to the hosts' one.

"There were moments that we were not competing at the level required and we need to know that that's mandatory in this competition because you will face teams with that demand again," added Alonso.

"The physicality, the duels, that is not the only explanation. I said that yesterday and I repeat that. We could do that better in a football way, not giving a ball away, trying to progress a little bit more, choosing better options. That's the solution as well but the physical part and the mentality part we can do better."

Chelsea have lost at home to both rivals Leeds and Tottenham for the first time in 67 years, upsetting supporters, who booed their team off at Stamford Bridge.

Alonso said: "I understand the disappointment for sure and we share that with them and whatever we can do is work, try to give our best to turn it back and to do much better."

Sports.title: Raya injured but Madueke rescues point for Arsenal in seesaw Newcastle draw
Sports.content:
If Mikel Arteta was delighted to see the back of Eddie Howe as Newcastle’s head coach, the bad news is that another similarly awkward technical area adversary has been installed at St James’ Park.

Arsenal’s manager never seemed to relish trips to face Howe’s old team and he certainly did not enjoy this latest trip to Tyneside, where Matthias Jaissle’s initially overwhelmed team fought back commendably to earn a point courtesy of a stellar second-half performance. At half-time the crowd had felt close to turning against Jaissle but he held his nerve and, thanks to a triple substitution and subtle tactical rejig suggested he is no mug after all.

It left Arsenal – who lost their outstanding goalkeeper David Raya to a potentially significant second-half shoulder injury – still top of the Premier League, six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City, and Arteta with a face like thunder.

View image in fullscreen David Raya is helped off the pitch with a shoulder injury. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA

Just last week Bruno Guimarães claimed he was “beloved” by Newcastle fans but the club’s former captain turned Arsenal midfielder found himself serenaded by a soundtrack of boos of the sort usually reserved for Sunderland players. Newcastle’s problem is that, despite spending about £275m this summer, they have struggled to replace last season’s departed star trio – Guimarães, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.

That reality perhaps left Howe’s successor – who arrived just before the start of the season – making a not so subtle point with his team sheet here. Of Jaissle’s starting XI only the goalkeeper, Lukas Hornicek, the right-back Amar Dedic and the midfielder Sean Steur were close-season signings.

The other five new faces were either benched (Nico González and Matias Fernandez-Pardo) or did not make the 20-man matchday squad (Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Touré). Admittedly Ewen Jaouen is injured but, given Bamba and Toure cost a combined £78.5m, their omission represented quite a statement. Ditto the decision to bench González and Fernandez-Pardo and their individual £50m plus price tag.

Meanwhile the jury remains out on Hornicek. The Czech international has made some excellent saves this season but, initially here, his kicking proved pretty much uniformly poor and he was fortunate to be reprieved after hesitating too long as the impressive Kai Havertz closed in.

Quick Guide Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: key facts Show • Arsenal ended a 21-game run of Premier League games without a draw (W18 D3) since a 2-2 draw with Wolves back in February. • Since the start of last season, all five of Newcastle’s Premier League draws at St James’ Park have been a 2-2 scoreline. • Eberechi Eze’s opener for Arsenal (pictured) was his first Premier League goal since April, which also put the Gunners 1-0 ahead against Newcastle. Opta Photograph: Lee Smith/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Jaissle’s frustration with his goalkeeper proved well apparent as Arsenal took increasing control of a first half that saw Newcastle’s lone striker, William Osula, isolated and even their normally imperious England left-back Lewis Hall given a thorough work out by Noni Madueke.

Much to Arteta’s chagrin, Lewis Miley, preferred to González in the midfield holding role, endeavoured to slow the tempo but the red tide could only be stemmed for so long.

When Havertz dispossessed Hall after the latter miscontrolled a long ball, he cut inside and slid a highly intelligent, beautifully calibrated, pass across to the on-rushing Eberechi Eze. Without breaking stride, Eze exhibited perfect balance and unleashed a gorgeous first-time shot that arrowed, inexorably, past Hornicek.

As the home fans fell eerily silent, Arteta and his staff celebrated a goal sufficiently special to rebuke suggestions that his side are all about efficiency at the expense of artistry these days.

With Declan Rice always available to reinforce his defence and smother any flickering home attack it proved a struggle to recall Newcastle making a meaningful attacking touch inside Arsenal’s box. Fans stationed near the home dugouts told Jaissle what they thought of it all.

Arsenal’s pressing was initially so good that Newcastle were left almost incapable of playing short passes and, instead found themselves reduced to aimless long balls. With Rice and Martin Ødegaard apparently operating on a different midfield planet an equaliser felt like a distant dream.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Yet that seemingly ambitious vision was something Harvey Barnes proved fully capable of buying into. When, early in the second half, Ødegaard made an uncharacteristic error, his heavy touch sliced the ball in Osula’s direction and the Dane played it into Barnes’s path.

All that remained was for the left winger to take a single, steadying, touch before an assured finish left the hitherto redundant David Raya picking his shot out of the net.

Jaissle’s second-half introduction of Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey and Anthony Elanga – all at Newcastle last season – at the expense of Dedic, Steur and Jacob Murphy was paying dividends. Suddenly, almost astonishingly, Arsenal were the team in danger of being pressed into submission.

The home side were closing their guests down far higher up the pitch and had morphed into an infinitely more menacing team. Soon, they were ahead in the wake of a Hall corner headed down by Dan Burn, allowing Malick Thiaw to stab the ball beyond Raya.

View image in fullscreen Malick Thiaw roars his approval after giving Newcastle a second-half lead. Photograph: Harvey Murphy/Danehouse/Getty Images

Shortly afterwards Arsenal’s goalkeeper was helped off the pitch in evident pain after sustaining a nasty left shoulder injury during an ostensibly benign collision with Osula. On came Kepa Arrizabalaga in a triple substitution also featuring Guimarães’s exit.

Madueke though was still around and he reminded everyone of his presence by meeting the counterattacking Ødegaard’s stellar pass, dummying two defenders and watching his slightly deflected shot evade Hornicek’s grasp.

No matter; Jaissle had done enough to win plenty of hearts and minds. Not least the chair, Yasir al-Rumayyan, over from Riyadh to watch his first match of the season and reportedly “take the club’s temperature”.

Sports.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.

It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.

Farke’s side were tactically superior against flimsy opposition. For Chelsea, who were jeered off after their fifth defeat in 11 games, the indignities piled high. Records are falling, but not in a good way. This is the first time in 67 years they have lost grudge matches at home to Leeds and Tottenham in the same season, leaving Alonso on shaky ground with supporters, and there was further alarm when Cole Palmer appeared to clash with Willie Isa after the side’s “cultural architect” urged Chelsea’s No 10 to acknowledge the crowd at full-time.

Palmer cut a disgruntled figure throughout and did nothing to make Thomas Tuchel rethink his decision to leave him out of the England squad. The one mitigating factor is that few players will thrive in a directionless team. What does Alonso want Chelsea to be? No one knows. There are no patterns of play and the main takeaway from this surrender is that the only sign of an identity was an addiction to calamitous defending.

Calvert-Lewin followed the lead of Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey by tormenting Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana. Alonso was appointed in the summer but the pressure is mounting already. The Spaniard’s control even let him down when a ball dropped towards the technical area in the second half.

View image in fullscreen Emmanuel Emegha (right) celebrates scoring Chelsea’s goal with teammates. Photograph: Toby Melville/Reuters

It was some turnaround from the visitors, who trailed when Emmanuel Emegha marked his full debut by scoring his first goal since joining Chelsea from Strasbourg last summer. Farke continues to excel. The best that can be said of Alonso is that he needs time. Losing Moisés Caicedo early on was a blow. Even then it is impossible to understand Alonso’s intended style of play. There is an emptiness to Chelsea. They faced 21 shots and failed to up the physicality after crumbling against Sunderland.

Admittedly Alonso is dealing with João Pedro’s absence in attack. He has toyed with a false nine in recent weeks, but used a target man this time and the early signs were promising. Emegha gave Chelsea a focal point and finished well when an error from James Justin allowed Rogers to send the striker through on goal.

Leeds were on top when they conceded. Chelsea had lost Caicedo, who made way for Jordan Henderson after injuring his back in a collision with Justin, and were already wobbling. Calvert-Lewin spurned three excellent headed chances and Leeds levelled after 28 minutes.

View image in fullscreen Noah Okafor holds off the Chelsea defence to score a 28th-minute leveller. Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty Images

Chelsea had no defensive leaders. Fofana is too easily ruffled in the air and was involved in the equaliser. He sent a routine header back into dangerous territory and Chelsea panicked. Josh Acheampong mistimed his jump as the ball bounced around and Calvert-Lewin was able to find Okafor, who cut inside and slipped a low shot past Emiliano Martínez.

Farke was rightly disappointed that Leeds were not ahead at half-time. Tarik Muharemovic charged forward from defence, away from Palmer’s feeble challenge, and crossed for Calvert-Lewin to flick wide. Ethan Ampadu ran midfield, outshining Henderson and Romeo Lavia, and the Leeds wing-backs were wonderful. Ao Tanaka went close and Muharemovic grimaced after having a goal disallowed for offside.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Alonso looked bewildered. Colwill, low on confidence since returning from a knee injury, kept misplacing simple passes and Estêvão Willian was ineffective on the right. Chelsea were jeered off and made a dreadful start to the second half. Martínez should have conceded a penalty for a challenge on Calvert-Lewin. Michael Oliver then pointed to the spot when Rogers was adjudged to have handled Jayden Bogle’s shot.

Quick Guide Chelsea 1-4 Leeds: key facts Show • Leeds have won their first game against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in all competitions since December 1999, ending a run of 10 away games against the Blues without victory (D2 L8), while they’ve scored 4+ goals away at Chelsea for the first time since January 1970 (5-2). • Leeds have won their first Premier League game in London since May 2022 (2-1 against Brentford), ending a run of 15 matches in the Capital without victory (D4 L11), while it’s their biggest winning margin in London since April 2003 (6-1 against Charlton). • Leeds’ Ao Tanaka (pictured with Cole Palmer) committed three fouls inside the first six minutes against Chelsea; no player has ever fouled more often inside six minutes in a Premier League game on record (since 2003-04). Opta Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

It looked harsh given Rogers’ arm was close to his body and the ball hit him close to the shoulder but the decision was upheld after a VAR check. Calvert-Lewin stepped up to score and the result was never in doubt once Leeds led. Chelsea, who were mentally fragile, crumbled. Leeds were rampant. Chelsea could not cope with Ampadu’s long throws. One was half cleared but Sean Longstaff worked the ball back to Ampadu, who crossed for Okafor to make it 3-1.

“We are in a fragile moment mentally,” Alonso said. “When we receive a punch we didn’t recover. The fans were disappointed because the expectations are high. I understand their disappointment. There were moments that we were not competing at the level required.”

The closing stages were miserable for Chelsea, who have already conceded 20 goals. Leeds cruised and completed the humiliation when Aaronson, a late substitute, turned past Malo Gusto before sliding a shot through Martínez’s grasp.

The home sections had already emptied out. Those who stayed soon made their displeasure clear.

Sports.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
Sports.content:
For Aston Villa, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago.

Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely.

“I am trying to select the players I think that are ready to play and the selection is thinking for the best of the team,” said Emery, who was again reluctant to blame the empty North Stand as a factor behind their disappointing home form, a sharp contrast to their 11-game winning run here last season. “In my experiences here and in Spain, when they [stadiums] are in works like we are in now, it’s a small sacrifice, but it’s not an excuse,” Villa’s manager added. “We have to play with this situation and next year it will be better.”

Villa’s frustration was underlined by a moment on the verge of half-time, when Emery gave Sunderland’s kit man, Luke Purcell, a gentle shove on the sidelines in an attempt to speed up a Villa restart. “We have increased our demands a lot, our level, but still there are favourites in front of us, to reach the top six, top four,” Emery said. “We are now again in a new construction with some new players who are sharing their qualities and we are trying to mix different players, young players to build our structure as fast as possible.”

View image in fullscreen Chemsdine Talbi of Sunderland shoots under pressure from Boubacar Kamara of Aston Villa. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images

With 90 minutes and 25 seconds showing on the big screens, Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched victory for Sunderland, the Moroccan winger shaving the upright of Zion Suzuki’s goal with a spell-bending strike. Talbi did almost everything right, bursting past Aaron Wan-Bissaka, comfortably eliminating the defender, before using Boubacar Kamara as a mannequin to get his bearings, but his curling right-foot shot was ultimately a few inches too close to the post. For Villa, a first clean sheet in the league here since March, but this draw extended their winless run to five matches in all competitions.

For Sunderland, this may not have been the dopamine hit of beating Chelsea, but it was was another gutsy showing, and without two key players in Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey, both of whom were absent through injury. It was a big team performance, another feather in the cap of Jules Ahoka, the 20-year-old midfielder who shone on his first Premier League start. Ahoka started last season playing on sandy pitches in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s second division. “He is getting better game after game,” Le Bris said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sunderland were happy to soak up the Villa pressure. Emery introduced the 17-year-old Brian Madjo, who trained with England under-21s during the international break, but in place of Nicolas Jackson rather than to join him in attack. By which point Mbaye had entered and combined with McGinn to fashion another nearly moment. Disbelief reigned in the stands, but had Talbi located the top corner, things could have felt a lot worse at the final whistle.

Sports.title: Evanilson and Kluivert sink Forest to earn Bournemouth ninth win in a row
Sports.content:
Marco Rose saluted the in-form Evanilson after the Brazilian scored for a sixth Premier League game in a row to lift Bournemouth up to fourth place with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

Evanilson’s brilliantly taken 19th-minute opener set his side on course for a club record ninth straight win in all competitions, while the defeat means Forest are only above the relegation places on goal difference having failed to build on the momentum of their 3-1 win against Manchester City before the international break.

Rose said: “We defend together as a team, and we attack together as a team, but the forward guys were excellent today. They did a great job scoring the goals and the other guys support them. Evanilson creates space, carries the ball, provides assists and now he scores goals as a No 9, really beautiful goals so I am happy.”

Both teams started the game on the front foot and Forest had the first sight of goal. Neco Williams nodded dangerously across the face of goal at the far post, but Liam Delap was beaten to the ball by home defender Antonio Silva.

Evanilson was denied by a brilliant last-ditch tackle from Forest centre-back Jair Cunha before Marcus Tavernier’s 20-yard curler was well saved by Matz Sels.

Bournemouth took the lead in the 19th minute. James Hill cushioned a header into the path of Evanilson, and the Brazilian took one touch before blasting a left-foot shot into the roof of the net.

View image in fullscreen Evanilson fires Bournemouth into the lead. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Justin Kluivert almost doubled the home side’s lead with an effort from 20 yards which sailed narrowly over the crossbar. Evanilson then failed to keep his shot down after a long throw from Hill caused chaos in the Forest penalty area.

Oliver Glasner’s side had a penalty appeal waved away when Adam Smith blocked Williams’s effort into the arm of teammate Tyler Adams. But Kluivert did make it 2-0 on the stroke of half-time with a simple far-post finish after a superb run and cross from Tavernier.

Forest were much improved in the second half, adopting a more direct approach in a bid to find a way back into the game. Delap turned provider by whipping in a cross for Morgan Gibbs-White but the captain could not properly connect with his header.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Quick Guide Bournemouth 2-0 Nottingham Forest: key facts Show • Bournemouth have won five successive games in the top-flight of English football for the first time. Only Arsenal (67, before Newcastle game) and Manchester City (60) have collected more Premier League points in 2026 than the Cherries (52 – W13 D13 L4). • Bournemouth have won each of their last nine games in all competitions, their longest ever such run, overtaking two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13. • Nottingham Forest failed to score in this game despite registering 2.14 expected goals, the highest xG tally by any team not to score in a Premier League match this season. Opta Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

James McAtee ballooned an effort over the bar as the visitors continued to misfire in front of goal. The substitute Chris Wood also miscued a header from a corner when he should have at least tested the underworked Bournemouth goalkeeper, Djordje Petrovic.

Bournemouth always looked a threat on the counter and Kluivert came close to his second and Bournemouth’s third when he stung the gloves of Sels from 18 yards out. Kluivert should also have been more clinical when he found himself within finishing range but unselfishly laid the ball off to Rayan and the chance went begging.

Glasner, whose side had 19 shots but only one on target, said: “Of course when you lose it’s always a tough 90 minutes, especially when you make too many mistakes like we did in the first half.

“The second goal straight before half-time was a little bit of a killer but credit to the lads in the second half for finding a filter back into the game. We had some good situations, but we couldn’t convert them.

“We are not able to score in this game, and this is what we have to look at and where we have to improve. We took too many touches, and were not so aggressive.”

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership roundup: Celtic sweep St Mirren aside to strengthen grip at top
Sports.content:
The recalled midfielders Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan both scored as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1. The champions brushed off the loss of midfield pair Mika Baur and Benjamin Nygren to injury to consolidate their place at the top of the Premiership.

The centre-forward Camilo Duran was also on target as Celtic killed the game late in the first half with three goals in nine minutes. Callum McGregor grabbed his first league goal of the season before Killian Phillips scored a consolation from the spot.

With Baur facing up to 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Nygren nursing a heel problem, Martin O’Neill would have been delighted with how his midfield functioned.

Oxlade-Chamberlain made his fifth start of the season and McCowan his second. The pair had never started a game together before. O’Neill also introduced the former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joël van den Berg for a debut in the second half and the 19-year-old showed some good touches.

Celtic started with a new-look front three of Duran flanked by Jota and Yang Hyun-jun. Duran was a constant threat and had two goals disallowed for offside in the opening quarter.

Yang was instrumental in the 33rd-minute opener, racing past Declan John and drilling a low pass which ultimately fell for Oxlade-Chamberlain to stroke into the bottom corner.

The South Korean soon passed up a brilliant chance, opting to look for Duran when played clean through by the goalkeeper Sam Johnstone. The pass was under-hit and Alex Gogic cleared.

Duran was on the end of a far better ball in the 40th minute, cushioning home a volley after a superb whipped cross by Kieran Tierney. Duran soon set up Jota, who was denied by Jacob Chapman, before finding Tierney, who provided another assist as McCowan drilled a first-time finish.

Celtic went four ahead in the 63rd minute when the ball broke for McGregor on the edge of the box. The captain quickly shifted the ball on to his right foot and swept it into the bottom corner.

Johnstone blew his chance of a clean sheet when he crashed into Calvin Ramsay as he came off his line to punch the ball. Phillips converted the resulting 70th-minute penalty and St Mirren kept pushing with Johnstone saving well from Ismeal Kabia and Samuel Ramos coming close.

View image in fullscreen Callum McGregor scores Celtic’s fourth against St Mirren. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

Hearts returned to winning ways in spectacular style as they destroyed 10-man Dundee 8-0. They went into the game on the back of a run of three straight defeats but they ran riot, scoring four in the first half thanks to Sabah Kerjota, a Pierre Landry Kaboré double and an own goal by Ryan Finnigan.

Dundee were reduced to 10 men after the break with Owen Bevan shown a straight red card before Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Kerjota with his second and Stuart Findlay blew Dundee away with four more goals.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Mario Frick enjoyed a dream start to life as Aberdeen manager by edging a six-goal thriller with a 4-2 win at Kilmarnock. Kevin Nisbet’s double along with Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall strikes secured three priceless points to leave the Rugby Park side rooted to the bottom

The visitors climbed to eighth spot after a remarkable afternoon where the Pittodrie side hit a much-needed scoring streak. Aberdeen opted to dispense with the services of Stephen Robinson after a run of one win from seven which saw them sink to second bottom and Frick was appointed as his replacement last Sunday.

Dundee United recorded their biggest ever win at Easter Road with an impressive 4-0 thrashing of Hibernian. Zac Sapsford’s first-half double laid the foundations before Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall found the net after the break.

The visitors were well worth the three points as they cemented their place in the top six and picked up their first win in Leith since 2021. It was a humbling afternoon for Hibs, who thought they had turned a corner under their new head coach, Marink Reedijk, after back-to-back victories before the international break.

Falkirk clung on to clock up six top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1966 with a 2-1 home victory against St Johnstone. John McGlynn’s team scored early in each half to remain third.

Jacob Murrell’s eighth goal of a superb debut season sent Falkirk on their way inside six minutes. Finley Barbrook’s second goal in as many games on 48 minutes doubled the advantage. Josh Campbell nodded in a late reply to serve up a scare but the hosts held firm.

Sports.title: WSL roundup: Chelsea thwarted by Liverpool keeper, London City move to third
Sports.content:
Khiara Keating’s resilient performance in goal denied Chelsea, the Women’s Super League leaders, and earned Liverpool a point, while London City Lionesses moved to within four points of the top by beating Crystal Palace 6-2.

After hard-fought 1-0 wins against Manchester City last Saturday and Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday night, Chelsea drew a blank. Against Gareth Taylor’s side, Chelsea’s lack of cutting edge was clear a week after beating City to go top. The calf injury picked up by Melvine Malard against City, the absence of Lauren James, who has a thigh injury, and the form of Aggie Beever-Jones, who scored her first WSL goal in more than a year in the 6-0 defeat of Charlton, have left Chelsea’s attack short.

Despite almost 70% possession and 47 touches in the box to Liverpool’s 12, Sonia Bompastor’s side amassed only 19 shots to Liverpool’s 13 and seven on target to their opponents’ four. Although the Blues remain unbeaten in the WSL, their third draw in five games in all competitions means City can leapfrog them at the top if they beat Tottenham on Sunday.

Liverpool had chances, particularly in the first half, but were hanging on after the break and Keating helped them to a fourth clean sheet, a tally bettered only by Bompastor’s side.

“It was a bit stressful; we don’t want to sit back but in games like this you have ‌to ride it out,” Keating told Sky Sports. “A clean sheet is ​always on our minds every game. We knew the mission. It was such a close game, it could have gone either way.”

The January transfer window will give the Blues an opportunity to strengthen their attack, but with three games before the winter break they need to step up in the final third, starting with their tricky fixture against London City Lionesses on 12 December after the international break.

London City came out on top in a thrilling end-to-end encounter with Palace. Having earned five of their nine points from losing positions this season, Palace did not cower when Eder Maestre’s team took the lead in Bromley. They twice came from behind to level the score before London City put the game beyond them.

The hosts had to weather some early Palace pressure, with Lexi Lloyd-Smith testing Elena Lete in the opening minute, with the goalkeeper starting in place of Mary Earps.

London City then took control and were rewarded for their dominance in the 14th minute, when Daniëlle van de Donk turned in Isobel Goodwin’s cutback from close range. Palace were carved open, but they were not down and out against the team with ambitions of earning a place in next season’s Champions League.

View image in fullscreen Daniëlle van de Donk who scored twice for London City Lionesses, celebrates with teammates. Photograph: Isabel Falle/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Jo Potter’s side drew level via an Abbie Larkin volley into the bottom corner to stun the home team, with the visiting fans in full voice telling Alexia Putellas what she could do with her Ballons d’Or.

It felt fated that the three-time winner of the trophy would have the last laugh and within six minutes of the restart she restored her team’s lead, the ball falling kindly for her to turn into an empty net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

London City’s third came three minutes later and the scenario was similar. Shae Yañez failed to deal with a cross and Van de Donk swept it goalwards. Mollie Bartrip was there to hook it away but the referee deemed it to have crossed the line.

The home team’s lead was cut to one in style by Palace when Fuka Tsunoda’s reverse pass was met by Annabel Blanchard and her side-footed volley looped over Lete and in. It was a stunning move and a stunning finish.

London City’s squad depth and fresh legs eventually helped them stretch the game beyond the stubborn visiting team, with Alanna Kennedy heading them back into a two-goal lead 15 minutes after coming on.

They killed the game off four minutes later, this time with Goodwin rising highest to head in from another set piece, and Putellas put the cherry on top with her second at the death, looping the loose ball in after a big save from Yañez.

There were positives for Palace, despite remaining a precarious three points clear of Birmingham City, who play Manchester United tomorrow but big-spending London City are just a cut above.

Sports.title: Pochettino needs New Manager Bounce to break torrid Manchester United turnover | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table. Or a promising start becomes a troubling dip, becomes a full-on battle against relegation.

Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager.

With hindsight, Michael Carrick’s dismissal was probably inevitable from the moment Manchester United lost at Hull on the opening weekend, just as Ruben Amorim was doomed from the moment cameras picked him up fiddling with magnetic counters on a tactics board in the rain at Grimsby. The message for Mauricio Pochettino is clear: don’t go playing badly on the east coast.

It’s generally acknowledged that Carrick, while he may not have been the ideal manager for United, was a long way down the list of the biggest problems at the club. So what was the point of sacking him? As Pochettino begins his United career at Anfield on Sunday, what realistically can any manager hope to achieve?

Sackings have become almost ritualistic. Football demands blood sacrifice. How else can the harvest be guaranteed but by the torching of the wicker man? How else can Crystal Palace stay up but by the sacking of Pierre Sage? Once, when the manager defined the club, bought the players, decided the tactics, set the mood, that perhaps made sense. When managers were messiahs, it requires only a slight tweak to the underlying theology to see a logic in sacrificing them.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino – a far more ebullient and charismatic figure than Michael Carrick – enjoyed Champions League success at Tottenham. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

But managers now, at least at the majority of Premier League clubs, are part of a wider structure. In one of his meltdowns at Spurs, Antonio Conte made the point that it made little sense for him to be answering questions about the broader future of the club when he had so little power compared with the tiers of executives. Why sack the manager rather than the head of recruitment or the sporting director or the chair?

The answer to that perhaps goes back to the emergence of the English idea of the manager, which began in the 1930s and blossomed in the post-war golden age of Matt Busby, Bill Shankly, Don Revie and Brian Clough. As Barney Ronay argues in The Manager, at least part of the reason he became a figure of such pre-eminence was that it was useful for the board to have a hapless ashen-faced figure standing out on the touchline to take the blame. A handful of geniuses aside, the manager was essentially a convenient scapegoat.

But does the sacrifice work? It was one of the shibboleths of football’s early data wonks that the new manager bounce was a myth. What was being witnessed when form improved after a sacking was nothing more than regression to the mean. Which sounds sensible: squads make games and are determined by finance. There is a wealth of evidence that the biggest single factor in determining league position is the wage bill.

And yet there is also evidence that new manager bounce does exist. A lot of early data analysis in football ignored the fact that those involved are human and respond emotionally to circumstance. More recent studies, though, suggest that, while around a quarter of clubs experience no improvement, the first five matches under a new manager show a 41% improvement in points per game, although the impact wears off after around 10 games.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That feels intuitively true and is readily explicable. A manager under pressure can become embattled, lashing out at enemies real and imagined, their capacity to make lucid decisions impaired as confidence ebbs, creating a doom spiral. Replacing him breaks that pattern and permits a psychological reset.

In a world where everything is studied endlessly, a new manager should make a team less predictable. It’s possible, of course, that as those early analyses suggested, performances would have turned anyway as part of a regression to the mean, but it is curious how often the uptick in form coincides with the replacement of the manager.

Anthropologists are yet to determine precisely why United sacrifice managers so frequently, although there does appear to be some sense of deflecting blame. There is also a sense that it has become routine, that reasons that once probably did exist have been forgotten over time.

Sacking the manager is just what the club do a few months into the season, the ritual now as divorced from its original purpose as modern Hallowe’en customs are from their origins in the Christian commemoration of All Hallows’ Eve.

Will the arrival of Pochettino help? He is a far more ebullient and charismatic figure than Carrick, whose status as a dead man walking for most of this season perhaps meant players did not take him as seriously as they might have an incumbent who appeared to be there for the long term, or had them beginning to ponder moves away from United.

But this remains a mismatched hotchpotch of a squad assembled over six previous managers. If there is some style of play that would suit most of them it has yet to reveal itself.

It will take time for Pochettino to instil in a side that are habitually outrun the levels of conditioning that characterised his Tottenham, and perhaps even longer to get them playing in a coherent pattern. There will probably have to be five or six new signings (and at least as many departures). Probably most difficult of all, there is the entire culture of the club to overhaul, which may not be possible without a change of ownership.

Given United came back from two goals behind three times in their final two games under Carrick, these are not usual circumstances: beleaguered managers rarely inspire such defiance, and the fans never turned against him. In that sense, there will not be the immediate benefit that comes when toxicity is removed.

Some sort of bounce, though, is probable under Pochettino, if only because a negative pattern has been broken. The question is how long it can be maintained.

Sports.title: European football: Doué carried off for PSG while Kane vows to return fresh
Sports.content:
Lazio continued to underline their Serie A title credentials with a comfortable 3-0 ⁠home win against Lecce as Gennaro Gattuso’s side remained unbeaten this season and extended their lead ⁠at the top ⁠of the ​standings.

Tijjani Noslin scored in each half and Davide Frattesi wrapped up the win in style with a 90th-minute ⁠strike as Lazio earned their 10th victory in 12 games to move to 32 points, four ahead of Inter ⁠who travel to Atlanta on Sunday. Como are fourth on 26 points after ​a 2-0 win against Cagliari ‌thanks to goals from ‌Jacobo Ramón and Lucas Da Cunha.

The majority of Lazio fans continue to ‌boycott home matches in protest against the club owner Claudio Lotito, yet the unrest has done little to unsettle Gattuso’s players. “I look at it the other way around,” Frattesi told Dazn when asked about being top of the league. “We’re on 32 points, with eight still to go [for 40 ‌points which usually guarantees survival].”

In Germany, Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha fired his side to the top of ⁠the Bundesliga table as they won 1-0 at bottom side Borussia Mönchengladbach. After Bayern Munich ⁠were held to ⁠a ​1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, Dortmund capitalised to take a two-point lead at the summit.

The home side played far better ⁠than their position would suggest, ​withstanding waves of pressure ‌from the visitors, ‌but Gladbach finally cracked in the 80th minute when Nmecha picked ‌up the ball on the edge of a packed penalty area and let fly. Unsighted by the thicket of bodies in front of him, the goalkeeper Daniel Batz misjudged the trajectory of the ball, and it flew over his right shoulder ‌and into the net.

Gladbach created a number of chances, but Gregor Kobel came to the rescue ​with several fine saves for Dortmund, and once the goal went in, there was no way back for the hosts. Dortmund have 24 points after 10 games, two ahead of Bayern and third-placed Freiburg, who ⁠beat Elversberg 1-0.

Fourth-placed RB Leipzig had five different players ​on the scoresheet ​in a 5-1 drubbing ​of Union Berlin that lifted them to 21 points. ​Bayer Leverkusen ‌thumped four goals ​without reply ​past Paderborn to remain fifth. Eintracht Frankfurt remained in the running for the European places thanks to a 1-0 win against Hoffenheim, with Jonathan Burkardt’s first-half goal securing the victory.

View image in fullscreen Felix Nmecha fires home Borussia Dortmund’s winner against Borussia Mönchengladbach. Photograph: Christopher Neundorf/EPA

Meanwhile, Fifpro said on Saturday it was “deeply concerned” by public comments from Bayern’s leadership about Jamal Musiala’s contract, accusing the German ⁠champions of putting pressure on the midfielder while he recovers from health problems. The global players’ union was responding to recent remarks by senior Bayern officials, including ⁠honorary president Uli Hoeness, ⁠chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen ​and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, about Musiala’s future at the club.

Hoeness earlier this month questioned whether the 23-year-old Germany international could return to his ⁠previous level after being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. Dreesen later backed those remarks, saying Bayern would evaluate Musiala’s progress and discuss his future with his representatives. Rummenigge subsequently defended ⁠the comments, saying the club’s consideration of Musiala’s health and contract situation was both responsible and normal.

“Bayern’s honorary ​president, chief executive and former chief executive ‌have all publicly questioned Musiala’s contract ‌in quick succession,” Fifpro said in a statement. “In FIFPRO’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put ‌pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.”

Musiala signed a contract extension with Bayern until 2030 in February last year. He has endured a difficult run of injuries and health setbacks in recent months. He broke his leg at the Club World Cup in July 2025, missed half of last season and collapsed twice within a ‌few days in August before being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. In September, he suffered a hamstring injury.

“Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty ​about a player’s future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury,” Fifpro added. “Making Musiala’s health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.”

Dreesen ​rejected suggestions that Bayern were trying ​to pressure Musiala. “We all hope that ​Jamal will be the Jamal we know again,” Dreesen said on Saturday. “He needs time ​to come back. We’ve ‌said that several times ​now. He has to ​be given that time. And then we’ll see how things look at the beginning of next year.”

Dreesen added that there was no need to keep talking about Musiala’s contract. After September’s injury, Musiala returned as a substitute in Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday in which Harry Kane sustained an injury that may mean months of rehabilitation.

On Saturday, Kane said he was looking to come back improved for “the business end of the season”. Kane tore a ligament in his left ankle and Bayern said the Ballon d’Or winner had undergone “successful surgery overnight” having earlier said that Kane would be out for “the next few months”.

Kane posted a photo on Instagram of himself smiling broadly, while sitting on a hospital bed after the surgery, with his leg encased in a medical boot. “The highs and lows of life!” the 33-year-old wrote. “Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.”

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino dealt blow with key Man United player to miss Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford is not fit enough to play for Manchester United this weekend against Liverpool, talkSPORT understands.

The winger has not played since October 13 due to a hip injury and is not expected to return to action at Anfield on Sunday.

2 Rashford will not feature for United against Liverpool due to injury in a blow to Pochettino ahead of his first match Credit: Getty

This comes as a blow to new United head coach Mauricio Pochettino as their injury list remains packed.

Manuel Ugarte, Benjamin Sesko, Luke Shaw and Carlos Baleba are all set to be sidelined for the match as well.

Rashford first sustained his injury during the 2026 World Cup with England and struggled to shake it off since.

His last appearance came in the 2-0 Champions League defeat away at Atletico Madrid.

The 29-year-old was then benched for the 1-1 Premier League draw with Leeds United.

Rashford struggles at United continue

With his latest setback, Rashford continues to endure a difficult first season back at United following his loan spell in Barcelona.

He hit 14 goals and 15 assists in a campaign that saw him return to his best form and win LaLiga at Camp Nou.

Barcelona had the option to buy him permanently for £26million, but they did not activate it and instead brought in Anthony Gordon.

This is despite Rashford revealing that he wanted to stay at the club given his success on loan.

United welcomed him back for the 2026/27 campaign and now wears the no. 9 shirt, having previously donned 39, 19 and 10.

2 Pochettino faces a gruelling start to life on the United touchline with a trip to their historic rivals Credit: Getty

However, he is yet to score or assist in any eight matches across all competitions this season.

Rashford has started six of those fixtures, four of which have come in the Premier League.

A January move to Everton has been speculated as he continues to refind his feet.

It would see him follow a similar path to Jack Grealish, who has done well for the Toffees after a dip at Manchester City.

Rashford has also missed the last two England camps despite being part of their World Cup squad.

He is on 78 caps and 19 goals with the Three Lions since making his debut in May 2016.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta worried about David Raya as update on Arsenal star’s injury given
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta worried about David Raya as update on Arsenal star’s injury given

Mikel Arteta confirmed David Raya will undergo an MRI after he sustained an arm injury in Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Newcastle.

Raya exited the contest midway through the second half after what appeared to be an innocuous collision with Magpies striker Will Osula.

3 Raya's teammates were quick to console him following his arm injury Credit: Getty

The Spaniard briefly fell to the turf and then quickly got back to his feet, only to clutch his arm in serious pain.

It quickly became clear Raya could not continue and he made his way off with his left arm placed in a makeshift sling.

Raya was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Mikel Arteta gives update on David Raya injury

Arteta now faces a nervy wait as to whether Raya will be fit to feature for the Gunners against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Speaking to media following the contest, the Arsenal boss admitted he was unsure how serious Raya's injury was.

"We don't know, unfortunately," Arteta said.

"Obviously we had to come off. We are worried, but we don't know.

"Tomorrow, he will have an MRI."

How Arsenal's draw with Newcastle unfolded

It was far from a vintage performance for the Gunners, who took the lead courtesy of Eberechi Eze.

Eze was slipped in behind Newcastle's defensive line and coolly slotted home with a first-time effort from close range.

3 Arteta's side will finish the weekend with a minimum three-point buffer to second-placed Brighton Credit: Getty

But a rare mistake from Martin Odegaard allowed the hosts back into the contest.

The Norwegian mis-kicked a throw-in from the left and sent the ball straight to Osula, who drove towards goal from the right before he laid it to Harvey Barnes.

Barnes, who was in plenty of space, gratefully slid the ball home past a diving Raya.

Newcastle then took the lead in bizarre fashion courtesy of Malick Thiaw.

3 Thiaw thought he'd scored the winner, but it was not to be Credit: Getty

A Dan Burn header towards goal landed into Joe Willock, who was being closely marked by Gabriel on the goal-line.

Thiaw was first to the loose ball and lashed it into the net, sparking wild scenes from the Toon faithful.

A VAR check for offside followed, but Thiaw's goal remained.

However, the hosts could not hang on for just their fourth league win of the season as Noni Madueke rescued a point for the Gunners in the 78th minute.

The winger capped off a blistering counter-attack when he cut in from the right flank onto his left foot and unleashed a strike that squirmed under Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

Sports.title: Premier League player suffers freak injury coming out of the tunnel
Sports.content:
Premier League player suffers freak injury coming out of the tunnel

Coventry City were dealt a blow when Taiwo Awoniyi picked up a bizarre injury just before the second half.

The striker was on the score sheet for the Sky Blues in their impressive 3-2 win over Crystal Palace on Saturday.



2 Awoniyi got the Sky Blues on their way to a huge three points Credit: Getty

And Awoniyi may have scored more, only to hurt himself when he re-emerged for the final 45 minutes.

As he ran out of the tunnel, Awoniyi fell to the turf and clutched his leg, with two Palace players helping him off the ground.

The strange incident prompted Coventry boss Frank Lampard into an unplanned substitution as Sidiki Cherif was brought on in place of Awoniyi.



Frank Lampard gives update on Taiwo Awoniyi's injury

Lampard then confirmed following the match Awoniyi had felt his ankle in the first half, with the club to now fully assess the extent of the damage in the coming days.

"He hurt his ankle," Lampard said.

"I don't know what the diagnosis is of that yet.

"He felt he could go and give it a try. Quite clearly, straight away he felt he couldn't."



How Coventry's win over Palace unfolded

Awoniyi got Coventry off to a dream start when he slotted home from close range in the fifth minute.

Sky Blues ace Jack Rudoni drove into the box on the left side and squared it to Awoniyi, who directed his effort past a diving Dean Henderson.



It was Awoniyi's second league goal this term for Coventry following his summer switch from Nottingham Forest.

2 Lampard has Coventry slowly creeping up the table after a difficult start Credit: Getty

Palace's Yeremy Pino equalised just eight minutes later, only for Tatsuhiro Sakamoto to restore the hosts' advantage on the half-hour mark.

But the two sides went into the break at 2-2 courtesy of Jorgen Strand Larsen, who lashed home from close range.



Yet there was one final twist to come in the 89th minute.

A long Coventry throw eventually found Brandon Thomas-Asante, who powered a header straight at Dean Henderson.

However, his save rebounded into a retreating Dwight McNeil and into the back of the net, sparking wild scenes among Sky Blues supporters.

The result marked Coventry's fourth league win this season and moved them up to 13th with 12 points.

As for Palace, who had Thomas Frank at the helm for the first time following his appointment, they remain rooted to the bottom of the ladder following their eighth defeat from 11 league games.

Sports.title: ‘Rotten’ – Shell-shocked Jason Cundy gives Xabi Alonso Chelsea sack warning as fans turn on manager
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy was a despondent man on the talkSPORT airwaves after watching his beloved Chelsea get thumped by Leeds United.

Leeds were 4-1 winners on Saturday in what was their first victory at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League since December 1999.

3 Leeds ended their 27-year wait to win at Stamford Bridge with a deserved victory against a dreadful Chelsea Credit: Getty

Noah Okafor scored two for the visitors, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson also netting against a woeful Chelsea side.

Cundy was at the Bridge and rushed to talkSPORT towers at the full-time whistle to join a gleeful Jamie O'Hara on the GameDay Phone-In.

'Disgusting' Chelsea leave Cundy worried

"We are rotten," he explained. "We were so bad, it was so bad... I'm in disbelief at what I've just witnessed."

The former Blues defender also expressed his concerns for manager Xabi Alonso amid a run of one win in five across all competitions.

A handful of fans were also heard chanting 'You don't know what you're doing!' to the Spaniard once Malo Gusto came on in the second half.

"That was a worrying performance, worrying. If that carries on, Alonso won't keep his job, I'm telling you that for nothing," Cundy added.

"You can't do what you did against Sunderland (1-0 loss), you can't do what you did against Leeds today and lose those two games."

"We were disgusting today, absolutely disgusting," Cundy continued. "I'm still trying to find the words... as every minute ticked by, we got worse, and Leeds got better."

Chelsea have dropped to eighth in the Premier League after losing for the fifth time this season, and Cundy thinks the next few months look bleak.

"It's almost disbelief at how bad we were, seriously, I'm not even joking. I'm worried... I'm worried about how this season is going to go," he said.

3 Cundy looked a broken man on the GameDay Phone-In and raised his concerns over how Chelsea will fare this season Credit: talkSPORT

3 He also warned Alonso that he could face the sack if their dismal run of form continues across the next few weeks Credit: Getty

"Genuinely now, I'm worried... I am worried about what this season looks like for us.

"I'm being completely honest here, I don't know whether we're going to finish... we look like bottom half fodder, easily bottom half fodder."

Later in the show, Cundy stated that Chelsea would have lost against Championship opposition with a similar performance.

"I actually think Lincoln could've beaten us today… anyone could've beaten us, we were that bad," Cundy said.

"I'm really struggling to work out how we could've been that bad."

Leeds also poked fun at Cundy on social media by giving him a taste of his own medicine with his famous 'Has anyone seen?' joke.

Alonso: Chelsea in a 'fragile moment'

Speaking to talkSPORT afterwards, Alonso detailed how Chelsea, who saw Moises Caicedo go off injured in the first half, struggle to bounce back from adversity.

"It was a tough one, a tough game, tough result to deal with," Alonso said. "My feeling is that we are in a fragile moment, when we get a setback, we are not able to recover quick enough to this competitive level required against a team as Leeds.

"The first half an hour we were good, we conceded the 1-1, and after that, the substitution, we lost total momentum. Leeds started believing more than us and we were not able to turn it our way."

Alonso added: "Leeds have their qualities and they do good. There are more reasons than just the physicality of the duels.

"I think that we could have done better, even that we lost a little bit of confidence to do the right things, how to keep the ball, how to be able to go through this first pressure of Leeds.

"The first half an hour we were able to play much more on the half, but the rest of the game we didn't progress that well."

Sports.title: ‘Where’s the fight?’ – Ian Holloway restrained by stewards as Swindon fans fume before slamming his players
Sports.content:
‘Where’s the fight?’ – Ian Holloway restrained by stewards as Swindon fans fume before slamming his players

Swindon Town boss Ian Holloway was 'bitterly disappointed' in his players following a 2-0 loss to Newport County.

Newport midfielder Aaron Lewis' first-half double condemned the Robins to a tenth loss in their last 15 fixtures.



2 Holloway did not hold back in his assessment following Swindon's latest defeat Credit: Getty

And Swindon supporters were not afraid to vent their frustrations at Holloway, with a clip of the frosty exchange shared on social media.

Ian Holloway clashes with Swindon fans

As Holloway approached the fans, he removed his cap and began walking towards the tunnel, but stopped in his tracks to bite back at one supporter.

The Robins boss then had to be led away by security.

An 'absolutely fuming' Holloway later ripped into his own troops in his post-match interview.



What did Ian Holloway say in his post-match interview?

"They've (Newport) improved, they put you under pressure and get balls in your box," Holloway said.

"Two of the softest goals I've ever seen in my life, absolutely killed us.



"And it's been coming. It looked like they didn't care. The rest of it was a waste of time. We ended up creating chances, but anyone can do that when you're 2-0 down.

"Bitterly disappointed in all of them and disappointed for the fans. I get it, that didn't look like our team.



"It's not very nice in there."

Holloway continued: "You need to win your header, and you need to win the knockdown, get your foot through it.

2 Holloway has been in charge at Swindon since October 2024 Credit: Rex

"They scored two ugly goals. All our chances that we had, normally we take them.

"Where's the fight? It's a local derby. I'm sorry, they've done their bits better than us."



It is not the first time Holloway has strongly criticised his own players, having described some as 'imposters' during pre-season.

When is Swindon next in action?

The loss to Newport leaves Swindon in 17th on 19 points, six clear of the relegation zone in League Two.

However, the Robins remain only four points away from the play-off positions in the fourth tier.

Swindon will look to avoid a third consecutive defeat in the league next Saturday when they host promotion hopefuls Chesterfield.

Sports.title: ‘Superstar’ – Luca Williams-Barnett likened to George Best as he emulates Gareth Bale feat
Sports.content:
‘Superstar’ – Luca Williams-Barnett likened to George Best as he emulates Gareth Bale feat

Alan Pardew branded Tottenham prodigy Luca Williams-Barnett a 'superstar' after he enjoyed a first senior competitive start to remember.

The 18-year-old scored the opener and assisted Dominic Solanke's strike as Spurs eased to a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday, with Hollywood royalty Ryan Reynolds and Sir Kenneth Branagh watching on.

2 Williams-Barnett put his name up in lights for Spurs against Ipswich Credit: Getty

Williams-Barnett's goal came after some intelligent movement at the back post to poke home Pedro Porro's cross from the right.

His assist was perhaps a little more special, as the teen whiz picked up the ball in his own half and dribbled all the way down the left and into Ipswich's box before he squared the ball across goal for Solanke to tap home.

The Spurs striker immediately pointed and ran towards Williams-Barnett to thank him for the assist.

Williams-Barnett was then brought off to a standing ovation in the 64th minute.

Alan Pardew: Luca Williams-Barnett is like George Best

And Pardew, who was on commentary for talkSPORT at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, believed the north London outfit have a real gem on their hands.

"We're seeing the arrival of a superstar," Pardew said.

"He made it look so easy."

Pardew added: "He's got lovely, fluid moves and style to him as a player... like George Best. He's got that agility to him.

"It was his show today. Spurs were okay today... but it was all about the young boy. He's had a perfect afternoon."

Pardew then said: "Spurs now have a Luca Williams-Barnett to counter Arsenal's Max Dowman.

2 Pardew has tipped a remarkably bright future for Tottenham whiz Williams-Barnett Credit: Getty

"When George Best used to move when he'd drop a shoulder without losing pace, it reminded me of that."

Luca Williams-Barnett nearly equals Gareth Bale feat

Pardew's bold prediction may not be so far-fetched given Williams-Barnett's goal put him in esteemed company.

Aged 18 years and 51 days, Williams-Barnett's strike against Ipswich made him the club's youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale, who was aged 18 years and 47 days when he netted against Fulham in September 2007.

It was an impressive performance from Spurs, who have now won three on the bounce at home.

The hosts also did it with manager Roberto De Zerbi sitting in the stands as he served a one-match touchline ban having accumulated three yellow cards this season.

As for Ipswich, the loss to Spurs extended their winless streak to a fifth match.

The Tractor Boys have also now failed to keep a clean sheet in their last 30 Premier League fixtures.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo caught waiting for Al Nassr match to end to make quick exit down tunnel
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo caught waiting for Al Nassr match to end to make quick exit down tunnel

Cristiano Ronaldo endured an awkward moment as he tried to rush down the tunnel at the end of Al Nassr's defeat.

The football icon went from hero to zero on Friday night, as he opened the scoring before missing a penalty in his side's 3-1 defeat to Al Ahli.



4 Cristiano Ronaldo missed a penalty as Al Nassr slumped to defeat Credit: Getty

Ronaldo put Al Nassr in front after just 14 minutes when he finished clinically, and then had the chance to double their lead minutes later.

The Saudi champions were awarded a penalty on 17 minutes, which Ronaldo stepped up to take, only for his effort to hit the post and bounce out to keep the score at 1-0.

His miss proved costly, as Al Ahli then turned the game on its head with Galeno grabbing the equaliser on the stroke of half time.



England striker Ivan Toney then put the visitors in front with a trademark penalty, before Roger Ibanez hit the winner minutes later.

Ronaldo's blunder

With Al Nassr heading towards just their second defeat of the season, Ronaldo was visibly frustrated in the final moments.



So much so in fact, that footage has captured the Portugal icon attempting to make a quick exit down the tunnel moments before the referee ended the match.

Ronaldo jogged off the pitch, only to realise the final whistle had not yet blown and was forced to step back on for the closing seconds.



Cameras then show the 41-year-old immediately rushing straight back off again as soon as the game officially came to an end.

Ronaldo's actions were quickly up on by fans online, with many left unimpressed by his behaviour as team captain.

One commented: "Look at Ronaldo closely, he doesn't care about this team."

4 Ronaldo headed for the changing rooms before the full-time whistle had blown Credit: X: @Rtiban1



4 The Al Nassr forward was then forced to cross back over the white line after realising the whistle hadn't blown Credit: X: @Rtiban1

Another said: "This is a captain?"

A third added: "He only wants 1,000 goals and doesn't care about the team."

Defeat for Al Nassr saw them slip to third place in the Saudi Pro League, two points behind leaders Al Hilal.

Meanwhile Al Ahli moved to just a place behind them in fourth, with four points less on the board.



While it was disappointment for Ronaldo on the night, he at least closed in on his ultimate target of hitting 1,000 career goals.

By scoring the opener, the Portuguese is now just 14 goals off the unprecedented milestone, sitting at an incredible 986 strikes in 1,340 professional games.

4 Ronaldo took his season's tally to ten goals in 13 games by scoring in Al Nassr's defeat Credit: Getty
