Ronaldo had also made a goalscoring return for Al Nassr after the international break, having had a rare break after announcing his retirement from Portugal duty a week earlier.



The Manchester United and Real Madrid great called time on his illustrious international career, which ended with a record 146 goals in 234 caps for his country.

Without him, Portugal were thrashed 4-1 by Denmark in the Nations Leagueon Saturday - their heaviest home loss in a competitive game.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s two transfer priorities revealed as £36.5m man faces January exit
Sports.content:
Fabrizio Romano has claimed Manchester United will prioritise a new centre-back and striker in the January transfer window.

And to make space for a new presence up top, the Red Devils may look to shift Joshua Zirkzee.



2 Zirkzee has just 11 goals in 85 appearances for United Credit: Getty

The Dutch star has struggled to fit in at Old Trafford following his £36.5million move in July 2024 but may enjoy a new lease of life under new United boss Mauricio Pochettino, who was appointed during the international break.

However, Zirkzee has only weeks to convince Pochettino of his qualities before the January window opens.

What has been said about Joshua Zirkzee's future?

"Zirkzee is now waiting to work under Mauricio Pochettino," Romano told DAZN.



"Maybe the story could change in the next few weeks, but Zirkzee already in the summer was close to leaving Man United with interest from Fiorentina, Juventus and Everton in the final hours of the summer window. The Toffees tried to sign Joshua Zirkzee, was not possible.

"Zirkzee wants to play on a regular basis. So, let's see what happens with Pochettino.



"But, if he's not going to play in the next weeks, well, an exit of Joshua Zirkzee in the January window could be a serious possibility."

Another name mentioned with a potential move from Old Trafford was fellow striker Benjamin Sesko.



The Slovenian remains sidelined with a shin injury and does not have a return date.

Will Benjamin Sesko stay at Manchester United in January?

Despite his fitness woes and links to Juventus, Romano does not believe Sesko will be pushed out the door.

"I'm told that Sesko is not going to leave Manchester United in the January transfer window, very clear position," Romano said.

2 Sesko looks set to be out of action for the rest of 2026 with his shin injury Credit: Getty



"Sesko wants to stay, wants to continue. He hopes to be ready in January to be back on the pitch, help United. But he's not planning to leave.

"So, Sesko to Juventus, despite the rumours and the links, is something that is not going to happen in the January transfer window."

United's decision to prioritise a centre-back and striker comes after a midfield spending spree in the summer.

The Red Devils brought in Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos for a combined £148million.



However, the trio's presence has failed to ignite many positive results for the club.

United went into the international break sitting in the bottom three, even though they rescued a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa by scoring twice in second-half stoppage time.

The club's poor results prompted Michael Carrick's axing after just ten league games of the season, with Pochettino drafted in as his replacement.

Pochettino will hope to start his Red Devils tenure with a win on Sunday when his side travels to Anfield for a bumper clash against bitter rivals Liverpool.

Sports.title: Newcastle vs Arsenal - Premier League: Toon halt Gunners charge in thrilling draw
Sports.content: Arsenal's dynasty drive behind their raft of new contracts: Why stars are desperate to play for Mikel Arteta, the ultimatum he gives each of them and the dilemma over whether to extend Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz

Sports.title: Arsenal's complacency and a lack of ambition allowed Newcastle a way back and the Gunners were fortunate to escape with a point after paying the price for not killing the game, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
Arsenal's complacency and a lack of ambition allowed Newcastle a way back and the Gunners were fortunate to escape with a point after paying the price for not killing the game, writes CRAIG HOPE

Do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned. Do not prod the bear. Do not start Bruno Guimaraes. The champions belligerently ignored all of that and put the grizzly to sleep in a typically smothering first half. The only problem? They forgot to kill it.

And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle – including three changes – Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute. By now, the two teams were unrecognisable from those who had played out a one-sided opening period, after which Arsenal led 1-0. Mikel Arteta would not have settled for a draw then.

Come the end, though, he was mightily relieved not to be beaten. For that, he had Noni Madueke to thank. The winger had been his best player throughout and, had he shown the same incision that produced his 78th-minute equaliser, Arsenal would have won. They would have won by half-time, in fact.

So dominant were they, maybe it was complacency. Or maybe there is a lesson here in showing more ambition when in front. Arteta, you feel, gets a kick from suffocating opponents. But during a pulsating second half in which St James’ Park throbbed to the beat of their brilliant team, the hosts grabbed the pillowcase.

Former Newcastle captain Guimaraes was hooked in the 70th minute after an ineffectual night, and Arsenal were better for their own changes.

The league leaders can absorb this result, of course. Of greater concern for Arteta is an injury to David Raya. The goalkeeper left the pitch at the same time as Guimaraes, not because of performance, but clutching his wrist, the upshot of a robust challenge from William Osula. That home forcefulness typified their second half, if not their first.

Noni Madueke saved Arsenal's blushes with an equaliser against Newcastle in a tough second half on Saturday

The Magpies were poor in the first period but a half-time team talk and changes from Matthias Jaissle worked wonders

Bruno Guimaraes earned a hostile reception as he returned to face the side he once captained

There is now concern for the Gunners, with goalkeeper David Raya going off injured

If Newcastle were to beat the champions, so suggested the crumbs of pre-match optimism, they would have to start fast. At least, that was the blueprint of old on red-hot nights such as this. Newcastle started slow. Arsenal weren’t much quicker, but they didn’t have to be. They moved through the gears as a flat first half unfolded and, with it, they began to move through Newcastle.

Arteta likes this sort of game, when it feels like minimum expenditure for maximum return. In short, it was easy. A training-ground drill. Attack versus defence. Come half-time, Newcastle had not touched the ball in Arsenal’s penalty area. They simply weren’t allowed to. Saying that, even with permission they would have found a way to pass it straight out of play or shank a cross into the Leazes End. Newcastle’s first half really was that short on inspiration. There wasn’t too much perspiration, either. And so the home fans booed on the whistle, for a fifth half on the spin at St James’.

MATCH FACTS Newcastle (4-3-3): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5 (Livramento 46, 7), Thiaw 7, Burn 7, Hall 6 (Botman 90); Miley 7, Steur 6 (Ramsey 46, 7); Murphy 5 (Elanga 46, 6), Willock 7 (Wissa 83), Barnes 7; Osula 6 Subs not used: Pope, Schar, Gonzalez, Fernandez-Pardo Booked: Burn, Dedic, Barnes Goals: Barnes 49, Thiaw 62 Manager: Matthias Jaissle Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Raya 5 (Arrizabalaga 70, 5); Timber 6, Konsa 6, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 6; Guimaraes 5 (Lewis-Skelly 70, 7), Rice 6; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7 (Merino 90), Eze 6 (Tzolis 70, 6); Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 90) Subs not used: White, Hincapie, Mosquera, Saliba Booked: Rice, Madueke Goals: Eze 33, Madueke 78 Manager: Mikel Arteta Referee: C Kavanagh 6

Arsenal led by one, and for them that should have been a source of regret. The goal came when Lewis Hall, despite screams from team-mate Dan Burn to ‘head it, head it’, decided to control, clumsily, on his chest, allowing Kai Havertz to steal. He freed Eberechi Eze and the first-time finish was routine. The punishment of Hall’s error, however, was ruthless.

Six days after bettering Lamine Yamal, England left back Hall was struggling to contain Madueke. In fact, he and each of his comrades could not get close to any of those in red. Martin Odegaard was picking his passes, probing delightfully as he does. Declan Rice, meanwhile, might as well have worn slippers. He was protecting a back four not in need of protection.

So, what happened at half-time, to both sides, was a mystery. It was as if they’d swapped shirts. From nowhere, Newcastle attacked. That may sound basic, but this was seismic. The exclusion zone that had been Arsenal’s penalty box was no longer off limits. Indeed, nothing was off limits for a home team who were suddenly able to run, tackle and, yes, shoot. From passive to aggressive in the space of 15 minutes during the interval, it was no surprise when they drew level in the 49th.

Joe Willock hurried Odegaard into a mistake, William Osula pounced on the loose ball and, when Harvey Barnes was set free, he was not going to miss. Barnes can be a spectator at times but his eye for a finish is indisputable. The turnaround was complete when defender Malick Thiaw forced over the goal-line from a corner which Arsenal had failed to defend – Dan Burn’s free header told you that someone, somewhere was not doing their job.

There were chances for a third and Newcastle looked the most likely winners. Then, Madueke burst inside two home jerseys and fired through Lukas Hornicek from 18 yards. If only he, or any of his team-mates, had been so purposeful at 0-1 then this would not have been a rescue act.

But amid the belated, home hostility, Arsenal knew that they were fortunate to survive.

Sports.title: The next Lamine Yamal? Why not! Roberto De Zerbi sets high bar for Luca Williams-Barnett after 18-year-old thrilled Tottenham fans in win over Ipswich, writes MATT BARLOW
Sports.content:
Luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' said De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'

Asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

You make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

There has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

Spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

MATCH FACTS Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5). Scorers: Williams-Barnett, Solanke. Booked: Maddison, Williams-Barnett, Kudus, Fernandes. Manager: Roberto De Zerbi 7. Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6. Booked: Diop. Manager: Gary O’Neil 6. Referee: Rob Jones 6.

Belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

Williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' said Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'

Spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

They were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

Savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.

Sports.title: Formidable and relentless Bournemouth's astonishing form is no mere hot streak, writes JAMES SHARPE, as dominant Cherries beat Forest to claim NINTH win in a row
Sports.content:
This is all becoming rather inevitable at Bournemouth. Will they ever stop winning? Will Evanilson ever stop scoring?

The numbers alone are astonishing. Nine wins on the bounce for the first time in their history, their victory here against Nottingham Forest making it six on the spin at home at an aggregate score of 15 to nil. Five wins in a row in the Premier League for the first time, too, a result that moved them into the top four.

This is Bournemouth, remember. Only this is Bournemouth now.

Make no mistake: this is no hot streak. This is not a team under Marco Rose carried to win after win after win on a wave of momentum and vibes. This is relentless, breathtaking stuff. This is a team that, week after week, outplays every team that stands in front of them. It doesn’t matter if it’s Forest, or Manchester United, or AC Milan. Bournemouth turn up and they blow their opponents away.

They move it quicker and sharper, they win it back faster and higher. They give teams no time to think or breathe, so it’s little wonder they have no answer.

‘We never really struggled, said Rose. 'We suffered a little bit at the end, but we defended quite well together, and that's why it's a deserved win.

Bournemouth racked up their sixth successive league victory and ninth in all competitions

'If we use the right approach every game – and this is really, really demanding – we win games. Next game, we have to prove it again. If we do it, then we can keep the level up. But as I said, this is a tough job.

‘The collective is strong, but even this we have to maintain. Because if you win games…I mean, some of our players right now are in a lot of noise and rumours.

'If we are able to keep these kinds of things away from the locker room, and if everyone comes into training every day, works hard and gives everything for the club and the team, then we are really, really good.'

EVANILSON ON FIRE...AGAIN!

The only real surprise was that Evanilson, Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian, didn’t leave with more than just his one, now customary, goal.

That itself was another fine finish after Tyler Adams won the ball high up the pitch – obviously – dinked it across to James Hill, back after his first England call-up, who flicked a header into Evanilson’s path. He thumped it past Matz Sels to do the rest.

Rose, who called him a ‘real No9’ the other week, had been urging him to get into the box more to finish off chances. He did that, all right. Twice earlier in the game, he raced on to through balls only to be denied by Sels and a last-ditch tackle from Jair Cunha.

His opening strike, his eighth goal in his last nine games, means he is the first Premier League player to reach double figures for goal contributions with six goals alongside his four other assists. He leads the press, he creates chances, he scores goals. He does the lot.

That’s now six league games in a row he’s found the net, halfway to breaking Jamie Vardy’s record of 11 in a row. You wouldn’t put it past him.

Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian Evanilson scored for the sixth successive league match

AFTER LORD MAYOR’S SHOW FOR FOREST AND DELAP

Forest came into this, after all, off the back of a huge, much-needed victory against Manchester City. After just one win in Oliver Glasner’s opening nine league games, that was the performance those around Forest felt that could spark the season into life.

It was also meant to be the one where Liam Delap’s Forest career burst into life with two thunderous goals in a bullying, battering-ram showing.

Alas, they both ran into a proper team this week.

Forest tried to go direct to Delap, partly to try to bypass the intense Bournemouth press, but nothing stuck. Delap lost possession with 23 of his 39 touches. He committed more fouls than he had shots and found his way into the referee’s book for clumsily bundling over Adam Smith.

The visitors huffed and puffed in the second half but never really looked like scoring. The closest they got was a couple of speculative long-range efforts from Morgan Gibbs-White and James McAtee before a late goalmouth scramble nearly provided an opening through chaos more than creativity.

It was only the busy hands of Sels that kept the scoring respectable.

’The defeat was deserved,’ said Glasner. ‘City and today were completely different. It's like a different sport. This is football, but it's different.

'When teams play like City, when it's more of a tactical game, we are doing well. When it's more of a physical, intense game, we're struggling. Today our weaknesses came to the surface.’

When asked if he had the players to play this way, Glasner responded: 'Right now, I have to say no. If not, we will add players. If we believe we need somebody to add this physicality, these quick solutions, we will do it.'

Did they expect much else, though? Forest never beat Bournemouth. That’s 13 meetings in a row now they have failed to win.

‘Nottingham Forest, it’s happened again,’ sang the home fans in the final few minutes.

Liam Delap and Nottingham Forest crashed into a proper team as they came back down to earth after their win over Man City before the international break

Marcus Tavernier's performances could get a chance with England if he maintains his form

TAVERNIER FOR ENGLAND?

Bournemouth have already had a couple of deserved England call-ups this season in Hill and midfielder Alex Scott. How long until Marcus Tavernier gets his chance?

No English player has scored more Premier League goals this season than the Bournemouth winger, level with Morgan Rogers and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and once again he was at the heart of everything good the Cherries do.

His superb cross behind the Forest defence found Justin Kluivert for Bournemouth’s second of the afternoon. He danced through the Forest defence to set up Rayan for a late chance.

'It was my 11th Premier League game today, and I couldn't see better offensive midfielders so far this season,’ said Rose.

‘If you see how he works and how he plays, the quality he has, he scores goals. He's 27, he's at the best age.

‘If he plays well, if he stays healthy, I think, like with Hilly, these things come. They're just around the corner.'

Sports.title: Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace ends in late defeat by Coventry as risk of relegation increases
Sports.content:
Thomas Frank changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace but it did little to alter the fortunes of the Premier League’s bottom club.

There were noticeable improvements on Frank’s bow. Palace were more structured in attack, with cleverly orchestrated moves and a clear, coherent plan for creating chances.

But the same problem persisted: they cannot defend. That diagnosis is simple to make. However, addressing it is complicated by inadequate personnel.

Palace replaced Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix with teenage defender Honest Ahanor and Chelsea castoff Axel Disasi in the summer.

Until they can address the oversight in their squad planning - thinking that would be enough to replace two international centre-backs - they will continue shipping sloppy goals.

Frank will address the structural problems, ensure players understand the positions they should occupy in specific situations and get Palace defending as a cohesive unit.

These are all things within his control and he began fixing them to some extent on Saturday.

Despite having a new manager in the dugout, the same old problems remained for Crystal Palace

His in-game management worked somewhat as Palace went from defending frantically in the first half to looking much more solid and organised, before conceding in the 85th minute.

What he won’t be able to eradicate, though, are the individual errors that have consistently cost Palace this season.

Ultimately, those mistakes come down to the quality of the defenders at his disposal.

Palace will look to address their personnel issues in January but they currently sit rock bottom of the league, with a massive game against Hull next weekend.

Unless they can cut out the errors that have contributed to their 27 league goals conceded this season, they risk being cut adrift before they can bring in reinforcements.

New boss Frank was more glass-half-full, though. ‘There is more positive than negative from the game,’ Frank said.

‘We looked like a threat. We scored two very good goals and we created quite a few more chances to score at least one more goal.

‘That was the big positive. I was extremely happy with the effort and the mentality of the players.’

Defensively, their 3-2 defeat against Coventry was a horror show. Three players were dragged out wide - including Axel Disasi, who was miles out of position - allowing Jack Rudoni to find Taiwo Awoniyi in the penalty area to poke past Dean Henderson four minutes into Frank’s bow.

Coventry should have had a second, too, after Palace overcommitted in attack and Awoniyi was played in behind. One-on-one with Dean Henderson, he took the ball around the goalkeeper, only for Axel Disasi to somehow get back and clear it off the line.

Palace had been on the front foot but were caught out by how quickly they had to transition from attack to defence, unable to get enough bodies back in time. They are struggling to find a balance between defence and attack.

Anan Khalaili failed to win his tackle for Coventry’s second, giving Rudoni space to run down the right. Nobody shut Rudoni down and he found Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, who rocketed a thunderous half-volley into the top corner from outside the area.

Coventry’s 85th-minute winner came from a long throw, which Palace failed to deal with.

Changing habits

Frank abandoned the back three, which had served Palace well for the last two years and nine months, and pivoted to a 4-2-3-1.

Offensively, Palace improved. The formation suited Yeremy Pino and Jorgen Strand Larsen particularly well, with the pair combining for both of Palace’s goals.

It should also bring the best out of Quinten Timber, Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton, as individuals are rarely isolated in midfield, unlike under Pierre Sage.

On the other hand, Tyrick Mitchell and Khalaili still tried to function as wing-backs rather than full-backs.

That is ingrained in their habits, and it will take time to coach it out of them. However, it remains a significant issue.

Both players committed themselves forward when attacking, leaving an already fragile centre-back pairing exposed and allowing Coventry to transition quickly and exploit Palace's vulnerability.

That cannot happen in a back four, as there were situations where Palace had eight players forward with only the goalkeeper and two centre-backs staying back.

Meanwhile, Coventry were far from convincing defensively but found a way to beat their relegation rivals, climbing to 13th on 12 points, three clear of the drop zone.

Sports.title: Man City are failing to give their supporters something to stand behind as Enzo Maresca's side radiate uncertainty with meek display in Fulham draw, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Man City are failing to give their supporters something to stand behind as Enzo Maresca's side radiate uncertainty with meek display in Fulham draw, writes JACK GAUGHAN

The bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week. In legal limbo, Manchester City’s supporters need something – anything – to stand behind but increasingly their team refuse to provide that solace.

City were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel. Some of that could have been directed at referee Thomas Bramall, after Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal, but certainly a significant number were jeering what they’d just seen. That simply does not happen at the Etihad Stadium, even during the torrid run of two years ago.

But they are witnessing a squad who radiate uncertainty. Who take three touches when two will do; who always receive possession squarely facing their own goal; who do not create passing lines for their mates. And crucially, who are forever momentarily confused as to who exactly is picking up which runner and those split seconds make all the difference in this division.

There is just this strange state of unease around how they want to approach games at the moment, something that adversity can provoke and something that Maresca is adamant he can correct. A coach of his calibre should do given the time and freedom.

Yet when he spent the two-week international break studying clips and fashioning ways of improving, he cannot have envisaged a scenario whereby home fans were so incredulous at a lack of energy that they were roused to their feet when Haaland deigned to close down Bernd Leno and force an error.

Man City put in an underwhelming performance as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham

Enzo Maresca's side are radiating uncertainty and look worryingly vulnerable at the back

Rodrigo Muniz made City pay as he put an impressive Fulham 1-0 ahead after 16 minutes

Fulham popped it about nicely and at will. Found pockets to hurt their illustrious hosts, who were again asking a centre half – in this case Marc Guehi – to charge into midfield. City did have more balance than at Nottingham Forest for including Ayyoub Bouaddi for Enzo Fernandez, yet Alvaro Arbeloa still aggressively pressed them in that area to some success.

‘I told the players that we will have the chance to beat them if we play with courage,’ said Arbeloa, who was indebted to the towering performance of defender David Affengruber.

Arsenal will have watched this grinning and could easily be racking up an unassailable lead once these teams meet in north London next Sunday. Unassailable with all the usual caveats about the appeal and what this season may or may not eventually mean.

City did create enough statistically but as with other games of late, that did not tell the whole story.

Calvin Bassey pirouetted through midfield, the heavily derided Gianluigi Donnarumma thwarting a number of strong Fulham chances, and City appeared somewhat lost and out of ideas.

Elliot Anderson equalised with a superb volley but City failed to create much after that

Maresca expressed his concern at City's lack of clean sheets after they struggled again

That is a worrying departure from recent defeats, where they attacked with the same abandon as that early season flourish when they might as well have hosted games at Madison Square Gardens and played with an orange ball.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS MAN CITY (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 7; Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Guehi 5, O’Reilly 5 (Gvardiol 78); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 7 (Fernandez 85); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 78), Foden 7 (Cherki 70), Doku 5; Haaland 5 Scorer: Anderson 57 Booked: Donnarumma Manager: Enzo Maresca 5 FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Leno 6; Tete 6, Affengruber 8, Bassey 7, Sessegnon 7 (Palacios 83); Berge 6, Charles 7; Bobb 7 (Garcia 78), King 6 (Larsson 70, 6), Iwobi 7 (Robinson 70, 6); Muniz 7 (Cairney 83) Scorer: Muniz 16. Booked: Iwobi, Bassey, Charles Manager: Alvaro Arbeloa 7 Referee: Thomas Bramall 5

Met with a Fulham who had not conceded more than once in the league since the start of September, City failed to create a meaningful opportunity in the last 25 minutes of a match they were desperate to win and should have been in the ascendancy of after Elliot Anderson’s volleyed equaliser after half time.

Maresca, though, is more concerned with a lack of clean sheets. It’s now none of those in nine games in all competitions for the first time in seven years, with Rodrigo Muniz opening the scoring on 16 minutes. A throw inside Fulham’s own third prompted Guehi to jump and lose his duel, City turned around and Oscar Bobb laid on for Muniz.

‘We’re conceding too many goals,’ Maresca said. ‘We need to avoid it. You need to win games 1-0. You need clean sheets. We’re not able to do it. But I can see many positive aspects. We started four months ago and not four years ago.

‘We’ve conceded almost 80 per cent of our goals at the start of the first half and second half. It’s something we need to improve. It’s a throw in at the corner flag and nobody is expecting they can create something.’

Maresca was also insistent that Haaland ought to have been awarded an equaliser before the break when poking in on the goal line, yet Bramall adjudged that Leno had the ball under control on field, with VAR not overruling.

Some hard luck, some profligacy with Haaland squandering a couple of big chances, but the day was summed up when in stoppage time, Jeremy Doku was penalised for a foul throw.

Sports.title: Giving Youri Tielemans a £35m release clause looks like an error... Aston Villa toiling to a draw with Sunderland was more proof Unai Emery could do with a midfield controller in January, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.

The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.

Unai Emery was distraught to lose Tielemans and against Sunderland, you could see why. Emery signed two central midfielders, Leon Goretzka and Joao Gomes, and has given more minutes to Ross Barkley.

None of the three gives him what Tielemans did and Villa may decide to move for another central player in January. Anything for a bit of cleverness in that part of the pitch.

Tielemans has struggled at United and it will be interesting to see what Mauricio Pochettino makes of him. He is no elite athlete and United supporters and pundits have criticised him because of it but he gave Emery what he craves above all else – control. Neither Gomes nor Goretzka has Tielemans’ passing range and Barkley looks more effective higher up the pitch.

With Sunderland sitting deep here, Villa desperately needed a player who could read the game and create angles like Tielemans. Without him, their passing was slow and predictable, against a Sunderland side without key men Dominic Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey.

Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele stretches for the ball but nobody could find the breakthrough

Regis Le Bris saw his side pick up another point to follow their win over Chelsea before the international break - Sunderland now sit 18th

Their only chance in the first half here fell to Emi Buendia, who won the ball high then failed to chip the back-pedalling Robin Roefs. In the second half, Ian Maatsen and substitute Ibrahim Mbaye shot far too close to the Sunderland goalkeeper, who tipped over another effort from Barkley.

Villa have still not lost in the league since they were beaten here by Nottingham Forest in September but teams aiming for the Champions League should put away Sunderland at home. And after 150 Premier League games at the helm, nobody will know that better than Emery.

Buendia reached Aston Villa immortality last May when he scored in the Europa League final and now he has his own banner.

‘It’s Buendia, with a beauty, on the banks of the Bosphorus’ read the slogan in the Holte End.

They will never forget that 3-0 win over Freiburg here but it is alarming just how quickly the team has split apart since then. Six months have passed since Istanbul but only two of the starting XI from that night – Buendia and Torres – were in Unai Emery’s line-up here.

Emi Buendia is now the subject of a banner from Villa fans for his Europa League final heroics

Youri Tielemans scored a stunner in the Europa League final but is now at Man United

True, Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof were injured, while John McGinn was left on the bench, with one eye on Tuesday’s return to Istanbul to face Galatasaray in the Champions League. Boubacar Kamara missed the final through injury.

Still these are huge changes. For most of Emery’s first four years at Villa, every player knew his role and understood the kind of team they were. Now Villa find themselves learning on the job in a three-sided ground, due to the improvement work that leaves the North Stand empty.

Emery knows it too. ‘We have brought a significant number of new players to the squad, many of whom are still adapting to the demands of competing at the level we have worked so hard to establish ourselves at.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Wan-Bissaka 6, Harwood-Bellis 6, Torres 7, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Goretzka 5 (Barkley 73, 6); Alysson 6, Buendia 6 (McGinn 60, 7), Manzambi 5 (Mbaye 60, 6); Jackson 6 (Madjo 73, 6). Booked: Goretzka Manager: Unai Emery 6 SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 7; Meunier 7, Mukiele 7, O’Nien 7, Reinildo 7; Ahoka 8, Sadiki 7; Hume 6, Le Fee 7, Talbi 7; Isidor 7 (Angulo 77, 6). Booked: Hume Manager: Regis Le Bris 7 Referee: Andrew Madley 6 Attendance: 36,771

'It takes time, patience, hard work and belief.

‘That is why, now more than ever, we must stick together, trust the direction we are heading in and continue to get behind our players and staff. Results are hugely important but so is recognising the hard work and development that will help us keep moving forward.’

These days clubs like Sunderland cannot afford to wait for young talents to prove themselves in other European leagues.

A decade ago, clubs in the middle of the Premier League could sign players like that for relatively small sums. Now everyone in Europe knows how rich top flight clubs in England are and adjust their prices accordingly.

That is why Sunderland paid nearly £10million for Jules Ahoka even though he had barely played a senior game for Royal Antwerp.

On this evidence, the Black Cats have spent wisely yet again. Ahoka is quick, athletic and strong – exactly what is required in English football today – and his technique is tidy too. If he stays healthy, a bright future awaits.

Sports.title: England dominated every area in complete performance: The lineout was formidable and the attack purred as Lewis Moody staring down the haka set tone for crushing win over New Zealand, writes NIK SIMON
Sports.content:
England dominated every area in complete performance: The lineout was formidable and the attack purred as Lewis Moody staring down the haka set tone for crushing win over New Zealand, writes NIK SIMON

From the moment Maro Itoje embraced Lewis Moody’s and escorted him into the middle of the Twickenham pitch, everyone knew it would take something formidable to break England’s resistance.

Moody, or Mad Dog as he was known when he won the 2003 World Cup, anchored England’s players as they walked into a V formation against the All Blacks’ haka. It was a moment of rugby history, sending chills down every spine in the stadium.

Moody is battling motor neurone disease and his remarkable, unbreakable spirit pumped through English veins. His presence set the tone as England secured their first back-to-back wins over the All Blacks since – rather fittingly – 2003.

England dominated every area but the lineout was particularly formidable. It is Steve Borthwick’s specialist subject and on days like this, with Jamie George at hooker, their set-piece drills look like the best in the world. They move quickly across the floor, with jumpers soaring like eagles, firing into the maul like a pumping assembly of pistons.

Their attack purred. Thanks to Lee Blackett, England’s set-piece strike play was unstoppable. The 10-12 axis between Fin Smith and Seb Atkinson cut through like an angle grinder. There were razor-sharp running lines and an industrious ability to find space faster than the labouring All Black defence. And at the grand old age of 33, when many had written him off, Henry Slade is again showing the best version of himself in an England shirt.

Slade scored after just five minutes and Jack van Poortvliet followed suit. This was the complete performance. There was a time when it felt like the entire All Black team could be cast as 007. They had an aura that made you think they would never die. Here, they were uncloaked. Ben Earl ran through Cameron Roigard like a wet paper bag to score the try that handed England a 19-0 lead after 36 minutes. James Bond? These Kiwis would not stand a chance against Robert Pattinson.

Lewis Moody (England, fourth right) took to the field before England's win over New Zealand and fronted the haka response

England's attack purred as they dominated every area - with the lineout particularly formidable

‘The most important thing is how you start the game against New Zealand,’ said England skipper Maro Itoje. ‘Teams have done different things against the haka, different formations.

‘Having Lewis and his family gave us an extra lift. The idea was floated about him potentially joining us for the haka and our senior guys gave overwhelming support.

‘I remember watching England play, particularly around 2011, and I remember his heroic performances for England, throwing his body around. The way he played was inspirational. He was one of the guys I looked up to as a young boy. To be able to welcome him onto the field was a memory that will live with me for the rest of my life.’

On Friday night, Moody and his 2003 teammates enjoyed a glamorous reunion at the Dorchester on Park Lane. Everyone from Sir Clive Woodward to Jonny Wilkinson were there. At one point, Mike and Zara Tindall even got on the microphone for a singalong.

The ‘03 lot are a patriotic bunch but even they could not reach a consensus about how Borthwick’s team would fare against the Kiwis. England had beaten Fiji, Argentina, Australia and Japan but, on paper, none of those teams were in the same division as the All Blacks.

This was the litmus test of the Class of 26’s progress and they excelled from the start. They suffocated the Kiwi attack, tackling in packs, forcing the most basic of handling errors from Damian McKenzie, Will Jordan and Jordie Barrett. The All Blacks’ world famous attack mustered just two linebreaks across 80 minutes. Credit there must go to defence coach Richard Wigglesworth.

England enjoyed 74 per cent of the territory. The Kiwis were turned over, lacked linespeed and were void of accuracy. It was so bad that by the end of the night, coach Dave Rennie was being asked if he feared for his job.

‘We were miles off,’ said Rennie. ‘We were well short. If you look at the stats, we were well beaten in almost every number. I’m not going to hide from he fact we weren’t good enough and I’m a big part of that. Against Wales, the only thing we lacked was our finish. Last week I said that we let the country down but we were way worse tonight. We need to work out why.’

Ben Earl made 20 carries in the first half - by full-time, he had beaten eight defenders and made 138 metres

The All Blacks have averaged more than 250 running metres per half under Rennie. In the first half here at Twickenham, they managed just 74. In contrast, Earl made 20 carries alone in the first half. By full-time, he had beaten eight defenders and made 138m single-handedly. He compensated for the absence of England’s front-line wingers, with Tommy Freeman pulling out shortly before kick-off with a thigh injury.

Cadan Murley joined Will Joseph on the wing. Murley delivered one of his best England performances and Joseph showcased the depth that is quietly building for next year’s World Cup.

England’s lineout clinic continued into the second half. Alex Coles stole Codie Taylor’s throw and Ollie Chessum scored down the left flank.

After losing to Wales last week, there were fears of a New Zealand backlash. ‘Born to Dare,’ read the All Black  outside Twickenham train station. Beauden Barrett’s breakaway try in the 52nd minute oozed class but it was a standalone moment.

Throughout the second half, Borthwick unloaded his smash and bash bench. Ellis Genge, George Martin and Greg Fisilau injected a level of power that the All Blacks could not live with.

Fin Smith limped off with cramp but Marcus Smith picked up the baton. He kicked penalties and sent Atkinson over to score. He ran his thumb across his throat in celebration as England turned the show into a blood opera.

Second to Moody’s appearance, the late sight of Chessum dump tackling Scott Barrett into the Twickenham turf summed up the performance. The All Blacks were well and truly buried.

Sports.title: Lewis Moody, 48, stares down New Zealand Haka with England as ITV viewers brought to tears
Sports.content:
Lewis Moody, 48, stares down New Zealand Haka with England as ITV viewers brought to tears

England legend Lewis Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease in September 2025, joined Steve Borthwick's players on the pitch to face the New Zealand haka ahead of Saturday's clash at Twickenham

View 3 Images Lewis Moody faced down the haka (Image: David Rogers, Getty Images)

Former England captain Lewis Moody joined Steve Borthwick's squad on the pitch to confront the New Zealand haka in an extraordinary moment before Saturday's encounter at the Allianz Stadium. The 2003 Rugby World Cup champion stood beside the current England team as they formed an arrow formation in answer to the traditional Maori challenge, with Moody positioned at the head of the arrangement in a gesture that touched spectators watching globally.

‌



‌



Moody, who received his motor neurone disease (MND) diagnosis in September 2025, was also afforded the privilege of presenting the England players with their jerseys before kick-off. The venue erupted as Moody appeared from the tunnel to be greeted by skipper Maro Itoje before taking his position to face the New Zealanders.

‌



Every England player embraced Moody before he departed the pitch to a standing ovation. The 48-year-old's participation created a particularly moving occasion, with England's choice to invite one of their former icons into their haka response attracting widespread acclaim.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

It proved a stirring sight as Moody stood alongside the players, with the ex-flanker once more confronting the All Blacks' renowned pre-match ritual.

‌



Co-commentator Ben Kay, who played alongside Moody, said: "It's very, very difficult to talk about that. I don't think there's anyone I played with that that would have meant more to. He was so pumped up for games. Loved facing the haka."

The response from viewers was instantaneous, with social media awash with messages from fans who confessed they had been brought to tears by the scenes. Television presenter Sonja McLaughlin was amongst those expressing her feelings, posting: "OMG what a brilliant idea to have Lewis Moody face the Haka. That's hit right in the feels."

‌



View 3 Images Lewis Moody faces the haka (Image: 2026 The RFU)

View 3 Images Lewis Moody stands at the tip of England's arrow to face the haka

‌



Another spectator commented: "Emotional scenes at Twickenham. Lewis Moody one of the greats."

The England setup also received recognition for including the former skipper in their response, with one fan posting: "A superb gesture from @EnglandRugby inviting @LewisMoody7 into the response."

‌



Someone else remarked: "Brilliant to see Lewis Moody on the pitch with England to face the Haka."

The emotional weight of the occasion was evident in numerous other messages, with one viewer confessing: "Might be crying here a tiny bit watching Lewis Moody on pitch for the Haka."

A further supporter contributed: "Lewis Moody faces the Haka once again. That was a special moment. Now, let's bring it ABs."

‌



Another shared: "In tears already seeing Lewis Moody with the England Rugby team! Face the Haka! Of New Zealand.."

The moment formed part of the unveiling of Moody's new 'Front Up to MND' campaign, in partnership with the My Name'5 Doddie Foundation.

‌



The project seeks to generate over £1million for research into the devastating disease, with its inaugural major fundraising event, 'Front Up: Walk the Coast', scheduled for June 12, 2027. Thousands of participants are being urged to complete 26-mile sections of coastline throughout England, Scotland and Wales, with over 175 routes on offer.

Moody has been resolute in using his platform to assist others living with the condition since announcing his diagnosis, and Saturday's occasion provided a platform to bring the campaign to a massive rugby audience.

Sports.title: Willie Mullins drops Mighty Park hint as Mark Walsh's mount makes winning start
Sports.content:
Willie Mullins drops Mighty Park hint as Mark Walsh's mount makes winning start

The 5-4 favourite put in a clear round on his chasing debut at Punchestown and came home ahead of two stablemates from Closutton, leading to bookmakers cutting his price for two Cheltenham Festival races

View Image Mighty Park ridden by Mark Walsh on their way to winning the Conway Piling Beginners Chase at Punchestown (Image: Damien Eagers/Press Association)

Willie Mullins dropped a hint about Mighty Park's future over fences as the bright prospect made a successful debut in the discipline.

‌



‌



The 5-4 favourite was not fluent at the second last in the Conway Piling Beginners Chase but he was able to take the lead under Mark Walsh and kept on up the run-in to beat stablemates Saint Baco and Laurets d'Estruval.

‌



A leading fancy for the Supreme Novices' Hurdle over two miles at the Cheltenham Festival last season, Mighty Park could only finish ninth behind the battling trio of Old Park Star, Sober Glory and Mydaddypaddy.

Bookmakers Betway cut the price of the Walsh's mount to 12-1 both the Arkle Chase (two miles) and Brown Advisory (three) at next year's flagship fixture in Gloucestershire.

Sports.title: Man City left frustrated by VAR decision as impressive Fulham prolong crisis
Sports.content:
Man City left frustrated by VAR decision as impressive Fulham prolong crisis

MAN CITY 1-1 FULHAM: A superb goal from Elliot Anderson wasn't enough to give Manchester City their first Premier League win for over a month, having gone behind against Fulham

View 2 Images Fulham went ahead through Rodrigo Muniz (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

Manchester City slumped to a fourth successive Premier League game without a win as they were held a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham. Elliot Anderson's superb volley cancelled out Rodrigo Muniz's opening goal, but Enzo Maresca and his players were ultimately left frustrated by an excellent Fulham performance.

‌



‌



Alvaro Arbeloa's men got off to a dream start through Muniz, who rewarded his manager's faith after being handed his first start of the season in the league. With 16 minutes on the clock, the Brazilian finished with aplomb to give Gianluigi Donnarumma no chance, but take nothing away from Oscar Bobb's wonderful assist.

‌



The former City winger bamboozled Anderson with his dribbling before cutting inside on his stronger left foot. Bobb's pass was the perfect weight for Muniz to control and fire high into the net, leaving the Etihad stunned.

‌



VAR then took centre stage, as Erling Haaland thought that he'd made it 1-1. After a dangerous cross from Iliman Ndiaye, the City striker forced both the ball and Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno over the line.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



But referee Thomas Bramall deemed that Leno had two hands on the ball when Haaland kicked it through his palms. A VAR check ensued - as well as a debate.

Joe Cole, on commentary for TNT Sports, said: "Bernd Leno does get two hands on it. Erling Haaland doesn't get much contact which is unusual for him. It's very harsh. Leno's got no control of the ball because he can't read Haaland hitting the ball."

‌



Meanwhile, Michael Brown bemoaned on BBC Radio 5 Live: "How soft is that? I don't think Bernd Leno has got enough control on that."

Much to Haaland and the home side's frustration, the goal wasn't given. VAR explained: "The ball is in control between both hands and then is played out of that possession by the attacker, and then into the back of the net."

‌



Should the goal have stood? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Erling Haaland was adjudged to have fouled Bernd Leno (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



City's supporters made their feelings clear upon the half-time whistle, but they were much happier soon after the break. When Fulham failed to fully clear a corner kick in the 58th minute, Anderson took aim and produced a volley which nestled past an unsighted Leno to level the scores.

Maresca rung in the changes as City pushed for a winner, although they had Donnarumma to thank for a good save to deny Muniz on the counter attack. Fulham held strong at the back themselves late on and claimed a deserved draw to move further away from the relegation zone.

Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk makes honest Liverpool exit admission and opens up on what's next

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk is out of contract in the summer and could leave Anfield

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk could leave Liverpool (Image: Marco Steinbrenner/Getty Images)

Virgil van Dijk admits he has no idea if he'll be at Liverpool next season but says he has the hunger to play on for many years yet.

‌



‌



The 35-year-old centre-back, who has claimed two Premier League titles and the Champions League during his time at Liverpool, is out of contract in the summer with no new deal on the table.

‌



"The most important thing for me is that I feel good and I look after myself, and I think I have many more years ahead of me on the pitch," he told Sky Sports.

‌



"Whatever happens after this season, we'll see. At the moment, anyone who says they know what I'll be doing next season is not telling the truth, because I myself have no idea as I'm speaking to you now."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The Netherlands international won't be short of potential suitors should Liverpool decide his Anfield chapter is over, and he insists he remains unfazed about what lies ahead.

"I'm calm about it," he added. "Those who know me know that I only focus on what I can control, which right now is the Manchester United game; then we'll focus on the Champions League, and we'll see what happens in the new year. If the contract is renewed, we'll see, and if not, I'll say goodbye to everyone in the summer."

View 2 Images Van Dijk has been at the heart of Liverpool's defence for nearly a decade (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

Van Dijk arrived at Liverpool from Southampton in 2018 and went on to taste remarkable success on Merseyside, eventually inheriting the captain's armband from Jordan Henderson.

‌



Casting his mind back over his time at the club, he said: "It has been a wonderful journey. I'll have completed almost 10 years in the summer; it has been a big part of my life, and I'll be forever grateful for everything that has happened over these years.

Sports.title: Harry Kane breaks silence on major injury from hospital as he faces months out
Sports.content:
Harry Kane breaks silence on major injury from hospital as he faces months out

Harry Kane faces months on the sidelines after suffering an ankle injury and he's broken his silence on the setback from his hospital bed

View 2 Images Harry Kane has posted an update (Image: Instagram/@harrykane)

Harry Kane has broken his silence after suffering a serious ankle injury. The England and Bayern Munich star posted an update from his hospital bed after undergoing surgery.

‌



‌



On Friday, Bayern faced FC Koln at the Allianz Arena and in the 15th minute, Kane was caught whilst attempting to connect with a Michael Olise cross. Koln defender Joel Schmied reached the ball first and followed through, crashing into Kane's standing leg.

‌



The Ballon d'Or winner, who has suffered from ankle problems in the past, attempted to run the injury off but eventually succumbed to the discomfort. He limped off alongside two physios after signalling to the dugout and later left the stadium on crutches following the 1-1 draw.

‌



Post-match examinations confirmed the 33-year-old striker had suffered a high-ankle injury involving the syndesmosis ligament. He will now face months out and has sent a message from his hospital bed after undergoing successful surgery for the ligament tear.

Harry Kane made secret visit at Premier League training ground READ MORE :

Inside England’s World Cup recovery including squad overhaul and Thomas Tuchel change READ MORE :

Kane wrote on Instagram: "The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

"'Tough times don't last, tough people do' – my guy [former NFL wide receiver Julian Edelman] told me this one! Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut!"

‌



His club, Bayern, confirmed that the surgery was successful and that Kane will be out for "the next few months." The German side wished their star striker well.

View 2 Images Kane faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

This means Kane will miss some key ties for club and possibly country. Assuming Kane returns around mid-to-late February, he will miss the remainder of Bayern's Champions League league phase, including a game against Manchester United on January 20. Some tough league matches, including a clash with Bayer Leverkusen, will likely be missed as well.

‌



Kane also faces a race to get fit for England's crucial Nations League quarter-final matches against Norway. This two-legged affair begins on March 27, so it will be touch-and-go whether Kane will make this date.

Sports.title: Rugby star, 42, tragically killed in motorcycle crash as club pay heartbreaking tribute
Sports.content:
Rugby star, 42, tragically killed in motorcycle crash as club pay heartbreaking tribute

The former Wales Under-21 international and Dragons RFC scrum-half has died following a motorbike accident in Bermuda

View 2 Images James Ireland (centre) has passed away (Image: Getty)

Former Wales Under-21 international and Dragons RFC scrum-half James Ireland has died tragically following a motorbike accident in Bermuda. The collision occurred in the early hours of Wednesday, November 11.

‌



‌



The 42-year-old has sustained severe injuries while riding a Vespa along North Shore Road in Hamilton parish. Having received emergency treatment for a serious head wound at the scene, he was rushed to King Edward VII Memorial Hospital, where he was sadly pronounced dead.

‌



Ireland was on the island competing in the Bermuda World Rugby Classic, representing Italy - the country where he turned out for Rugby Parma and Crociati Parma throughout his playing career.

‌



He made 10 appearances for the Dragons and also lined up for Birmingham Moseley, Newport, Cross Keys, London Welsh and Bedwas. The scrum-half was capped by Wales at Under-21 level and was part of the squad that clinched an U21 Six Nations Grand Slam in 2005.

James Botham's Wales absence explained as Steve Tandy reveals why he changed winning team READ MORE :

In a statement confirming the heartbreaking news, Ireland's former club Parma said: "A grave loss has struck the Gialloblu family. James passed away last week in Bermuda, where he was with the Italia Classic team competing in the World Rugby Classic. He was only 42 years old.

View 2 Images Ireland (left) played for Wales at Under-21 level (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"A scrum-half, he wore the yellow and blue shirt in the 2008/09 and 2009/10 seasons, when the team played in the Super 10, before continuing his career with Crociati Parma from 2010 to 2012.

‌



"On behalf of the entire Club, the management, the coaches, the players and the fans, we extend our deepest condolences to his family and all his loved ones."

Dai Rees, Ireland's former coach at the Dragons, Wales Under-19s and Cross Keys, said: "It's a deep, deep, deep sadness to hear of James' accident and the loss. My thoughts are with his parents, his family and his wife and three children."

‌



In an official statement, Bermuda Police confirmed: "Sadly, the Bermuda Police Service (BPS) can now confirm Bermuda's 16th road fatality of 2026, a 42-year-old male visitor and extends sincere condolences to his loved ones.

"The visiting 42-year-old UK national was seriously injured in a reported single-vehicle collision involving the 50cc rental scooter he was riding, along North Shore Road, in Hamilton parish, around 2am Wednesday, 11th November 2026.

‌



"Police, Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service, as well as ambulance personnel responded.

"Despite lifesaving efforts at the scene, which continued as he was rushed to King Edward VII Memorial Hospital via ambulance, an on-call doctor later pronounced him dead.

Sports.title: Harry Kane out for MONTHS as Bayern Munich confirm England captain's major injury blow
Sports.content:
Harry Kane out for MONTHS as Bayern Munich confirm England captain's major injury blow

Harry Kane had to be substituted in the 20th minute of Bayern Munich's 1-1 draw with Koln on Friday night and tests have confirmed that the 33-year-old has suffered a serious ankle injury

View 2 Images Harry Kane will be sidelined until 2027 (Image: Getty)

Bayern Munich have confirmed that Harry Kane will be ruled out for a 'few months' after the England captain tore his ankle ligaments. Kane, 33, was forced off after just 20 minutes as Bayern drew 1-1 at home to Koln in the Bundesliga on Friday.

‌



‌



The striker had his ankle caught by Koln defender Joel Schmied, who won the ball before making contact. Kane winced in pain as he received treatment but managed to walk off the pitch before being replaced by Tom Bischof.

‌



After Bayern's medical staff assessed Kane's injury, however, it was found that he'd torn his syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle. A statement released after full-time confirmed that he'll be out of action until the new year.

‌



Bayern posted on social media: "Harry Kane sustained a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during this evening's home match against 1. FC Köln. This was confirmed by an examination carried out by FC Bayern’s medical department. The 33 year-old will be sidelined for the next few months. Get well soon, Harry!"

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Reports from Germany suggest that the exact timeframe for Kane's recovery will be three months. That would see him return in time for England's Nations League quarter-final fixtures against Norway on March 27 and March 30.

Unfortunately for Bayern, a full three months on the sidelines would see the Ballon d'Or winner miss a total of 16 games - 18 if Vincent Kompany's side reach the DFB Pokal quarter-finals. That period includes Bayern's game away to Manchester United in the Champions League on January 20.

‌



The German giants also lost Michael Olise to injury at half-time on Friday but say that it's only a bruise, meaning that the French winger could be back for Wednesday's journey to Lille. Bayern had to come from 1-0 down against Koln after Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore scored his first goal for the club in the 12th minute.

‌



View 2 Images Harry Kane suffered the injury after a tackle by Joel Schmied (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

Kane's replacement, Bischof, set up with the equaliser, which was scored by summer signing Nathaniel Brown. But Bayern couldn't find a winner, as Koln earned a valuable point in Munich to pull further away from the relegation zone.

"I think we didn't get off to a bad start, we were really in the game and had some pace," Kompany said post-match. "But then Harry Kane and Michael Olise suffered injuried of course. However, no excuses."

Sports.title: New Cardinals QB Johnson, on 15th team, set to start with Beck out
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, paving the way for 40-year-old Josh Johnson to get his first start for Arizona.

Coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Arizona was preparing Johnson to start after Beck experienced back spasms again this week. Beck didn't practice Thursday or Friday after being a limited participant Wednesday.

Sunday against the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium will be Johnson's first start since Week 18 of last season and just his 12th career start after being a fifth-round pick in 2008. He is 2-9 overall.

Although he doesn't have a lot of starting experience compared with his longevity in the league -- Arizona is his 15th NFL team -- the situation Johnson is in feels "familiar."

"It's kind of my testimony my whole life, just the unknown, what can happen," Johnson said. "And so just always just being in the moment, being prepared for myself. I've been in this situation, particularly in the NFL, a lot. So more excited than nerves, I would say."

Johnson said he is in a constant state of staying ready, which has been a factor in him playing into his 40s. At this point in his career, he's used to it.

Josh Johnson was 1-1 as a fill-in starter for the Commanders in 2025. AP Photo/Ross D. Franklin, File

Last season, Johnson replaced injured Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota in Week 16 and then started the final two games of the season after not starting since 2021.

"My job is to always be ready no matter what, no matter how the situation," Johnson said. "So I focus more on that than what's not ideal. And so this is just the next step of that process, and it keeps happening and so you just keep accepting it. You don't fight it, you embrace it, and you just go with it."

Johnson said his experience working with LaFleur in 2020 when LaFleur was the San Francisco 49ers' receivers coach and in 2021 with the New York Jets when LaFleur was the offensive coordinator will help "tremendously" on Sunday.

"Just understanding how he calls the game first and foremost is very important because you don't have to get antsy, like, 'Oh, what is he going to do in these moments?'" Johnson said. "And Mike is pretty consistent. He's been consistent. I've always been a big fan of him as a playcaller, as a coach, just in general."

Johnson is also familiar with Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, having played against him and being on the Giants when Spagnuolo was New York's defensive coordinator in 2016.

Despite a familiarity and comfort with LaFleur, Johnson is also realistic about how Sunday can go after spending less than two weeks learning the offense.

"I also understand that everything ain't going to be perfect," Johnson said. "I'm not trying to go out there and be perfect. I'm trying to go out there and play winning football."

Sports.title: Titans DL Harrell hospitalized after car accident in Tampa
Sports.content:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Tennessee Titans defensive lineman Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident Friday and remains hospitalized, according to the team.

Harrell, 24, was a passenger in an Uber in Tampa, Florida, when the accident occurred. No further details were available.

"Yesterday, Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident that resulted in him being taken to the hospital in his hometown of Tampa, Florida," the Titans said in a statement. "We have been in constant communication with Jaylen's family and are still working to gather more information.

"At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care. We ask that Jaylen and his family's privacy be respected at this time. We will provide an update when appropriate."

Harrell tore his ACL in the preseason and was placed on season-ending injured reserve. The Titans selected Harrell in the seventh round of the 2024 draft, and he finished his rookie season with 13 combined tackles.

He started two games for Tennessee in 2025 and 25 combined tackles, including 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble.

Sports.title: Maresca: Man City denied 'clear' goal in Fulham draw
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

Enzo Maresca said Manchester City were denied a "clear" goal in their 1-1 draw with Fulham after Erling Haaland was judged to have fouled goalkeeper Bernd Leno.

Haaland thought he had scored when he bundled the ball over the line from Iliman Ndiaye's cross. But referee Tom Bramall decided Leno had control of the ball, a view backed up by VAR.

"I review the goal after the game and from my point of view it is quite clear that it is not a foul, but I am not the guy who decides," Maresca said.

The City boss also said Haaland was convinced he had scored when the ball appeared to slip out of Leno's grasp.

Erling Haaland's goal against Fulham was disallowed for a foul on the goalkeeper. Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images

"He was absolutely sure even when they were reviewing the VAR that it was a goal because I asked from the touchline, but the referee decided differently," Maresca said.

City have now gone four Premier League games without a win and nine games in all competitions without a clean sheet.

Fulham, meanwhile, snapped a 20-match losing run against City stretching back to 2011.
