Sports.title: Raiders owner Davis upset by 'Madden' version of his father: 'Totally unfair'
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis said he was "hurt" by the depiction of his father, the late Al Davis, in the movie "Madden" that was released on Prime Video this week.

"I did the best I could to protect him," Mark Davis told USA Today Sports on Friday. "It's absolutely a crime that they're able to treat people that have passed away and characterize them in ways that are unfair, and there's nobody around to protect their legacies. It's just unfair. I don't know what the purpose of the movie was to be real honest."

"Madden" tells the story of legendary football coach, broadcast and video game icon John Madden, with Nicolas Cage in the titular role and Christian Bale as Al Davis. The film has received criticism for some over-the-top portrayals of several notable sports figures, with The Associated Press review describing the performances as running the "gamut from 'SNL'-style parody to earnest drama."

"Cage's prosthetic-aided performance feels more like a well-meaning misfire than any kind of real travesty. This is more like a goofy, unfunny comedy that can't find the end zone, let alone the 50-yard line," AP reviewer Jake Coyle wrote.

Mark Davis echoed some of that review, calling "Madden" a cross between "Pulp Fiction," "Vacation" and "Saturday Night Live" -- and "not in a good way."

He said the filmmakers had reached out to him about aspects of the movie but that he was off-put by how it depicted his father's reaction to a massive injury to New England Patriots wide receiver Darryl Stingley during a 1978 preseason game against the Raiders. Mark Davis said the filmmakers said they wouldn't be able to change the scene.

"For them to put in the Darryl Stingley incident, that my dad was trying to talk John [Madden] out of going to see him -- that was just such a hurt to me personally because that's my father's legacy is how he treated people," Mark Davis told USA Today. "No matter whether they were Raiders or not, he cared about people. That's one of the redeeming qualities of my father throughout his life. And I just thought it was totally unfair for them to portray it that way."

Mark Davis focused his frustration on the filmmakers, saying "I don't blame Christian Bale. I don't blame Nicholas Cage. All they did was what the director and the writers told them to do."

Al Davis served as coach, general manager and owner of the Raiders. Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1992, Davis became principal owner of the Raiders in 1972 and ran the team until his death in 2011.

Sports.title: 🔮 NFL Week 11 crystal ball: Predictions on upsets, TD scorers, more
Sports.content:
What Stephen A. is looking to see from Vikings in 'litmus test' vs. 49ers (2:29)

Open Extended Reactions

Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Texans defeated the Colts on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 12 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs that could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Eagles pull off an upset over the Steelers? Is 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey in for a big receiving day against the Vikings? Does Titans quarterback Cam Ward have fantasy potential against the Cowboys? Will we see another touchdown for wide receiver Josh Downs in a Chiefs uniform?

Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Philadelphia Eagles +4.5 (+180 moneyline) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers

Quarterback Aaron Rodgers hasn't given much reason to trust Pittsburgh laying points on the road Sunday. Philadelphia's specialty is playing more man coverage and sending extra rushers, both of which have bothered Rodgers in 2026. Plus, defensive tackle Jalen Carter can attack an offensive line that just lost guard Mason McCormick (ankle).

Eagles backup QB Joe Milton taking sacks is the main concern for their offense, but he can still get positive yards as a scrambler. With wide receiver DeVonta Smith potentially returning from a hamstring injury, the Eagles have enough to win this by a field goal.

Minnesota Vikings +3 (+138 moneyline) vs. San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City

Minnesota's defense remains the strength in this Sunday night matchup. Coordinator Brian Flores brings pressure from different places, and 49ers QB Brock Purdy took five sacks against Dallas in Week 10. The Vikings have also been excellent at forcing field goals near the end zone.

Quarterback Kirk Cousins faces a tough matchup himself in his second start for Minnesota, but he gives it a more reliable offense than before. In Mexico City, I trust the Vikings' defense to keep this tight and give Cousins a shot to win it late.

Walder predicts three stat lines

George Karlaftis, Edge, Kansas City Chiefs: 2.5 sacks, 7 pressures, 31% pass rush win rate

It's hard to imagine a better matchup to record a sack than this. Karlaftis typically lines up opposite the left tackle, which means he'll face Arizona's Jayden Williams -- who ranks dead last in pass block win rate at tackle but has missed the past two weeks with a knee injury -- or Williams' backup Josh Fryar.

Karlaftis will be chasing down rookie QB Carson Beck in his second career start -- Beck took five sacks (at over a 20% sack rate) in his debut against the Rams -- or veteran journeyman Josh Johnson. Plus, the Chiefs are 15.5-point favorites, so the Cardinals almost certainly will be behind and need to pass.

Christian McCaffrey, RB, San Francisco 49ers: 9 receptions, 74 receiving yards, 1 receiving touchdown

I'm focusing on McCaffrey's receiving production because I think that will be the headline here. He is already an elite receiving back, but this Vikings matchup should result in heavy usage through the air.

All running backs catch passes more frequently against zone coverage compared to man (almost twice as often), and Minnesota plays the second-highest rate of zone coverage in the league (74%). It also blitzes the most of any team, which would cause most running backs to stay in and block most of the time. But not McCaffrey, as he still runs a route 65% of the time when the opponent blitzes.

So when Minnesota brings the heat in Mexico City, Purdy is going to be looking for his star running back ... a lot.

Joe Burrow, QB, Cincinnati Bengals: 31-of-39, 378 passing yards, 3 touchdowns, 0 sacks, 91 QBR

I know this is chalky considering the heater Burrow is on, but I feel especially confident that he will put up numbers against the Commanders.

Washington blitzes 42% of the time, the third-highest rate in the league, but somehow has a below average pass rush win rate. That is quite the indictment on its ability to disrupt the opposing quarterback. And it's an especially bad combination against Burrow, who is thriving even more when blitzed (86 QBR) than when not (77 QBR) in 2026.

Burrow has also become quite adept at sack avoidance (4.4% sack rate), which is partially a reflection of better pass protection this season. Plus, the Commanders have the most pass-inducing defense in the league, based on NFL Next Gen Stats' opponent pass rate over expected.

Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers

Ryan Flournoy, WR, Dallas Cowboys (37.8% rostered in ESPN leagues)

It's easy to overlook Flournoy as the Cowboys' WR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but he has been productive. Over the past six games, Flournoy has averaged 5.1 targets and 13.2 fantasy points per game.

The Titans-Cowboys matchup has one of the highest totals on the slate. And Tennessee's defense has allowed the most receptions and fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.

Cam Ward, QB, Tennessee Titans (26.0%)

Let's stick with the same game and go with Ward, who has scored at least 19 fantasy points in each of his past two games. He'll be without wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) but could get back rookie Carnell Tate, who has missed the past two games due to a shoulder injury. Ward is a dual-threat quarterback with an excellent matchup against a Cowboys defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points and third-most rushing yards per game to quarterbacks.

play 1:27 Why Cam Ward has real streaming potential in Week 11

Justice Hill, RB, Baltimore Ravens (18.7%)

Ravens running back Derrick Henry has struggled recently, averaging just 3.0 yards per carry over his past five games. Hill, on the other hand, had at least eight touches and scored at least 8.0 fantasy points in each of those games, including 18.2 fantasy points against the Jaguars in Week 9.

Hill could continue to be more involved Sunday against the Panthers. Carolina has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to running backs this season.

Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers

Josh Downs, WR, Kansas City Chiefs

After getting traded from the Colts, Downs caught a touchdown pass in his Chiefs debut against the Falcons. He finished with 53 receiving yards on five targets, operating as an outlet from slot alignments for quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Plus, Downs can attack the third level on seams or wheel routes.

Downs has a great matchup in Week 11 versus a Cardinals defense that has allowed 22 touchdown passes (tied for most in the league) and plays zone coverage on 67.5% of opponent dropbacks. Chiefs coach Andy Reid will have answers to scheme open Downs for a score.

Javonte Williams, RB, Dallas Cowboys

While Williams has found the end zone only once in the past three games, he has nine rushing scores on the year and at least one goal-to-go carry in nine games. I'm expecting him to cash in on a low red zone attempt Sunday against the Titans. Tennessee has allowed 10 rushing touchdowns this season, tied for the 10th most in the NFL.

play 0:41 'A walking atrocity!' Stephen A. can't even laugh about Cowboys' defense

Courtland Sutton, WR, Denver Broncos

Let's take Sutton in a positive matchup versus the Raiders' defense. He has only two touchdown receptions this season, but he has seen seven end zone targets from quarterback Bo Nix, including one in two of his past three games. And Las Vegas has given up 22 touchdown passes in 2026, tied with the Cardinals for the most in the league.

Solak makes four more predictions

The Titans will beat the Cowboys

I don't particularly love the Cowboys changing defensive playcallers the week before they play the Titans, who have gone no-huddle on a whopping 40% of their snaps since Week 7. The Titans' willingness to speed up Dallas will strain its communication with a new coach on the mic, and WR Carnell Tate's return to practice Thursday (albeit in a limited fashion) could foretell a return to the starting lineup.

The Titans have been competitive against the Bengals and Jaguars in recent weeks; they're not an easy out.

Commanders CB Trey Amos will get his first career pick

I like what I've seen from second-year cornerback Amos, who returned to the Commanders' lineup in Week 6 from a fibula injury and has been a solid starter since then. Amos gave up a lot of easy underneath stuff to the Rams' Puka Nacua in Week 9, but he can stay sticky with the Bengals' Tee Higgins downfield Monday night.

Burrow will test the young cornerback, and Amos will take some lumps. But he'll also rip down an interception for his troubles.

Bears RB Kyle Monangai will rush for 100 yards

Monangai looked like a Year 2 leap candidate through four games before a turf toe injury cost him over a month of absence. Two of his four games in 2026 cleared the century mark, and now he draws a Saints defense that is 29th in EPA per designed rush, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Expect Monangai to immediately get back on track.

Jaguars WR Parker Washington will go for 150 receiving yards

Fresh off a big performance against the Titans, Washington draws a great matchup against the Giants, who play the fifth-highest rate of man coverage among all defenses. New York's blitz rate since Week 4 is second highest as well. Washington is QB Trevor Lawrence's preferred target against the man and when blitzed on the season. He can also line up in the slot to avoid the Giants' strong duo of outside corners. High-volume day inbound.

Sports.title: NHL Tonight: What to watch in all 14 games on Saturday
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

From a superb matinee between two of the NHL's top Stanley Cup contenders all the way through to a showdown between the Nos. 1 and 32 in the standings, Saturday is another packed day of action for hockey fans.

With so many options from which to choose, we're here to provide some stats and storylines to help figure out which games get your attention.

Read on for a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Edmonton Oilers at Carolina Hurricanes

1 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | CAR -180, O/U: 6.5

DraftKings lists the Hurricanes (+550) and Oilers (+750) as the two teams with the shortest odds to win the Stanley Cup this season.

And what's more, the two needed a shootout after a 5-5 regulation contest back on Oct. 22. So yeah, this game is definitely worth watching!

Hockey fans are well aware of the Oilers' high-scoring star trio of Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard, but their goalies have started to earn their due too; Devon Levi's 10 wins have him tied for sixth most in the league, while Tristan Jarry's .912 save percentage is tied with Connor Hellebuyck for 10th (among goalies with six or more starts).

Carolina's Sebastian Aho has been overlooked for long enough that he has become the "... and I took that personally" Michael Jordan meme; through 22 games, his 29 points have him tied for 10th in the league. The Canes were also boosted during the past week with the return of captain Jordan Staal, the 2026 Conn Smythe winner who tore his calf earlier this season.

Both teams are coming in to this matchup having lost their most recent game, thus breaking extended winning streaks. Which one can start a new streak going?

Chicago Blackhawks at Calgary Flames

3:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CGY -162, O/U: 5.5

It would not be surprising to see these teams vying for positioning in the draft lottery standings as the end of the season closes in, but there are tantalizing reasons to check out this matchup nevertheless.

The Blackhawks will again be without captain Connor Bedard, whose recent shoulder injury will keep him out for at least four games. Unfortunately, Chicago has had a lot of experience playing Bedard-less in recent seasons, but it's an opportunity for others like Frank Nazar to shine.

On the other side, Flames leading scorer Joel Farabee has been delivering the goods on a bargain $5 million AAV contract. Does all this production result in a trade before this season's deadline, or is the Syracuse native part of the long-term plans?

Buffalo Sabres at Florida Panthers

6 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | FLA -155, O/U: 6.5

Are the Cats primed for some vengeance?

The Sabres defeated the Panthers 5-3 back on Oct. 12 in Buffalo, one of the club's nine wins this season and one of two against Atlantic Division foes. Noah Ostlund had the go-ahead goal in that one, while Tage Thompson added an insurance tally.

Thompson's Team USA Olympic teammate Matthew Tkachuk had just one assist in that game but is now riding a nine-game scoring streak with 12 points total during the span.

Pittsburgh Penguins at Nashville Predators

6 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NSH -135, O/U: 6.5

It's a 2017 Stanley Cup Final rematch!

One of these teams is much more likely to get back there than the other this season, as the Predators enter this game in the first Western wild-card spot while the Penguins are last in the Eastern Conference.

But, it was Pittsburgh that won the first game between the clubs this season, 3-2 in OT back on Oct. 24.

A trio of veterans leads the scoring charge for Nashville -- Filip Forsberg (24 points), Steven Stamkos (12 goals), Roman Josi (21 assists) -- while Erik Karlsson (16 assists, 19 points) and former Pred Tommy Novak (eight goals) top the charts for Pittsburgh.

Washington Capitals at Boston Bruins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | BOS -120, O/U: 6.5

The Capitals are one of four teams to have not hit the 21-game mark, i.e. the quarter point of the regular season, but will do so here. It has been a rough time lately, with four straight losses -- two to the Devils, as well as the Lightning and Sabres.

Boston was in first place in the Atlantic Division recently, but some uneven play -- coupled with the competitiveness among the top-tier teams -- has them down to fourth as play begins Saturday.

So there's pressure on both teams to earn a W here, particularly as both have designs on qualifying for the playoffs.

Alex Ovechkin remains at just one goal this season, but offseason addition Alex Tuch has 13 of them! For Boston, captain David Pastrnak leads the scoring across the board, with 10 goals and 18 assists.

Columbus Blue Jackets at Toronto Maple Leafs

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TOR -122, O/U: 6.5

These two teams made a pretty fun trade on the eve of the season, with Kirill Marchenko among the players headed to Toronto and Matthew Knies the leading player that was sent to Columbus.

While it seemed like the kind of mutually beneficial deal that could make both teams better positioned for a playoff push, each has struggled mightily thus far.

Marchenko scored in his first game against his former team (a 6-2 Leafs win), but has not played since Oct. 26 and is just now returning to practice.

Knies had a lot of goose eggs on his game log but has gotten in a groove in November with seven points in eight games. Maybe he has something special in mind for his return to Toronto?

Philadelphia Flyers at Montreal Canadiens

7 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | MTL -166, O/U: 5.5

An atrocious start of the season put the Flyers in the Eastern Conference basement, but they have now gone 4-1-1 in their past six games. Could this be the start of something big?

This matchup will give us a clue. The Canadiens have been a bit up-and-down as of late, but enter this game riding high following wins over the top two teams in the Metro Division -- 3-2 over the Devils on Wednesday and 2-1 in OT against the Canes on Thursday.

It's the first matchup of three this regular season between the clubs.

Los Angeles Kings at Ottawa Senators

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -170, O/U: 5.5

The Kings' Eastern road trip has gotten off to a great start, with a 3-0 win over the Bruins and a 4-3 shootout victory over the Leafs. Does that continue Saturday against the Sens before a date Monday with the Canadiens?

Artemi Panarin -- the Kings' leading scorer who has been away from the team for personal reasons -- is reportedly set to return for this game, and that's a big addition: He leads L.A. in both goals (eight) and assists (11).

Ottawa will hope that Linus Ullmark can limit Panarin and the Kings' offense better than the tandem of Samuel Ersson and Jonas Johansson did in L.A.'s 6-5 OT win on Oct. 29. Ullmark is the NHL's current leader in goals-against average (1.42) and save percentage (.940).

New York Islanders at Detroit Red Wings

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYI -112, O/U: 5.5

Would you rather build your team around a 24-year-old Swedish winger or a 19-year-old Canadian defenseman?

Breaking News from Emily Kaplan Download the ESPN app and enable Emily Kaplan's news alerts to receive push notifications for the latest updates first. Opt in by tapping the alerts bell in the top right corner. For more information, click here.

That's the foundational question as these teams square off for Game 1 of their regular-season series.

The Red Wings are led across the board in scoring by Lucas Raymond, the aforementioned winger, who has nine goals and 13 assists, while the Islanders are similarly led by reigning Calder Trophy winner Matthew Schaefer, who has nine goals and 15 assists.

One game won't decide the answer of course, but pay special attention to how each of those players takes over the ice when he's out there.

New Jersey Devils at St. Louis Blues

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ -135, O/U: 6.5

This is the second and final matchup between these interconference rivals this season, after the Devils won 5-4 in OT in Newark in Connor Hellebuyck's fourth game with his new team.

It was not Helly's sharpest game of the season -- allowing four goals on 32 shots -- but that was a shade better than Jordan Binnington, who allowed five on 37.

Jack Hughes is the Devils' leading goal scorer thus far, with 10, while Jesper Bratt leads New Jersey in assists (18); Jimmy Snuggerud (12 goals) and Robert Thomas (16 assists) are their counterparts for St. Louis.

Vegas Golden Knights at Winnipeg Jets

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | VGK -135, O/U: 6.5

Vegas is looking to get some of its swagger back after four straight losses, including -- almost unbelievably -- to the Canucks. Meanwhile, Winnipeg is winners of seven of its past eight contests.

Mark Stone -- who became the Knights' all-time leading scorer Thursday -- is the current goals leader for Vegas (11), while Mitch Marner tops the assists column (23).

The Jets are led by by old mainstays Kyle Connor (18 goals) and Mark Scheifele (22 assists).

Anaheim Ducks at Utah Mammoth

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -162, O/U: 6.5

Sadly, Cutter Gauthier's goal-scoring streak ended at 10 games, as no one on the Ducks was able to score against the Avalanche on Thursday. Is it time for him to start another?

Tasked with stopping him is a Mammoth team that beat those same Avalanche its last time out, thanks to goals from four different scorers.

Given that both teams are in the bottom dozen in goal suppression, there should be opportunities for each here; keep your eyes on Gauthier, Leo Carlsson and Jackson LaCombe for Anaheim, along with Clayton Keller, Logan Cooley and Mikhail Sergachev for Utah.

Minnesota Wild at Vancouver Canucks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -285, O/U: 6.5

On Oct. 25, defenseman Quinn Hughes made his first appearance back in Vancouver as a member of the Wild following last season's blockbuster trade. Despite the best wishes of the home faithful, Minnesota won 4-2, and Hughes finished with a goal and an assist.

As play begins Saturday, this game matches the top team in the NHL standings in the Wild against the team at the very bottom in the Canucks. So one would assume that Hughes, Kirill Kaprizov & Co. would roll here, right?

To counter that notion, the Canucks have won two of their last three, both of which were against high-caliber teams in the Golden Knights and Mammoth. Are the Wild next up on the upset train?

Seattle Kraken at San Jose Sharks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | SJ -118, O/U: 6.5

A relatively sparse early schedule -- including time off before and after two games in Finland -- means that this is Game No. 20 for Seattle, while this will be the 25th of the season for San Jose.

That matters, because the Sharks -- projected by many to be a playoff team this spring -- are just a point ahead of the Kraken, who did not begin the season with that kind of expectation.

This is the first of four matchups between the Pacific Division foes, and each team is led in scoring by its 2024 first-round pick:

Macklin Celebrini (No. 1) has 27 points in 22 games for San Jose.

Berkly Catton (No. 8) has 17 in 19 for Seattle.

Reminder: Fans can catch all the action in the NHL streaming hub and on the ESPN App.
