In a statement on Saturday, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) described the rally as a “disgraceful flop” and said that residents of Oyo State and other parts of the region had shunned the event.

The organisation said the turnout showed that the South-west had rejected Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid and was increasingly backing Mr Makinde as an alternative in the 2027 presidential election.

“Burdened by failure and rejection, President Tinubu could not articulate any meaningful message to the people of Oyo State, but ironically accepted an empty scorecard by saying, ‘I will not be able to speak much to you. I just want to greet you.”

However, the campaign’s claim of poor attendance contrasts with a report by The ICIR, whose reporter at the venue described the gathering at Mapo Hall as a “mammoth crowd,” with supporters filling the main stage, backstage areas and surrounding streets.

The rally was also reportedly scaled down following a directive by Mr Tinubu that it be held without much fanfare in honour of victims of Friday’s boat accident in Bayelsa State. The president had expressed condolences to the bereaved families and directed federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts.

The MDPCO, however, argued that the rally’s turnout was evidence of Mr Tinubu’s waning popularity, contrasting it with the crowds that attended Mr Makinde’s presidential declaration on 14 May 2026, under the Allied Peoples Movement (APM).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It also accused the president of resorting to insults, mudslinging and unfulfilled promises instead of presenting his administration’s record to voters.

“Instead of presenting his stewardship in government, President Tinubu is making another list of fake promises, including the provision of electricity, the same promise he made three and half years ago,” the statement said.

The campaign’s reaction followed Mr Tinubu’s remarks at the rally, where he appeared to take a swipe at the APM, describing its members as a group with nowhere to go.

Mr Tinubu at the event also publicly endorsed the APC’s governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states: Sharafadeen Alli, Solomon Adeola and Obafemi Hamzat.

World.title: Niger village attack sparks deadly reprisals
World.content:
A dawn attack in which many people were reportedly killed in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State has triggered a wave of violence in neighbouring communities, including deadly reprisal attacks targeting Fulani residents and refugees.

Suspected terrorists reportedly killed at least 11 people, including a village head, his wife and children, in the attacks on Saturday in Lumman-Ba’are and Gada-Oli communities, according to a report by Daily Trust.

The newspaper stated that the assailants also burnt houses, abducted residents and rustled cattle.

The spokesperson for the Niger State Police Command, Wasiu Abiodun, confirmed the attack on Lumman-Ba’are.

In a statement quoted by Daily Trust, Mr Abiodun said the police received a report at about 5 a.m. on Saturday that armed men had invaded the village and killed about five people.

“Joint security teams have been deployed to the location, efforts to apprehend the suspected perpetrators ongoing. Further development will be communicated,” he said.

The newspaper reported that the village head and his wife were among those killed. Their bodies were reportedly buried in New Bussa, the headquarters of Borgu LGA.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A resident told the newspaper that the attackers opened fire on worshippers during morning prayers and set the village head’s palace ablaze.

Another source said the attackers also invaded Gada-Oli community at about 2 p.m. while residents were observing afternoon prayers, killing an unspecified number of people.

The newspaper reported that several residents fled their homes following the attacks.

SaharaReporters, quoting a resident, also reported that at least 11 people were killed in Luman Ba’are, including children under five. The source said some victims were burnt and several residents abducted.

According to PREMIUM TIMES’ findings, the attackers in Luman Ba’are targeted members of the Kambari community.

The community had been engaged in a violent conflict with Fulanis following a series of terror attacks attributed to a Boko Haram franchise terrorising the area.

Some locals allege that Fulani collaborators aided the insurgents, a suspicion that has further fuelled tensions (both offline and online) between the communities.

Following Boko Haram attacks on villages like Pisa, Kaduna Daji and Kabe among others, Kambari militias launched a reprisal campaign against Fulanis, forcing many of them to seek refuge in garrison towns such as Wawa, Agwara and neighbouring Kebbi State.

Sources, whose identities have been protected for safety reasons, confirmed to PREMIUM TIMES that armed men killed the village head of Lumma Ba’are and some other residents in the early hours of Saturday and that the assailants also set houses ablaze.

“The village was attacked while heading to the mosque for prayers around 5:00 am,” a community youth leader said, adding the deceased was thrown into a flaming fire.

The community is predominantly Kambari

Reprisal

By late morning, Kambari militias had gathered in their numbers, and launched reprisal attacks on Gada Oli, Wawa, Tunga Ibrahim and other villages where Fulanis were either residing or taking refuge.

In Wawa, a Niger community housing two military bases, the militias, riding on motorcycles, launched targeted attacks on Fulanis, killing them on sight.

“We thought they were terrorists,” said an eyewitness and businessman whose shop premises became a bloody site (two Fulanis killed there).

“They told us not to run,” he continued. “They said they were after the Fulanis.”

The reprisal attacks spread across about four villages, with the assailants spending roughly an hour in Wawa without encountering security personnel, according to eyewitnesses.

The scale of the casualties remains unclear. However, two eyewitnesses said they counted about 20 bodies in Wawa alone.

Footage and images from the attack are too gory for publication.

The violence in Wawa followed the withdrawal of Mobile Police (Mopol) officers from the town.

The Mopol, sources said, were deployed to Wawa about two months ago.

A simmering war

For weeks, PREMIUM TIMES has monitored social media posts and videos which pointed to mounting tensions in parts of the Borgu emirate, with some Fulani residents alleging killings of their kinsmen, while other videos captured individuals identifying as Fulanis threatening reprisals.

Online tensions escalated last week with the alleged killings of some Fulani travelers around Ibbi and Zugurma.

Recent attacks in Niger

The latest killings add to a series of attacks on rural communities in Niger State.

On 15 October, PREMIUM TIMES reported that suspected bandits killed five farmers, abducted 18 people and burnt houses and shops in separate attacks on Fanga community in Mashegu LGA and Kigbere and Kokani communities in Borgu LGA.

The attacks, which occurred between 9 and 12 October, forced residents to flee their homes. A resident told Daily Trust that the armed men had repeatedly imposed levies on Fanga community and attacked it after residents failed to meet their latest demand.

In another incident reported in the same period, residents of Rukukuje community in Rijau LGA fled their homes following reports of armed men moving into the area from neighbouring Zamfara State.

The recurring attacks have heightened concerns about the safety of rural communities, particularly farmers and residents who depend on access to their land and local markets for their livelihoods.

World.title: 2027: We’re not part of opposition coalition against Tinubu  –  Wike-backed PDP
World.content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has said it is not part of the coalition seeking to unite opposition parties behind a single presidential candidate to challenge President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election.

The opposition party said the only coalition arrangement it is committed to is the Rainbow Coalition, promoted by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to support Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid. Mr Wike is a PDP member.

The PDP National Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Mohammed, stated this in a statement on Saturday, distancing the party from the opposition coalition arrangement being promoted under the Coalition for Democracy by Salihu Lukman, a former member of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The Coalition for Democracy emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on 31 August. Its founding members include the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP).

The parties are reportedly exploring the possibility of fielding a single presidential candidate to challenge Mr Tinubu of the ruling APC in 2027.

At that Abuja meeting, representatives of six opposition parties discussed a framework for cooperation. They agreed to establish leadership, publicity and legal committees and five working groups to develop a national covenant for democratic renewal, single four-year transition government, national reform programme, framework for opposition unity and roadmap to a common presidential candidate

The coalition was scheduled to hold its second opposition summit on 23 November but later announced its postponement to 30 November to allow interested opposition parties to conclude their scheduled campaigns.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, Mr Mohammed insisted that the PDP was not part of the coalition and that its members would not attend the summit.

“The PDP wishes to categorically state that it is not part of the said coalition, will not participate in the proposed summit and has not authorised any individual or group to represent or commit the party to the arrangement or any other political engagement of that nature.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the only coalition arrangement to which the PDP has expressed political commitment is the Rainbow Coalition, in accordance with the political direction and directives of our National Leader, His Excellency, Nyesom Wike. No other political coalition arrangement should be attributed to the PDP or presented as its official political position,” he said.

The PDP’s declaration is coming even though it is presenting its own presidential candidate, Sandy Onor, a former senator, in the 2027 election.

PDP threatens legal action

Mr Mohammed said the PDP members who had indicated interest in representing the party at the summit are not legitimate members, claiming that they had been expelled.

He said the coalition would not achieve its objectives if its organisers continued to associate the PDP with individuals who, according to him, are no longer legally recognised as members of the party.

“We wish to make it abundantly clear that this arrangement is dead on arrival, particularly insofar as its promoters seek to associate the PDP through individuals who have no lawful authority to represent the party. Nigerians should not be deceived by what appears to be a political project built on misrepresentation, questionable representation and a lack of sincerity,” he said.

The PDP spokesperson warned the organisers against involving the party in their political activities, threatening legal action if they continued to associate it with the coalition.

“Furthermore, the PDP hereby issues a stern warning to Mr Salihu M. Lukman, his associates and all promoters of this Kangaroo Coalition for Democracy to immediately desist from using the name, identity and institutional authority of the Peoples Democratic Party in furtherance of their political activities. The party will not hesitate to pursue appropriate legal action against any person or group that continues to unlawfully associate the PDP with this arrangement,” he said.

The PDP also urged members of the public, political stakeholders and its supporters to disregard claims that the party was involved in the coalition.

Background to opposition coalition

The latest effort to unite opposition parties ahead of the 2027 general election follows an earlier agreement reached at the National Summit of Opposition Political Parties held in Ibadan, Oyo State, on 25 April.

At the meeting, attended by prominent opposition figures, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi, participants adopted a communiqué known as the Ibadan Declaration.

Among other resolutions, the opposition leaders agreed to resist the ruling APC attempts to establish a one-party state, defend multiparty democracy and work towards presenting a single presidential candidate to challenge President Tinubu in 2027.

They also demanded the removal of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Chairman, Joash Amupitan, over alleged bias, and called on the National Assembly to review provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 that they considered capable of undermining electoral credibility.

However, the proposed opposition alliance subsequently faced setbacks following disagreements among its leading figures and defections from the ADC, which had emerged as a major platform for the opposition realignment.

In May, Mr Obi and Mr Kwankwaso, who were among the prominent figures at the Ibadan summit, left the ADC and joined the NDC, due to internal crises, legal disputes and uncertainty surrounding the party.

Their departure raised fresh questions about the opposition’s ability to agree on a common presidential candidate, particularly amid competing presidential ambitions among its leading politicians.

Meanwhile, disagreements over the legitimacy of party representatives at the Ibadan meeting also prompted the Wike-backed faction of the PDP, some ADC factions, the Labour Party and the Accord Party to distance themselves from the summit and its resolutions.

World.title: Many die in Bayelsa boat mishap, Tinubu orders federal agencies to join rescue effort
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has directed federal disaster response agencies to join rescue operations following a boat accident in Bayelsa State.

Police say four people were killed, but community sources told PREMIUM TIMES that the death toll could be higher.

The accident occurred around 11 a.m. on Friday at the Oweikorogha/Otuan river junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area, involving a passenger boat conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony.

In a statement posted on X on Saturday, the Nigerian Presidency said Mr Tinubu was saddened by the incident and had directed relevant federal agencies to work together to ensure successful rescue and recovery operations.

The president also ordered that the APC presidential campaign rally scheduled for Saturday in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who died.

Police spokesperson in Bayelsa, Musa Mohammed, a deputy superintendent of police, in a statement posted on the Facebook page of the Command said preliminary investigations indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways.

He said some passengers reportedly urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank, but he allegedly refused before the boat capsized.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to the police, four bodies, comprising two adults and two children, had been recovered and deposited at the Federal Medical Centre mortuary in Yenagoa.

Twenty-four survivors were rescued. Nineteen were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five injured passengers were conveyed to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa.

However, community sources told PREMIUM TIMES that more than four people died in the accident, raising questions about the actual casualty figure.

The police said the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, was taken into custody for investigation.

The Commissioner of Police, Ajao Saka Adewale, directed the Marine Police and local divers to intensify search and rescue operations to account for everyone aboard the boat.

Mr Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, Governor Douye Diri and the people of Bayelsa State.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu promises to halve out-of-school children, recruit 20,000 teachers by 2031
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has promised to halve the number of out-of-school children in Nigeria by 2031 as well as recruit and train 20,000 additional teachers, setting measurable targets for a sector still grappling with poor access, inadequate facilities and weak learning outcomes.

The president’s promises are contained in the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s 2027–2031 manifesto, “From Reforms to Prosperity,” which was presented on 10 November in Abuja.

The Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Jumoke Oduwole, who presented an overview of the document on behalf of the president, outlined plans to expand school access, improve retention, strengthen teacher capacity and make learning environments safer.

Under the section titled “We Will Guarantee School Access, Safety, And Educational Retention,” the president says it will “scale HOPE-EDU nationwide to halve the number of out-of-school children by 2031.”

He also promised to extend the Adolescent Girls Initiative for Learning and Empowerment (AGILE), which currently operates in 18 states, to other states with high numbers of girls excluded from education.

He further proposed “dedicated return-to-school pathways for teenage mothers,” recognising the barriers that often prevent young mothers from continuing their education

On teacher recruitment, President Tinubu said he will build on the 80,284 teachers already certified and licensed by recruiting and training another 20,000, with priority given to female educators and underserved rural communities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also pledged to enforce safe-school standards, expand access to water and sanitation facilities and publish an annual education dashboard tracking enrolment, dropout and completion rates.

Nigeria’s out-of-school children

The proposed reduction in out-of-school children comes against the background of a long-standing national education challenge.

A 2024 UNICEF report estimated that 10.2 million primary-school-age children and 8.1 million children of junior secondary school age were out of school in Nigeria.

The federal government has also provided a different estimate. In April 2026, the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, reportedly put the figure at 15 million, while the ministry said nearly one million children had been mapped for reintegration into formal schools and alternative learning pathways.

The different estimates make it necessary for the government to establish a clear baseline for its 2031 target. Although the president promised an annual education dashboard, he did not state the precise number of out-of-school children against which the proposed 50 per cent reduction will be measured.

He did not also provide annual targets showing how many children the government expects to enrol or retain in school each year.

The challenge also extends beyond getting children into classrooms. UNICEF has reported that 74 per cent of Nigerian children aged 7 to 14 lack basic reading and mathematics skills, highlighting the need to assess learning outcomes alongside enrolment figures.

How the new promises compare with the 2023 manifesto

Education was also a major component of Mr Tinubu’s 2023 manifesto, Renewed Hope: Action Plan for a Better Nigeria.

The earlier document promised improvements in school infrastructure, teacher training, curriculum development, digital learning and girls’ access to education. It also proposed stronger accreditation standards, professional development for teachers and improved learning facilities.

Several of those priorities remain in the 2027 document, particularly teacher development, girls’ education, technical training and the use of technology in schools.

The new manifesto, however, attaches specific numerical targets to some commitments. These include halving the number of out-of-school children by 2031 and recruiting and training 20,000 additional teachers.

The 2027 document also promises an annual education dashboard to track enrolment, dropout and completion rates, creating a proposed mechanism for monitoring progress.

What the government says it has achieved

The manifesto presents several figures as evidence of progress under the Tinubu administration.

It reports that 3.7 million girls have been enrolled in secondary schools across 18 states through the AGILE programme, while more than 10,000 schools have been rehabilitated.

The document also says 80,284 teachers have been certified and licensed, about 978,000 teachers have received training and 10,000 classrooms have been renovated nationwide

These are figures reported by the government in the manifesto. They do not, on their own, establish whether the interventions have improved learning outcomes or significantly reduced the number of children excluded from school.

The manifesto acknowledges that the next phase must ensure that children can enrol, learn effectively and complete their education safely.

It states that the immediate priority is “ensuring every child can enrol, learn effectively, and complete their education safely,” supported by more trained teachers, stronger school protection and modern learning environments

Beyond access and retention, the president proposes measures to improve the quality and relevance of education, particularly in science, technology, engineering, mathematics and digital learning.

The manifesto says the government will “prioritise foundational learning, science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and digital capabilities across all educational levels.”

It also promises stronger partnerships with industries to provide practical, work-linked training and align courses with labour-market needs.

On technical and vocational education, the president proposes expanding training programmes, building on the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) initiative. The manifesto reports that the initiative has enrolled 117,152 verified trainees, while monthly stipends increased from ₦22,500 to ₦30,000

He says the success of these programmes will be assessed through graduate employment, business survival and workplace productivity.

At the tertiary level, the manifesto promises to scale the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), expand the National Smart Learning Initiative and extend the Student Venture Capital Grant and Diaspora BRIDGE to more institutions [p. 42].

The document reports that NELFUND had processed 1,659,853 applications and paid ₦355.87 billion in student loans. Of the amount, ₦192.89 billion went towards institutional fees for students in 319 institutions, while ₦162.98 billion was paid as upkeep allowances [pp. 37–38].

It also says the Renewed Hope Energising Education Programme has provided electricity to 37 federal universities and seven teaching hospitals.

However, the manifesto leaves unanswered how the government intends to address the financial and social pressures that keep children out of school, particularly in communities where poverty, distance to schools and other barriers affect attendance.

The annual education dashboard could provide a basis for public scrutiny, but its usefulness will depend on whether it publishes verifiable, state-level data and tracks actual learning outcomes.

For a country still struggling to get millions of children into classrooms, the success of the proposed education plan will depend on whether the commitments translate into sustained enrolment, improved teaching and better learning outcomes.

World.title: Three killed, 13 injured in attack on Gombe community
World.content:
Residents have demanded justice after an attack on Friday night, allegedly by personnel of the Nigerian Air Force (NAF), left three people dead and 13 others injured in Lawanti community in Akko Local Government Area of Gombe State.

The community accused personnel attached to the Air Force’s 109 Combat Reconnaissance Group (109 CRG) in Gombe of shooting and beating residents during a confrontation over suspected theft of armoured cables.

Speaking to journalists on behalf of the community, the Programme Officer of Lawanti Foundation, Idris Maigari Lawanti, called on the federal and state governments to identify and prosecute those involved for the attack.

“Our families deserve to know what happened, who gave the orders and who carried them out,” Mr Lawanti said.

He said no allegation of criminal wrongdoing could justify the use of excessive force against civilians.

“We call on the Gombe State Government and the Federal Government to ensure a prompt, independent investigation into allegations that personnel of the Nigerian Air Force’s 109 Combat Reconnaissance Group were involved,” he said.

Mr Lawanti named the three deceased residents as Yayaji Alhaji Abdul Kura, Hamma Magaji, and Inna Anttu Umar Bello.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said Mr Kura was received in the hospital dead after sustaining gunshot wounds, while Mr Magaji allegedly died following a beating.

According to the community, Mr Bello died during the incident due to what residents attributed to shock.

The exact medical causes of the deaths have yet to be established.

Mr Lawanti said 13 residents sustained injuries, with 12 taken to the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe, for treatment.

He named Sale Abubakar, 30, as one of the injured persons, saying he was taken to the operating theatre for emergency surgery.

Another victim, Paul Simple, was reportedly taken to the Cottage Hospital in Amada after allegedly being beaten.

The community called on the Gombe State Government to settle the medical bills of the injured and provide financial and other assistance to the families of those who died.

“Lawanti is a peaceful community. If any resident is accused of wrongdoing, that person is entitled to answer the allegation before a court,” he said.

“An accusation against an individual can never justify opening fire on residents or beating anyone as punishment.”

The community demanded that investigators obtain evidence from survivors, eyewitnesses, hospital officials and relatives of the deceased.

It also insisted that the findings of the investigation should be made public.

“Where the evidence establishes wrongdoing, those responsible must face the full consequences of the law,” Mr Lawanti said.

He appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid taking the law into their own hands.

“We appeal to our people to remain calm and to continue looking after one another as we seek justice,” he said.

Meanwhile, Governor Yahaya has condemned the incident and ordered an investigation.

In a statement issued on Saturday by his Director-General of Press Affairs, Ismaila Uba Misilli, the governor described the incident as deeply distressing.

The government acknowledged preliminary reports of three deaths and 13 injuries, with some victims receiving treatment at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe.

Governor Yahaya directed a delegation led by the Secretary to the State Government, Ibrahim Njodi, to visit Lawanti, meet affected families and assess the situation.

He also ordered an investigation to determine the circumstances of the incident and ensure appropriate action under the law.

The governor assured residents that his administration would work with relevant security agencies to address the matter.

He also promised government support for the injured and bereaved families, while appealing to residents to avoid reprisals or actions that could escalate tensions.

Efforts to obtain the Nigerian Air Force’s reaction to the allegations were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

Repeated telephone calls to officials of the 109 Combat Reconnaissance Group in Gombe and the Nigerian Air Force Headquarters in Abuja, including attempts to reach the unit commander and the Force’s spokesperson, went unanswered.

Consequently, the military’s account of the confrontation and its response to the allegations against its personnel could not be obtained.

Another resident, Musa Haruna, said the community wanted more than expressions of sympathy, stressing that the circumstances surrounding the deaths must be established and those found culpable held accountable.

He urged the authorities to make the investigation’s findings public and ensure that affected families receive appropriate assistance.

World.title: Fountain of Life Crisis: Jimmy Odukoya sues sister, trustees over removal
World.content:
Jimmy Odukoya has reportedly sued his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and members of the Fountain of Life Church’s board of trustees over the dispute surrounding his removal as the church’s senior pastor.

The suit, filed at the Federal High Court in Lagos and marked FHC/LAG/CS/1568/2026, seeks to invalidate the decisions through which a group of trustees withdrew its recognition of Mr Odukoya as the church’s spiritual leader.

Leadership newspaper reported the development on Saturday.

The Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church and Mr Odukoya are listed as the first and second claimants.

Tolu Odukoya, Biodun Balogun, Biodun Awosika, Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo were named as respondents.

Rival court action

The federal court action is the latest development in the church’s escalating leadership dispute.

It came days after the trustees opposing Mr Odukoya’s leadership announced that the Lagos State High Court had restrained him from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The trustees said the court also barred him from interfering with the church’s governance, administration and activities.

Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin issued the orders in suit number LD/0126PRA/2026, instituted in the name of the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church against Mr Odukoya.

In their application, the trustees argued that Mr Odukoya had ceased to occupy the position because the church’s late founder, Taiwo Odukoya, had designated another successor under its constitution.

They also asked the court to prevent him from disrupting the church’s administration while they complied with the Lagos State High Court’s pre-action requirements.

The court granted the applicants permission to commence the action under the pre-action protocol and directed that Mr Odukoya be served with the originating processes and accompanying documents.

Succession dispute

The crisis became public after the group of trustees announced Mr Odukoya’s removal and named Rotimi Okpaise as the church’s interim spiritual and administrative leader.

The group subsequently released a video purportedly recorded by Taiwo Odukoya in December 2021. In the recording, the late founder was heard naming Adekunle Areogun as his preferred successor and assigning Mr Odukoya an administrative role, along with responsibility for the youth church.

Mr Odukoya and those supporting his leadership rejected the announcement, maintaining that his appointment as senior pastor in September 2023 was unanimously approved and remained constitutionally valid.

The competing lawsuits have now moved the battle over the church’s leadership from public statements and social media into the courts.

World.title: Soldiers die in Yobe road accident
World.content:
By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman

Several soldiers are feared dead, while others sustained injuries in a road accident involving a military vehicle at Garin Malam Adamu, near Buni Yadi, headquarters of Gujba Local Government Area of Yobe State.

The accident reportedly occurred on Friday, November 20, while the soldiers were travelling from Buni Yadi to Damaturu, the state capital.

The victims were reportedly evacuated to the Yobe State University Teaching Hospital, Damaturu, for medical attention.

Although the exact casualty figure remains unknown, preliminary accounts have linked the accident to the poor condition of a section of the road.

At the time of filing this report, military authorities had yet to officially confirm the incident or disclose the number of casualties.

Vanguard News

World.title: Tinubu doing fantastic job on sports infrastructure, says Infantino
World.content:
FIFA President, Gianni Infantino

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for its investment in sports infrastructure, describing its efforts as a “fantastic job” and an indication of Nigeria’s commitment to the future of its young population.

Infantino gave the commendation on Saturday while addressing the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in Abuja.

The FIFA president urged members of the Nigerian delegation to convey his regards to Tinubu, while acknowledging the contributions of the President and other Nigerian leaders to sports development.

“On behalf of President Tinubu, please send him our warmest regards. He is doing together with all of you. Fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” Infantino said.

He particularly praised investments in sports facilities, noting that they reflected confidence in the potential of young Nigerians.

“We were discussing this yesterday as well, also with the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, my brother Shehu. The investments done in sports facilities infrastructure show that you believe in your youth, in the young girls and the young boys of Nigeria,” he said.

“Thank you for that. Congratulations for that,” he added.

Infantino also thanked Nigeria for hosting him and his delegation, which included FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, describing the visit as an opportunity to reconnect with the continent.

“Thanks for welcoming me and our delegation with the Secretary-General and the others here at home in Africa, in Abuja. Thank you for your support. It means the world to me,” he said.

His remarks followed an inspection of sports infrastructure projects in Nigeria on Friday, including the remodelled Warri City Stadium and the Hussey College mini-stadium and sports complex in Delta State.

He also visited the ongoing FIFA Forward Technical Centre project at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja, describing the facility as an investment in the future of Nigerian football.

“This is a collaboration between Nigerian football and FIFA for the future of the girls and the boys of Nigeria,” he said.

During his visit to the Warri City Stadium, Infantino stressed the importance of developing grassroots sports facilities to ensure that football remained accessible to people across communities.

“That’s what football is about. It’s for everyone, everywhere. It’s the big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also the smaller stadiums, it’s the proximity,” he said.

The FIFA president also expressed appreciation for the reception he received in Nigeria, assuring the country of the world football governing body’s continued support.

“I feel so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. I am very happy to be here. You can always count on FIFA. We are not just your partners; we are your family members,” he added.

Infantino’s visit also coincided with Nigeria’s endorsement of his bid for another term as FIFA president.

The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, announced Nigeria’s support for Infantino’s re-election bid on behalf of President Tinubu during the CAF assembly.

World.title: Odukoya drags sister, others to court over removal as senior pastor
World.content:
The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has dragged his sister and others before a Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his purported removal from office and the decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees.

Odukoya, alongside the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, instituted the action against eight defendants, including Pastor Tolu Odukoya, Mr Biodun Balogun, Mr Biodun Awosika, Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, Pastor Tobi Enuha, Pastor Gbenga Onabanjo, Pastor Fred Ohiani and Pastor Akin Osinbajo.

This is coming some days after a Lagos State High Court had restrained him from parading as the senior pastor in the church.

Odukoya in an affidavit in support of the applications is asking the court to determine whether meetings held by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions taken at those meetings complied with the church’s constitution.

Odukoya said he was appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees at an emergency meeting of the board on September 14, 2023, and was subsequently installed in September of the same year.

He said the church and its organs were governed by its constitution, amended by a special resolution dated January 16, 2003, and that the defendants were members of its Board of Trustees.

According to his affidavit, the disagreement began after a December 19, 2025, meeting of the board, attended by Bishop Mike Okonkwo, at which the possibility of handing over the church’s administrative arm to the Associate Senior Pastor was discussed.

He said no resolution or final decision was reached at the meeting.

Board meeting

Odukoya said he subsequently convened a board meeting for January 5, 2026, but it could not hold because there was no quorum. He added that some trustees later presented proposals to him, many of which he declined because, according to him, they were inconsistent with the church’s constitution.

He said the trustees subsequently sent him a letter dated January 7, 2026, requesting a response within three days, but he did not see it until after the deadline had elapsed.

Odukoya said he later directed the board secretary to schedule a meeting for January 30, 2026, after a request for a special meeting was made by a board member.

However, he alleged that a separate notice for a meeting on January 22 was circulated by the fourth defendant and did not come from the board secretariat.

“I received the notice late in the evening of January 20, 2026, effectively giving me one day notice of the purported meeting,” he stated.

He said he declined to attend the meeting, but the defendants proceeded with it under the name of “concerned members of the Board”.

According to him, they “purportedly adopted a number of resolutions” which included separating the offices of Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, suspending the board secretary and a church pastor, dissolving the church’s Executive Council and amending its constitution.

Odukoya said a series of conciliatory meetings followed but produced no meaningful result. He added that another meeting was held on February 9, 2026, where he reiterated his position on the disagreement.

He said he was subsequently invited to a meeting with Bishop Okonkwo and, following an understanding reached there, wrote to the concerned members of the board on February 13. The trustees replied on February 15, while he responded on February 20.

At the February 28 meeting, Odukoya alleged that some individuals convened a gathering which was neither a board meeting nor a meeting of the church council.

“Nonetheless, a vote was taken among those present, and I was purportedly removed as the Chairman of the Board,” he stated.

He said he responded to the purported removal in a letter dated March 2, 2026, addressed to the concerned trustees.

Meetings

The pastor further alleged that the defendants caused an individual describing herself as an interim secretary to issue notices for board meetings, despite what he said was the failure to validly remove the substantive secretary in accordance with the church’s constitution.

Odukoya said the defendants later issued a notice for another board meeting scheduled for November 16, 2026, which he said was served on November 14.

He said he objected to what he described as the continued disregard for the church’s constitution in a letter dated November 15, but the meeting went ahead.

“The Defendants upon their meeting on November 16, 2026, wrote to me the letter dated November 17, 2026, which purports to remove me as the Senior Pastor and Chairman, Board of Trustees, upon some bogus facts,” he stated.

He maintained that the three disputed meetings and the decisions taken at them violated the church’s constitution.

“I know, by my knowledge of the provisions of the 1st Plaintiff’s Constitution, that the meetings on 22nd January, 2026, 28th February, 2026 and 16th November, 2026 held by the Defendants either amongst themselves or with other persons in attendance and all the decisions and resolutions emanating therefrom are in contravention of the constitution of the 1st Defendant,” he said.

In his application for urgent intervention, Odukoya also alleged that the defendants had plans to disrupt church meetings to prevent him from carrying out his duties.

“Despite their disregard for the constitution of the 1st Plaintiff, the Defendants have perfected the plan to violently disrupt any meeting of the 1st Plaintiff with a view to violently prevent me from performing my duties as the Senior Pastor of the church,” he stated.

He further alleged that the defendants were influential and had the capacity to use law enforcement agents to enforce what he described as illegal resolutions.

Odukoya said he feared that the dispute could disrupt church activities and lead to a breach of peace if the defendants were not restrained.

“Unless the Defendants are urgently restrained by an order of this Honourable Court, the Defendants will continue with their nefarious activities, wreaking havoc on the activities of the church which may lead to counter reactions by those opposed to them and which may result in a breach of peace,” he stated.

Explaining why he considered the matter urgent, he described himself as a public figure and an inspiration to young people.

“I am a clergy, a public figure and an inspiration to many young persons all over the world; a single public embarrassment and scandalous encounter would have irreparable effect on my personality, and this would definitely negatively affect those persons, especially the young ones, who, by the grace of God, look to me for guidance,” he said.

The court

The pastor is asking the court to restrain the defendants from interfering with his functions and the management of the church’s affairs pending the determination of the dispute.

The court had yet to make a determination on the issues raised in the processes as of the time of filing this report.

The dispute became public on November 17, when some members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced Jimmy’s removal, citing a December 2021 video in which the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, reportedly named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor and assigned Jimmy an administrative support role and leadership of the youth ministry.

The trustees also raised objections to Jimmy’s remarriage.

However, Jimmy and the church rejected the removal, insisting that his appointment in September 2023 was valid and that the decision violated the church’s constitution.

The trustees later named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise interim spiritual and administrative leader.

World.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy death toll rises to 26
World.content:
… Governor Diri, deputy visit scene

By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa

The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has climbed to 26, with rescue and recovery operations continuing into Sunday as grieving families besiege the Ayama waterfront.

Governor Douye Diri and his deputy visited the accident scene on Saturday to assess ongoing recovery efforts.

The ill-fated wooden passenger boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when it capsized around 11 a.m. between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities waterway.

The overcrowded vessel reportedly developed a mechanical fault mid-journey before going down.

The Bayelsa State Police Command initially confirmed four bodies recovered and 24 survivors rescued on Friday. By Saturday night, local divers and marine police had recovered 22 additional bodies, bringing the total to 26.

A source close to the Southern Ijaw council chairman, speaking anonymously, confirmed the updated toll and said search operations would resume Sunday.

“It’s so unfortunate. This tragedy would have been averted if commuters and boat operators had heeded our advice,” the source said. “We have repeatedly warned them to provide life vests for passengers, but these were not provided. The boat itself was very old and no longer seaworthy.”

The council plans to enforce an order ensuring anyone violating safety laws is apprehended and prosecuted.

An indigene of Ukubie said divers had set nets along the Oporoma waterways to trap bodies that may have floated away.

He revealed that seven of his relatives were aboard, with three bodies among those recovered Saturday.

Nineteen survivors were treated at Ayama Clinic, while five injured passengers were transferred to a hospital in Yenagoa. The vessel’s manager was taken into custody for investigation, while the operator reportedly fled.

The Bayelsa State government warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation, speeding, travelling without life jackets, night journeys and operating in unfavourable weather.

Commissioner for Information, Orientation and Strategy Ebiuwou Koku-Obiyai said the government is supporting search-and-rescue operations and will assist emergency responders until the exercise concludes.

The tragedy has renewed concerns about safety enforcement on Bayelsa’s waterways, with community leaders calling for stricter scrutiny of vessel seaworthiness and mandatory life vest compliance.

World.title: Arsenal held by Newcastle rally and lose Raya to injury
World.content:
Newcastle United’s German defender #12 Malick Thiaw has his shorts pulled by Arsenal’s German midfielder #29 Kai Havertz during the English Premier League football match between Newcastle United and Arsenal at St James’ Park in Newcastle-upon-Tyne, north east England on November 21, 2026. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /





Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday.

The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes.

But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle.

Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points.

However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise.

Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions.

Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James’ Park.

Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title.

Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on.

Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August.

The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener.

It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek.

Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break.

Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so.

Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level.

Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks.

Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya.

That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell.

But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title.

Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek.

World.title: Tinubu: No student will be denied university education over poverty
World.content:
Urges graduates to be creative, enterprising

By Dayo Johnson, Akure

President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians that no student will be denied access to tertiary education because of financial constraints.

The President gave the assurance at the 37th convocation ceremony of the Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA), where he said the establishment of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) was a deliberate step towards removing financial barriers to higher education.

Tinubu, who was represented by Prof. Olatunde Peter Ajagbonna of the National Universities Commission (NUC), Abuja, said NELFUND provides financial support, including upkeep allowances, to eligible students in public tertiary institutions.

He pledged that his administration would continue to strengthen the scheme to guarantee equitable access to university education.

“My administration is equally committed to ensuring uninterrupted academic calendars and timely completion of academic programmes,” Tinubu said.

He disclosed that the Federal Government had prioritised the welfare of staff in public tertiary institutions, leading to the conclusion and signing of agreements with various staff unions, with financial backing already provided for their implementation.

“I believe that sustained dialogue and mutual understanding are essential to industrial harmony and stability in our institutions.

“I therefore urge all staff of our tertiary institutions to reciprocate the government’s commitment through dedication, professionalism and diligence,” he said.

The President charged lecturers, researchers and other university workers to remain focused on imparting relevant knowledge, practical skills and sound values to students to produce competent, innovative and responsible graduates capable of thriving in a rapidly changing world.

He said Nigeria was blessed with enormous human and natural resources, adding that universities must take the lead in harnessing them.

“I expect institutions such as FUTA to strengthen research, develop home-grown technologies and promote productive partnerships with industry.

“These efforts are essential to economic diversification, technological advancement and the emergence of a knowledge-driven economy,” Tinubu said.

Addressing the graduating students, the President urged them to take advantage of opportunities emerging from the ongoing transformation of the economy.

“Be creative, adaptable and enterprising. Do not allow present challenges to limit your aspirations.

“Rather, use your knowledge and skills to create opportunities, generate wealth and contribute to building a stronger and more prosperous Nigeria,” he said.

Tinubu also called on Nigerians at home and in the Diaspora, the private sector and development partners to support national development, stressing that building a prosperous and globally competitive Nigeria required the commitment, cooperation and sacrifice of all stakeholders.

“Let us work together in the overriding interest of our country and future generations,” he added.

In her address, the Vice-Chancellor of FUTA, Prof. Adenike Oladiji, commended the Federal Government for its interventions in the institution, saying they had significantly improved teaching, learning, research and administrative capacity.

According to her, the interventions had upgraded critical infrastructure, enhanced the quality and functionality of academic facilities, expanded opportunities for practical training and research, strengthened institutional capacity and reinforced the university’s ability to fulfil its mandate as a leading centre of technological education, research and innovation in Nigeria.

Oladiji disclosed that almost all academic programmes in the university had secured full accreditation from the NUC.

“This strong regulatory validation underscores our commitment to institutional quality, providing the bedrock upon which our specialised research hubs thrive. Chief among these is the prestigious Centre of Excellence in Food Security, proudly domiciled within our School of Agriculture and Agricultural Technology (SAAT),” she said.

She said the university’s Teaching and Research Farm had institutionalised progressive models in agribusiness, sustainable land use and practical training.

“We have successfully scaled our core oil-palm operations from an initial 18 acres to 61 acres of thriving plantation, establishing a resilient resource that currently hosts over 1,200 productive trees plus another 1,000 newly established trees,” she said.

Oladiji added that the university launched an agricultural diversification programme in August, establishing advanced greenhouses for high-yield tomato and bell pepper production.

“Simultaneously, we planted over 500 improved prolific oil-palm seedlings and 500 Malayan dwarf coconut seedlings, closely followed by the development of brand-new cocoa and cassava plantations to secure a long-term research and production base,” she said.

Also speaking, the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Dr. Olugbenga Akande Awe, commended the Tinubu administration for its attention to the development of tertiary education in Nigeria.

“The advancement of universities is fundamental to the nation’s aspirations for technological innovation, economic diversification and sustainable development.

“We are grateful for the courtesies extended to FUTA and for the approval of your representation at this important academic gathering,” Awe said.

He said the Governing Council recognised the importance of the Federal Government’s role in strengthening public universities through policy direction, institutional support and investment in critical infrastructure.

“We assure Your Excellency of our commitment to responsible governance and to supporting initiatives that advance the objectives of your Renewed Hope Agenda, particularly in education, research, innovation and human capital development.

“We therefore remain steadfast in our commitment to sustaining the confidence reposed in FUTA through the production of competent graduates, advancing research and contributing practical solutions to the challenges confronting our nation,” he said.

World.title: Best Apps to Download News and Current-Affairs Clips Offline in 2026
World.content:
News video is worth saving for two reasons: to catch up on your own time, and to keep a copy of something that might get edited or pulled later. Both reward speed — a clip you grab now is one you still have when the feed has moved on, the correction has gone up, or the original quietly disappears. With current affairs, the window to keep a copy is often measured in hours, not days.

Snaptube goes first for pace: it resolves in seconds, and it hands you the clip as video or as audio depending on how you’d rather follow the story. Android users get it from the official site as the Snaptube APK download application. Five more sit below, each suited to a different way of keeping current affairs offline.

1. Snaptube

The same report can be two things, and that is the first reason to start here. Keep the news clip as video when you want to see it, or pull it as audio when you only want to hear it — and with current affairs, listening while you commute is often the faster way to stay on top of the day than sitting and watching. Snaptube takes either from the same post, so you need only one video download app for both habits — a bulletin can be a file you keep for the record or a track you play on the way to work, your choice at the moment you save.

Coverage is the next piece, because the same news gets posted by different outlets in different places. Snaptube reaches well over a hundred platforms, so if you want to line up how two or three sources framed the same story, one app pulls all of their news clips rather than sending you to a separate tool for each outlet’s channel. Following a story across who reported it stops meaning a drawer of downloaders.

Speed is the part that actually matters with news. A hot clip can be edited or taken down within the day, so the window to keep a copy is short — Snaptube‘s resolving happens on its servers and returns in seconds, so you paste and have the file before the story shifts, where a slower web tool might leave you watching it disappear mid-load. To do it: paste the link or search inside the app, pick a quality or switch to audio, and save. A one-off install from the official site or the store your phone came with, and it’s ready.

2. VidMate

VidMate sets a search box beside a discovery feed, so you can track a running story and save clips as they appear, across a wide set of sources at up to 1080p. For keeping up with current affairs on the phone, that scroll-and-save flow fits the pace.

Pick it when browsing the news and grabbing clips in one app suits you — the feed keeps a running story in front of you and the save is one tap away as each new angle appears. The trade-offs stay the same — a free build thick with ads, and a download that comes straight from the developer instead of any store, so inspect the web address carefully before installing, since this is a much-imitated name.

3. SaveFrom.net

SaveFrom.net is a long-running web tool that saves from a broad spread of sites with nothing to install, which suits a quick desktop grab — a news clip you want kept while you’re reading at a computer, no app added to the machine.

Use it for the occasional one-off on a laptop. Two things hold it back for regular use: the page is heavy with pop-ups and redirect ads, and it changes web address often and is blocked in some places, so confirm you’re on the genuine site and read each button before you click, rather than trusting the first result you land on.

4. Videoder

Videoder covers many sites with batch downloading, so you can queue several related reports and pull them together — handy when a single story has spawned a dozen clips worth keeping side by side. A range of quality steps lets you decide how much space each takes.

Weigh its upkeep: it carries a no-longer-maintained flag, and a report’s source can quietly stop resolving as the site changes, with no fix coming. Test it on the outlets you actually follow before you count on it for a breaking story, and keep a backup tool in reach for the ones it can’t reach.

5. HD Video Downloader

An Android app with a built-in browser that sniffs out video, background and large-file support, and the option to save straight to an SD card — useful for stacking a lot of news clips somewhere other than crowded phone storage.

Consider it when you’re archiving a run of clips and want them on a card rather than filling phone storage with a growing pile of reports. Be clear on its weak spots, though: the ratings run low, ads cover the screen more than you’d like, and some saves come down without sound — a real problem for news, where the audio often carries the substance — so check an important clip plays back in full before you trust it with anything you can’t re-grab.

6. Hitube

Hitube can be used on the web or as an Android app, with no account asked, and it saves social clips at up to 1080p, picking a dropped transfer back up on the app. Since much current-affairs video circulates as social reposts, it covers that case with nothing to install.

Use it to catch a news clip straight from a feed in seconds, nothing installed. The catch is that it’s a recent tool with little independent track record, so its long-run reliability is unproven — reasonable for a quick social grab, less so for archiving a story you need to keep, which a fuller downloader does more dependably.

Which One Fits the News

For time-sensitive clips, lead with the fastest resolver so a copy is yours before the story changes or the original is edited; for comparing how outlets covered it, the widest platform reach saves the most app-switching when the same news is scattered across their separate channels. The slower web tools have their place for a one-off on a computer, but speed and reach are what a running story actually asks for.

And when you only want to follow along rather than watch, pulling the audio turns a stack of bulletins into something you catch up on during a commute — one save, played whichever way the day allows, read in full when you’ve time or heard in passing when you don’t.

World.title: 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has described the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s decision to postpone the clean-up of the national voters’ register until after the 2027 general elections as a major failure.

The party said INEC had four years to prepare for the exercise.

However, ADC said the voters’ register is only one of several issues that will determine the credibility of the 2027 elections. They pointed to electronic transmission of results, result collation and compliance with the Electoral Act as other major areas of concern.

Speaking to Vanguard, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said INEC’s failure to clean up the register raised questions about its commitment to conducting credible elections.

“This shouldn’t have happened. INEC had four years to prepare and plan for this, and its failure to do so does not suggest that it is taking its responsibilities seriously, particularly the issue of maintaining a credible voters’ register,” he said.

Abdullahi, however, said the party would not make the outcome of the 2027 elections depend solely on whether INEC produced a credible voters’ register, noting that previous elections had been conducted despite imperfections in the register.

“We do not believe that the credibility of the 2027 general election rests solely on INEC’s ability to produce a credible voters’ register. It would have given everyone greater confidence if the commission had been able to do so, but we are not going to hinge the fate of the 2027 election on that single issue.”

He said the ADC was also concerned about how INEC would implement the Electoral Act, particularly the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation process and the duties of electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E.

“There are other, more pertinent issues of concern to our party. These include compliance with the Electoral Act, the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation of results and the additional responsibilities assigned to electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E.”

On the possible effect of the voters’ register on the elections, Abdullahi argued that strict compliance with the law, particularly provisions on voter accreditation, could reduce the impact of its shortcomings.

“If INEC complies with the Electoral Act, particularly regarding voter accreditation, the shortcomings in the voters’ register may not have as much impact. Problems arise when the commission fails to abide by its own rules and the provisions of the Electoral Act,” he said.

He said the ADC was studying possible weaknesses in the electoral process and making arrangements to ensure that its votes were protected.

“We know where the loopholes are, and that is why we continue to focus on them and ensure that we make adequate arrangements to protect our votes.”
