World.title: Plateau Courts Global Investors at Three Major African Summits
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Yemi Kosoko in Jos

Plateau State has intensified efforts to attract local and foreign investments, showcasing its opportunities in the creative economy, agriculture, mining, tourism and renewable energy at three major continental investment gatherings in Lagos, Abuja and Calabar.

The state participated in the Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026), the International Investors Summit Nigeria and the 6th African Sub-Sovereign Governments Network (AfSNET) Investment Conference, using the platforms to market its investment potential to global financiers and business leaders.

At CANEX in Lagos, Plateau showcased its indigenous leather products, fashion, visual arts and highland coffee, while local creatives engaged international buyers and investors. The event came as Afreximbank expanded its support for Africa’s creative economy to $2 billion through 2027.

In Abuja, the state presented a portfolio of investment-ready projects in agriculture, mineral processing, renewable energy and tourism. Officials highlighted opportunities in the Irish potato value chain, dairy production, lithium, tin and columbite beneficiation, as well as tourism assets such as Jos Wildlife Park, Pandam Game Reserve and Wase Rock.

The investment drive continued in Calabar at the AfSNET Conference, where Afreximbank unveiled a $2 billion financing facility for state and local governments to accelerate infrastructure and development projects.

Commissioner for Commerce and Industry, Musa Ibrahim Ashoms, said the three-pronged engagement was part of Plateau’s strategy to convert its vast potential into bankable investments.

“At CANEX, we showed that our culture is capital. In Abuja, we demonstrated that our projects can attract global investment. In Calabar, we reinforced the role of sub-national governments as drivers of AfCFTA opportunities,” he said.

Ashoms noted that ongoing infrastructure renewal, peace-building efforts and recent agreements with Chinese investors for an industrial park were strengthening investor confidence in the state.

The government said it remains committed to transforming Plateau into a major industrial processing hub and called on investors, development partners and the diaspora to partner in driving economic growth, job creation and shared prosperity.

World.title: REC Appeals for Participation as INEC Holds Mock Voter Accreditation in 598 Delta’s Polling Units
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Delta State, Sir Etekamba Udo Umoren, has appealed to citizens and the electorate in the state to actively participate in the commission’s mock Bimodal Voter Accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, 2026.

Umoren said that the test of Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC’s) Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and result upload processes would be conducted in 598 polling units selected across the 25 local government areas of the state on November 28 to enable INEC identify areas of possible technical challenges as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections.

Briefing journalists yesterday in Asaba, the Delta REC assured that the exercise would enable the Commission determine the configuration accuracy of the electoral equipment and systems preparatorily to the 2027 election, noting the selection of the units was to ensure good geographical scope.

The REC said, “The Mock Accreditation and Result Upload will be conducted across the 25 local government areas of Delta State on 28th November, 2026. The polling units will open by 7.30amand Accreditation will commence at 8am and close at 2 30pm.

“The commission is using 598 Polling Units across the 25 LGAs, two units per Registration Area (ward) in Delta State will be selected and utilised for the exercise.

“We have 25 local government areas in the state and 299 registration areas, otherwise called wards. If you multiply 299 by two, it gives you 598 polling units. That is how we arrived at the 598 polling units.

“The exercise will provide an opportunity to test the functionality and reliability of technologies and equipment, particularly the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS).

“It will also access the effectiveness of the accreditation, voting, result recording, transmission, and other relevant Election-Day processes, as applicable to the exercise.”

Moreover, the Mock Accreditation and Result Upload exercise would help INEC determine the preparedness of its personnel, including the “neutrality” of its regular and ad-hoc staff, in terms of understanding of polling procedures, proper handling of election materials, accreditation, voting, sorting, counting as well as result management, he stressed.

On logistical arrangements, Umoren said that the exercise will also test the commission’s preparedness for “timely deployment of personnel, election materials, equipment and other resources to designated polling units.”

He also responded to questions on INEC’s real time electronic transmission of election results from polling units to the INEC Result Viewing Portal and the commission’s preparedness to ensure hitch-free upload of polling results that accurately reflected the action of the electorate in the election proper.

Umoren said, “It is for us to look at whether we have properly set or configured the system to work the way they should. If there is any technical issue, that will be corrected.

“These are the likely situations we want to identify. The exercise will give us a clear picture, and then we will know whether we have properly configured the system and whether it is ready for the election.”

“It is important to emphasise that the mock accreditation is not the actual election and will not involve the declaration of winners and losers,” noted the Delta State REC, who was flanked by the Administrative Secretary, Davis O. Eldred, and other management staff the commission in the state.

Umoren also appealed to stakeholders, including registered political parties, security agencies, civil society organisations as well as community leaders and the media to collaborate with the INEC to ensure that eligible voters participate and that the exercise is peaceful and successful.

World.title: Alausa: TVET Starter Kits Empower Graduates for Job Creation
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 





Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Minister of Education, Dr. Maruf Tunji Alausa, has reaffirmed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s commitment to youth empowerment, skills development and economic self-reliance.

Alausa spoke at the Graduation and Starter Kit Handover Ceremony of the Federal Government’s Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Initiative, held at the Federal Technical College, Yaba, Lagos, yesterday.

The Lagos exercise is part of the phased nationwide distribution of starter kits, with 7,000 beneficiaries expected to benefit in the state.

The initiative is designed to bridge the gap between skills acquisition and economic opportunity by equipping trained youths with tools to establish businesses, pursue self-employment, secure jobs and contribute to national productivity under the Renewed Hope Agenda.

Speaking at the ceremony, Alausa stressed that vocational training must translate into tangible economic outcomes, noting that access to tools is essential for graduates to turn skills into viable livelihoods.

He said the starter kits would help beneficiaries transition from training to productive enterprise, enabling them to provide services, earn incomes, build businesses and create employment for others.

The minister disclosed that 87,701 trainees had successfully completed the first cohort nationwide across trades including welding and fabrication, electrical installation, automobile mechanics, solar photovoltaic installation, fashion design, hospitality, ICT, agriculture, leatherwork and beauty therapy, among others.

He also announced that 1.49 million applications were received for the second cohort, with 150,000 learners admitted into accredited training centres across the country.

Dr. Alausa clarified that starter-kit distribution is being undertaken in phases, subject to assessment, verification and documentation, to ensure transparency and accountability. He noted that training completion, certification and eligibility for starter-kit support are distinct stages.

Beneficiaries in certain agricultural and livestock-related trades, where conventional starter kits may not be readily available, would receive monetary support to establish their ventures.

Addressing the graduates, the minister urged them to use their equipment responsibly, uphold professional standards, observe safety requirements, honour commitments to customers and continually improve their competencies. He encouraged them to grow their businesses into sustainable enterprises capable of employing others.

In her opening remarks, the Director overseeing the Office of the Permanent Secretary, Dr. (Mrs.) Folake Olatunji-David, represented by the Director of Technology and Science Education, Mrs. P.O. Ogungbemi, described the ceremony as a significant milestone in repositioning TVET as a driver of skills development, youth empowerment, entrepreneurship and national economic growth.

She commended the leadership of the Minister and the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Said Ahmad, for prioritising TVET under the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI) and the Renewed Hope Agenda.

She urged the graduates to embrace innovation, uphold professionalism and maximise the opportunities provided.

Feyisayo Onafowokan, a leatherwork and shoemaking trainee, described the initiative as life-changing. Recounting her struggles as a single mother in search of employment, she explained how she learnt about the programme through someone who assisted her with registration. She expressed gratitude to President Tinubu, the Minister, the Civic Initiative and her instructors.

Similarly, Mr. Femi White of Femi White Welding and Fabrication commended the Federal Government, describing the initiative as timely and impactful. He emphasised the value of vocational skills in building livelihoods, achieving independence and contributing to economic development, while calling for sustained investment in technical education.

The Minister commended the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE), the National Business and Technical Examinations Board (NABTEB), the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), training centres, instructors, assessors, quality assurance personnel, development partners including GIZ and UNESCO, and other implementation teams.

He also called on state governments, community leaders and private-sector partners to support graduates through mentorship, recruitment opportunities and enterprise development.

Alausa reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to strengthening TVET through quality training, competency-based assessment, recognised certification, industry partnerships, entrepreneurship support and employment tracking. He stressed that success would be measured by graduates securing employment, establishing sustainable businesses, improving earnings and creating opportunities for others.

World.title: NDCCITMA Unveils New Push for Niger Delta Industrial Growth
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The Niger Delta Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Trade, Mines and Agriculture (NDCCITMA) has pledged to intensify efforts to promote industrialisation, investment and sustainable economic development across the Niger Delta region.

Chairman of the Chambers, Mr. Idaere Gogo-Ogan, made the commitment yesterday in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, at the maiden Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the organisation.

Gogo-Ogan said the Chambers would continue to provide a platform for business advocacy, investment facilitation, private-sector collaboration and economic development, stressing that the region must move beyond dependence on the extractive sector.

He called for greater emphasis on industrialisation, innovation, entrepreneurship, value addition and regional economic cooperation as pathways to sustainable growth.

According to him, the Niger Delta possesses abundant natural resources, a strategic coastal location and significant human capital that could be leveraged to transform the regional economy.

He said, “Since inception, the Chambers has provided nano, micro, small and medium-scale enterprises with support through entrepreneurship development, training, access to finance, market linkages, institutional partnerships and business-to-business arrangements, in view of their fundamental value in employment generation and wealth creation.”

The chairman disclosed that NDCCITMA had commenced moves to establish a Science, Innovation and Technology Park and acquired a 50-year lease over 100 hectares of land at the Goldland Industrial Park in Okansu/Egada, near Omoku in Rivers State.

He said the land would be developed and leased to generate revenue while supporting industrial and business activities in the region.

Gogo-Ogan also revealed that the Chambers had established an equipment and mobility leasing facility and was working towards an international trade fair and convention centre, alongside other strategic partnerships with organisations and multinational companies.

He said NDCCITMA would deepen engagements with national and international chambers of commerce and business partners to expand investment and trade opportunities for businesses in the Niger Delta.

While commending the management of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), led by Chief Samuel Ogbuku, for its support, Gogo-Ogan urged members, stakeholders, investors and business partners to contribute their expertise, experience and resources towards advancing the region.

He assured that the board, carefully constituted from across the Niger Delta, would remain committed to the mandate of the Chambers.

“The present board will not betray the confidence reposed in us. The Chambers was created as a child of necessity, and we will ensure that its mandate is fully upheld and diligently executed,” he said.

World.title: NECA: Businesses Neglecting Workforce Will Not Achieve Excellence
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Dike Onwuamaeze

The Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association (NECA) has warned that any business that is growing while neglecting its people would not achieved excellence.

NECA stated this recently in Lagos during a press conference to announce the 5th edition of its NECA Employers’ Excellence Award with the theme ‘Celebrating Excellence in Enterprise, Leadership and Responsible Employment’.



The award is scheduled to hold next week on November 26.

Speaking during the conference, the Director General of NECA, Mr. Adewale-Smatt Oyerinde, said that the employers’ excellence award “represents our collective commitment to building a business environment where excellence is encouraged, responsible employment is valued, innovation is rewarded and people remain central to enterprise success.”

Oyerinde said that over the years, the awards has evolved into a distinguished platform for celebrating organisations and employers on merit, whose leadership, enterprise, innovation and workplace practices contribute meaningfully to national development.

He said, “The Awards reflect NECA’s enduring commitment to promoting a business environment in which enterprise success is matched by responsible employment practices, investment in people, respect for workers’ rights, innovation and corporate responsibility.

“We strongly believe that the success of any economy is closely linked to the quality of its enterprises, the effectiveness of its leadership and the capacity of its workforce.

“Organisations that invest in their people, embrace innovation, promote inclusive workplaces and operate responsibly are not only building sustainable businesses; they are also contributing to national productivity, economic growth and social development.”

He explained that the award’s theme underscored the importance of recognising employers who demonstrate that “business growth and profitability can go hand in hand with sound leadership, employee development, workplace inclusion, innovation and responsible employment practices.”

The Chairperson of the Awards Planning Committee, Mrs. Taiwo Dayo-Abatan, remarked that many Nigerian have kept their doors open, kept their people at work and kept faith with good practice when it would have been easier to cut corners.

Dayo-Abatan, who was represented by committee’s vice chairperson, Mr. Michael Alasa, said that the theme of the award stated their position plainly that are looking for employers who “build strong enterprises and treat people well” because “a business that grows while neglecting its people has not achieved excellence. We are looking for employers who do both.”

World.title: ELAN New Chairman Pledges to Extend Leasing to MSMEs, Rebrand Association
World.content:

Dike Onwuamaeze

The newly elected Chairman, Board of Directors, Equipment Leasing Association of Nigeria (ELAN), Mr. Tunde Netufo, has pledged to “pursue partnerships that help to extend the reach of leasing to more businesses, particularly Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and other productive sectors of the economy.”

Netufo, who is the Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Frontline Trust Limited, stated this in his acceptance speech at the 24th National Lease Conference of ELAN.

He said that other priorities of his tenure would include “strengthening member engagement, advancing access to suitable funding, supporting professional standards and capacity development, and sustaining advocacy for an enabling business and regulatory environment.”

He also stated that the new board has resolved to change the face of ELAN by stepping up in terms of rebranding.

“We can do better that we are doing. ELAN is about advocacy. It is about creating awareness for the organisation and I can assure that God helping us we are going to take ELAN to the next level,” he said.

According to him, there comes a time when things have to change.

Netufo said that the theme of the conference, which is “Equipment Leasing in Nigeria: Maintaining Balance in a Changing Economy,” spoke directly to the task before the association and its members.

“For leasing practitioners, maintaining balance means pursuing growth while protecting portfolio quality, embracing innovation while exercising sound judgement, and meeting customers’ needs while sustaining our businesses.

“For the new board, it also means responding to members’ immediate concerns while keeping our attention on the industry’s long-term development,” he said.

He added that the new board recognised that progress would depend on the contributions of all stakeholders including lessors, financiers, equipment suppliers, insurers, professional advisers, investors, government institutions and equipment users all have a part to play.

Therefore, “we will work to strengthen these relationships and ensure that ELAN remains a useful platform for cooperation and industry development,” he said.

The immediate past Chairman of ELAN, Mrs. Elizabeth Ngozi Ehigiamusoe, said in her welcome address during the conference that the theme reflected the choices many of leasing firms face every day.

Ehigiamusoe said, “We want to grow our businesses, but we must be careful about the risks we take.

“Our customers need affordable rentals, while we must cover funding and operating costs. Finding that balance is becoming more demanding.”

She said that the conference addressed “three important priorities for our industry: managing risk while pursuing growth, using technology to improve efficiency and sustainability, and developing funding solutions that support viable lease transactions.”

World.title: NISO Threatens Sanctions Against Steel, Cement Firms over Grid Distortions
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

. Power supply plunges below 1,000mw, begins recovery

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja

The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) has warned steel and cement manufacturing companies connected to the national grid to urgently address power quality violations or face sanctions.

This is coming amid concerns that harmonic distortions from their industrial operations could undermine the stability and reliability of electricity supply.

The system operator, in a statement in Abuja yesterday, specifically identified electric and induction furnaces, rectifiers and variable frequency drives as equipment capable of injecting distortions into the grid, potentially increasing technical losses, overheating equipment, interfering with protection systems and affecting electricity quality for other consumers.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NISO, Bello Mohammed, gave the warning at a stakeholder engagement with grid-connected steel and cement manufacturers held at the operator’s head office in Utako, Abuja.

Mohammed said operators must ensure that their industrial activities remained within acceptable power quality thresholds, in line with the Grid Code and other established technical requirements of the Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry (NESI).

He stressed that compliance was mandatory and that companies must implement corrective measures to address identified deficiencies, warning that failure to operate within prescribed limits could attract sanctions under the applicable regulatory and technical frameworks.

He listed the priority actions expected from affected companies to include comprehensive power quality assessments, identification of harmonic sources, improvement of power factors, installation of appropriate harmonic mitigation solutions and continuous monitoring, alongside regular technical reports to NISO.

The NISO chief executive also identified excessive reactive power demand and poor power factor as additional challenges, explaining that they could increase network loading and complicate voltage management.

He disclosed that the operator was already monitoring industrial customers in real time and developing an enhanced monitoring system to improve its visibility into harmonic injections and compliance with power factor requirements.

While urging companies to take timely corrective action, Mohammed said NISO was willing to provide technical guidance and work with operators to overcome implementation challenges.

Earlier, the Executive Director, System Planning, Shehu Abba-Aliyu, said the engagement was a follow-up to NISO’s earlier meeting with steel and cement manufacturers in September 2025 and subsequent correspondence reminding companies of their grid code obligations.

He said the latest meeting was intended to review harmonic assessment findings, examine compliance at identified industrial connection points, clarify technical requirements and consider available technologies for harmonic filtering and power quality improvement.

Abba-Aliyu commended companies that had responded positively to the operator’s communications, urging others to strengthen their engagement and close identified compliance gaps.

He warned that uncontrolled harmonic injections could discourage power-quality-sensitive industries from connecting to the national grid, potentially undermining efforts to expand industrial participation in the electricity market.

He said NISO’s objective was not merely to identify non-compliance but also to understand the technical and institutional difficulties confronting industrial operators and guide them towards meeting the required standards.

Also, the Executive Director, Finance and Corporate Services, Babajide Ibironke, urged participating companies to sustain compliance with NISO’s technical standards, maintain open communication and work with the operator to resolve outstanding challenges.

The General Manager, System Planning, Kabiru Adamu, and the Assistant General Manager, Engineering, Research and Innovation, Thomas Oludeji Ojo, also presented technical findings on harmonic assessments, grid compliance requirements and options for improving power quality.

Meanwhile, Nigeria’s electricity supply to Distribution Companies (Discos) plunged to 948MW at 2:26pm on Friday, underscoring the continued fragility of the country’s power system, before recovering to 2,717MW by 5:25pm.

The figures showed that as the grid began to recover, allocation to the 11 Discos increased by 1,769MW, representing a recovery of about 187 per cent within three hours, THISDAY observed.

At the height of the decline, Ikeja Disco received the highest allocation of 133MW, followed by Eko with 132MW and Ibadan with 119MW, while Kaduna, Jos and Kano received just 28MW, 30MW and 31MW respectively.

By 5:25pm, Abuja Disco had emerged as the biggest recipient with 485MW, followed by Ikeja with 366MW and Eko with 364MW. NISO had yet to explain the cause of the drop as of the time of going to press.

However, the sharp fluctuations in allocation highlight the persistent instability in electricity supply, with households and businesses continuing to contend with an unreliable national grid.

Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has inspected and showcased locally modified armoured fighting vehicles at a Research and Development (R&D) Exhibition in Bauchi.

The COAS also launched the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).

According to a statement issued by the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, the activities formed part of the maiden Nigerian Army Armoured Corps Biennial Conference, Reunion and Pulling-Out Ceremony, aimed at strengthening professionalism, operational efficiency and combat readiness in response to evolving security threats.

She explained that the newly launched SOP was designed to standardise operational procedures, enhance accountability and improve coordination in the deployment, management and maintenance of armoured assets.

Colonel Anele said the initiative highlighted the Nigerian Army’s commitment to institutional reforms and the modernisation of its combat capabilities to meet contemporary operational demands.

“A major highlight of the event was the R&D Exhibition, which featured tanks and Armoured Personnel Carriers (APCs) modified by Proforce Limited and Terra Industries, both indigenous defence equipment manufacturers. The exhibition demonstrated the growing collaboration between the Nigerian Army and local defence industries in developing innovative solutions to enhance equipment performance, operational sustainability and combat effectiveness,” the statement said.

The Army spokesperson added that the initiative reflected the Nigerian Army’s drive towards technological advancement, indigenous defence production and greater self-reliance in military equipment maintenance and modernisation, in line with the Federal Government’s ongoing investment in strengthening national defence capabilities.

World.title: ‘The system wants the people to be beggars’: Pensioners’ anger runs deeper than grant reviews
World.content:
Frustration over SASSA’s grant reviews has opened up a wider conversation about how far the grant actually goes.

Petro Snyders shared her view on The South African’s Facebook page, in a thread about SASSA’s bank account checks.

‘While the can just take’

Snyders accused the system of keeping people dependent.



“The system want the people to be beggers while the can just take!!!” she wrote.

Linda Arran shared that suspicion: “They are using any excuse to cut your grant.”

Their comments reflect a feeling among many pensioners that the grant barely covers the basics, and that reviews now threaten even that.



A grant stretched thin

The Older Person’s Grant reaches most older South Africans. Nearly three in four older people in South Africa receive an old-age grant.

Researchers say it carries a heavy load. The grant has helped reduce poverty among older people, but rising living costs and growing care needs are stretching it to its limits. The grant has kept pace with inflation, but only just.

In many homes, the pension supports grandchildren and unemployed adult children as well as the grant holder, which leaves little room when food, electricity and transport prices rise.



Fewer recipients ahead

Government expects the number of grant recipients to shrink. Treasury expects tighter controls to result in fewer people receiving grants. It expects stronger verification measures to save R13.1 billion over three years.

Pensioners also face other pressures on their grants. GroundUp reported that pensioners complained to the minister about deductions from their grants.

For Snyders, Arran, and many others, the reviews feel like one more burden on a grant that already struggles to stretch to month-end. That explains why their anger runs deeper than any single bank account check.

World.title: Leon Schuster plays another epic prank [video]
World.content:
Leon Schuster has done it again with another one of his silly pranks, this time on his best friend, Alfred Ntombela.

The veteran comedian is known for his popular candid camera movies, like You Must Be Joking, Millennium Menace and Oh Schucks!

Earlier this month, Schuster pranked SABC media personality Leanne Manas during an interview. He also reflected on his scariest filming experience.



LEON SCHUSTER PRANKS PAL

In a video posted on Facebook, actor Alfred Ntombela revealed how Leon Schuster had pranked him yet again.

In the clip, Alfred – known as “Shorty”, and who often features in many Schuster movies as his sidekick- visited his pal’s house in Johannesburg.

During their visit, Schuster offered his visitor a cup of piping hot tea, which he playfully pretended to spill on him.



While Alfred was visibly shaken, the 75-year-old veteran star laughed as he exclaimed: “I got you!”

Alfred then questioned his longtime friend about quitting his shenanigans, to which Schuster responded: “I’ll never stop!”

‘I’LL DIE A PRANKSTER’

During an interview with Leanne Manas earlier this month, Leon Schuster revealed that he had no ill intent behind his candid camera pranks, some of which have courted controversy for their portrayal of “blackface”.



He shared: “I’m a prankster, and I’ll die a prankster. It’s all part of the culture of this land”

“It’s important you know your audience. I try to give the people what they want. I’m so sorry I can’t make one final candid-camera movie. But one more clap and my neck will break”.

He added: “I want to be remembered as that okie from the Free State who stood firmly on the ground, who didnt a swollen head, and who contributed somehow to unify our nation through my movies”.



NETFLIX FILM IN THE WORKS

Meanwhile, Leon Schuster has shared the exciting news that he is working on a film in collaboration wth Netflix.

Although it won’t be a candid camera movie, it will feature him in a comedic role.



Leon has shared that he is likely to film a significant portion of the film in a wheelchair, given his chronic back pain, which has affected his mobility.

Schuster’s last movie was Mr Bones 3, released in 2024, during which he injured his back.

World.title: The Top 10 African countries with the highest English proficiency
World.content:
Africa has the widest range of proficiency scores of any region, according to the latest index. Image: Unsplash

Which African country is the most proficient in English? The latest international rankings reveal a close race at the top, with just one point separating the continent’s two leading contenders.



The 2026 EF English Proficiency Index (EF EPI), published by Education First (EF), ranks 117 countries and regions according to their English skills (reading, writing, listening, and speaking).

South Africa, once again, tops the continental rankings with 588 points, placing it 14th globally. Zimbabwe is hot on its heels, scoring just one point less.

Kenya and Nigeria complete Africa’s top four, with scores of 582 and 578 respectively.



Here are the 10 African countries with the highest English proficiency, according to the latest index.

African rank Country EF score Global rank 1 South Africa 588 14 2 Zimbabwe 587 15 3 Kenya 582 20 4 Nigeria 578 21 5 Ghana 535 35 6 Uganda 517 48 7 Ethiopia 506 53 8 Morocco 492 60 9 Tunisia 490 61 10 Tanzania 477 70

language development across the continent

The report highlights the continent’s considerable differences in English proficiency.

In fact, EF says Africa has “the widest range of proficiency scores of any region.” There is a gap of almost 200 points between its highest- and lowest-scoring countries.



The report attributes this disparity partly to Africa’s colonial history. It also reflects the different roles English plays in modern African societies.

However, there is an interesting finding concerning gender. Africa is the only region where women outperform men in English proficiency on average.

Ethiopia recorded the world’s largest female advantage, with women scoring 51 points higher than men. Malawi followed with 44 points, while Nigeria recorded a 25-point gap.



EF also identifies a link between English proficiency and economic development. Its research suggests that stronger English skills can help workforces attract international investment and collaboration.

Global English proficiency continues to decline

Despite some strong performances, the global picture is less encouraging.

The worldwide average English proficiency score declined for the fifth consecutive year in 2026. More than two-thirds of countries with comparable data recorded lower scores than in 2025.



The report also identifies a significant gap between people’s ability to read English and their ability to speak it.

Reading remains the strongest skill in four out of five countries and regions assessed. Speaking is the weakest in approximately 40%.

Globally, the average speaking score trails reading by 57 points.



The 2026 index draws on results from 2.3 million adults across 117 countries and regions. Participants took EF’s online Standard English Test (EF SET) during 2025.

World.title: The real reason Orlando Pirates fans love Evidence Makgopa
World.content:
Evidence Makgopa received a loud reception when he came on during Orlando Pirates’ Carling Knockout Cup semi-final clash against Stellenbosch.

The 26-year-old striker came off the bench in the second half and scored a brace to send the Buccaneers into the final.

Having struggled with injuries this season, Makgopa has hardly featured for Pirates during the campaign. However, when called upon, Ngwana Sesi delivered when it mattered most.



In a tightly contested encounter, his two goals proved crucial for the Soweto giants, reminding doubters why he remains a popular figure among the Buccaneers faithful.

What makes Makgopa popular at Orlando Pirates?

In the 107 appearances he has made for Pirates, Makgopa has scored just 25 goals. However, statistics do not always tell the full story, as many of his goals have come in important moments.

His three goals against Kaizer Chiefs in the Soweto Derby have played a significant role in winning over the Pirates supporters in recent seasons.

Beyond his goalscoring record, his work rate, intensity and passionate celebrations have earned him praise from supporters, including some who initially struggled to appreciate his contribution.

His fighting mentality and humility have also endeared him to the Buccaneers faithful, qualities that have continued to shine through when representing the national team.

Makgopa has arguably delivered more than many strikers who have represented Orlando Pirates over the past decade. When fit, he always carries a goal threat, particularly in big matches.



He is not a striker who goes missing when the pressure is on. He constantly puts defenders under pressure, works hard off the ball, links up play and is willing to contribute defensively when needed.

At just 26, Makgopa still has plenty of years ahead of him and is building a strong legacy at Orlando Pirates.

If he continues delivering in the biggest moments, Ngwana Sesi could cement his place among the club’s most beloved players.

World.title: Why one deposit could get your SASSA grant flagged
World.content:
A short comment about a Father’s SASSA grant has raised a question that worries many older South Africans.

Charmie Botha shared her family’s experience on The South African’s Facebook page, in a thread about SASSA cutting grants after bank account checks.

‘It was a ONCE-OFF payment’

Botha said her father had already been through what other commenters feared.



“Happened to my dad it was a once off payment,” she wrote.

Her comment suggests her father’s grant was affected after a single deposit appeared in his account. Many pensioners receive occasional lump sums, such as a payout from a former employer, an insurance claim or money from the sale of an asset.

How SASSA says it treats deposits

SASSA has tried to calm fears about one-off amounts. The agency said the existence of money in a bank account does not mean every amount is automatically treated as permanent monthly income that disqualifies a person.

The agency also warned against misinformation. SASSA urged beneficiaries not to be misled by social media claims about automatic grant cancellations.

Reviews still examine the full picture. SASSA checks bank statements against credit bureau information and data from other government departments to identify potential discrepancies.

What families can do

Pensioners who receive a once-off payment should keep proof of where the money came from, such as a letter, payout statement or sale agreement. That evidence can help explain the deposit if SASSA flags it during a review.



Responding quickly also matters. SASSA has urged beneficiaries to act as soon as they receive a review notice, and it can only send notifications to the contact details recorded on its database.

Families who believe SASSA made the wrong decision can first ask the agency to reconsider.

Botha’s comment drew attention because it described a real experience rather than a fear. For many families, it serves as a reminder to keep records of every unusual payment.

World.title: Springboks lose to Ireland, but reach Nations Championship ‘final’
World.content:
The Springboks lost their Nations Championship clash against Ireland at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Saturday, but did enough to reach next weekend's 'final'. Image: X @Springboks

The Springboks lost their Nations Championship clash against Ireland at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Saturday, but did enough to reach next weekend’s ‘final’.

Ireland won 20-17 after leading 17-10 at half-time.

READ | England deny All Blacks



Ireland scored three tries thanks to a brace by wing Robert Baloucoune and a five-pointer by hooker Rónan Kelleher. Flyhalf Sam Prendergast added a conversion and a penalty.

The Springboks scored tries by scrumhalf Morne van den Berg and hooker Malcolm Marx, while flyhalf Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu added both conversions and a penalty.

South Africa’s bonus point for losing by fewer than eight points was enough to see them top the Southern Hemisphere standings ahead of New Zealand on points difference.

They will contest the ‘final’ against either England or France on Sunday, 29 November at 18:40 (SA time).

World.title: Coalition Conundrum | Talks reach critical stage | 21 November 2026
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Coalitions are entering a critical stage in South Africa's biggest metropolitan municipalities.

Meanwhile, voters are waiting with keen anticipation to find out who will lead their municipalities following the local government elections.

In Gauteng, negotiations appear to be nearing completion, with reports suggesting ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba could return as Johannesburg mayor.

In eThekwini are also working to forge a governing coalition after no single party secured an outright majority.

As negotiations continues behind closed doors, questions remain about the stability and durability of the arrangements being negotiated.

World.title: UK's Princess Catherine explores life after cancer in 'personal documentary'
World.content:
Prince William's wife Catherine will explore life beyond a cancer diagnosis in a personal documentary, almost two years after she revealed she was in remission, her office said on Saturday.

The British future queen, 44, also known as Kate, announced in March 2024 she had been diagnosed with an unspecified cancer and was undergoing chemotherapy.

"Heal", described as a "deeply personal" documentary, will be broadcast by the BBC on November 29, the princess's Kensington Palace office said in a statement.

It will air internationally via NBCUniversal in the United States on November 30, Channel 9 in Australia on December 1 and CTV and Noovo in Canada on December 7, it added.

Catherine, whose formal title is Princess of Wales, has three children aged between eight and 13 with heir to the throne William.

She revealed she was in remission in January 2025.

The documentary "follows the princess on a personal journey through some of Britain's most spectacular landscapes" as she takes part in one of the UK's best-known endurance events, the Three Peaks Challenge, the statement said.

Participants in the challenge, which Catherine completed in June, climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours.

"Set against the backdrop of the challenge itself, the princess reflects on her own experience alongside individuals navigating their own health journeys," the statement said.

"Together they explore the profound impact serious illness can have on the whole person and the people, places and experiences that can help us heal," it added.

Catherine's father-in-law, King Charles III, was also diagnosed with cancer, which was revealed by Buckingham Palace on February 5, 2024.

Charles, 78, has returned to public duties but is still being treated for an undisclosed cancer.

All funds generated by the documentary's distribution will go to Britain's Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.

World.title: Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino
World.content:
African football supremo Patrice Motsepe said Saturday that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino's bid for re-election as FIFA president.

Motsepe made the declaration in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino's two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo is present.

former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate.

The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat -- the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations.

CAF has been consistently behind Infantino -- who is seeking a fourth and final term -- even after the furore he stirred up in July with his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 World Cup.

"Gianni, you have our support on behalf of the 54 nations in Africa to be our candidate," Motsepe said.

"I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we are unanimously supporting Gianni."

Infantino has faced multiple calls to step down and lost the backing of European football's governing body UEFA, whilst CONCACAF has also been strident in its criticism of the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer.

Motsepe though has been a vocal supporter and Infantino said such loyalty was reciprocal.

"You will always find, in me and in FIFA, a trusted partner," Infantino told the assembly, announcing cash inflow of $25 million to each member of CAF, starting January 2027 for development projects.

On Wednesday, UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister told AFP that Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at the 1960 Olympics in Rome, should not be seen as solely a European candidate.

"He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF countries," she said.

McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of UEFA, noted though that confederations do not vote as a bloc.

"There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda," the 61-year-old said.

"There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands.

"This applies everywhere in world football. This is not about Europe, the same rules apply globally."

World.title: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka to be laid to rest in eXesi
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka will be laid to rest in eXesi in the Eastern Cape on Saturday 28 November.

She passed away on Friday after complications from a medical procedure.

Mlambo-Ngcuka has been granted a State Funeral and her memorial service will be on Tuesday at the Our Lady of Lourdes Catholic Church in Rivonia, Johannesburg.

World.title: Finland detects drone attack on Russian cargo ship in Baltic
World.content:
Finland's military detected a drone attack on Saturday morning on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea which caused the vessel to catch fire, the Nordic country's authorities said.

The Finnish defence ministry did not specify who was behind the drone strike, but Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a message on X: "War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity... Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."

Fighting off a Russian invasion now in its fifth year, Ukraine has stepped up its long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the front lines.

"On Saturday morning, the Finnish Defence Forces detected a drone attack against a Russian cargo vessel west of Suursaari, in the eastern Gulf of Finland, in international waters," the ministry said in a statement.

According to Finnish border guards dispatched to the scene the ship caught fire and began drifting towards Finnish waters after the strike.

"The situation currently poses no danger to other vessels," the border service said in a press release.

Authorities gave no immediate details of the boat's crew.

Finland immediately informed NATO of the strike, the defence ministry said.

It said temporary restrictions were enforced in the airspace and maritime area of the eastern part of the Gulf.

The Baltic Sea has become a potential flashpoint in the wake of Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, with Western countries accusing Moscow of conducting a "hybrid war" in the strategic waterway.

Lying at the easternmost end of the Baltic along the coasts of Finland, Estonia and Russia, the Gulf of Finland is a key maritime passage for Russia, leading to the former capital, Saint Petersburg.

World.title: 'I'll be back': vows Kane after ankle surgery
World.content:
Bayern Munich's star striker Harry Kane pledged to return and help his injury-ravaged side for the "business end of the season" after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday.

Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle.

Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d'Or winner had "successfully undergone surgery" on his left ankle.

"The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program," Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months.

Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season.

"The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season."

Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: "tough times don't last, tough people do", while thanking his supporters for their messages of support.

Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023.

England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England's most capped player's rehabilitation progresses.

England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March.

- Bayern's casualty ward -

The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front.

Bayern have been without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer in recent weeks.

On Friday, Michael Olise -- one of Bayern's few remaining forwards -- went down after a tackle late in the first-half.

Despite continuing until the break, the France star did not return for the second-half.

World.title: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka granted State Funeral
World.content:
Her official funeral will take place at the family home in eXesi in the Eastern Cape.

Mlambo-Ngcuka was, at the time of her death, Chancellor at the University of Johannesburg since 2022.

She served as deputy president under former president Thabo Mbeki from 2005 to 2007. She also served as Minister of Minerals and Energy from 1999 until 2005.

She also served deputy minister of trade and industry from 1996 until 1999.

Mlambo-Ngcuka is survived by her husband Bulelani Ngcuka and her five children.

Ramaphosa, who is currently in the US says he is looking forward to offering his condolences to the family upon his return.

World.title: Greek PM under fire over Grand Theft Auto post
World.content:
Greece's prime minister has come under fire for asking youngsters whether they'd like the mature-content Grand Theft Auto VI videogame for Christmas.

"Which of you will ask for Grand Theft Auto VI as a Christmas present from grandad and grandma?" Kyriakos Mitsotakis said in a TikTok post on Friday, with the game's logo briefly flashing on-screen.

"We all know that grandfathers and grandmothers rarely say no to their grandchildren," he added.

The post was designed to promote a 400-euro ($439) pension bonus from Mitsotakis' government, as it faces elections next year.

But it came under attack from critics calling it inappropriate to encourage minors to buy a mature game.

"The prime minister 'promotes' a video game that is banned for minors just to follow the trend," the main opposition socialist Pasok party said.

Leftist daily Efsyn called the move a "gaffe" while conservative newspaper Dimokratia said it was a "tragic" error.

Ironically, Mitsotakis' government has joined a growing number of countries imposing curbs on young people's use of social media.

World.title: IEBC under pressure as legal battles threaten 2027 election preparations
World.content:
IEBC chairperson Erastus Ethekon. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

Stakes in the 2027 elections could not have been higher, however nothing seems to be working in that direction. At least going by the bickering from politicians, the court cases and the stalled tendering process.

Stakeholders in the electoral process have raised concerns over the ability of the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) to conduct credible polls next year, citing shrinking timelines and the numerous challenges facing the commission.

World.title: Narok Senator under fire after threatening to shoot auctioneers in Sh1.2m dispute
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama ole Kina is at the centre of a national uproar after a viral video captured him threatening to shoot individuals during a volatile confrontation involving auctioneers and a former Senate office employee.

The dramatic standoff erupted when court-backed agents attempted to seize a milk delivery truck over an unresolved legal dispute and has since ignited intense public debate regarding political accountability and the rule of law.

The controversy surrounds long court battle after Zakayo Rotiken, who served sacked as Narok North Constituency Coordinator between 2017 and 2020, was sacked.

According to records, the claimant was illegally dismissed amidst unpaid salary arrears.

On October 31, 2023, the Employment and Labour Relations Court ruled in Rotiken's favour , a decision that was subsequently upheld when the Senator lost his appeal.

With accrued interest, the court decree now stands at Sh 1.2 million.

Consequently, when the debt remained unsatisfied, licensed auctioneers moved in to execute lawful warrants which in turn provoked a furious reaction from Senator Ole Kina, who fiercely framed the entire episode as a political witch-hunt.

The lawmaker argued that Rotiken was hired by the Narok Senate office rather than his personal capacity, maintaining that any resultant liabilities ought to be handled by the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) rather than attaching his private property.

Defending his harsh words in the widely circulated footage, the senator dismissed the agents as trespassers and asserted action against them.

"Anybody who trespasses will get a bullet in their head or leg because that is trespass," said Ole Kina.

“Nitakupiga Risasi!” Senator Ledama Ole Kina embroiled in confrontation with alleged auctioneers over unpaid car loan https://t.co/k4OSXpNsdi November 21, 2026

The claimant's legal team condemned the threats made against statutory court officers emphasizing that a court judgment is an enforceable command rather than a mere suggestion, calling upon the Inspector General of Police of Police and the Director of Criminal Investigatons to urgently investigate the alleged death threats.

Rotiken noted that he merely sought justice through proper judicial channels and should not be penalized or intimidated for pursuing his lawful entitlements.

"When I was illegally dismissed with unpaid salary arrears, I did not resort to violence or politics—I went to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Nobody is above the law, and I appeal to the police to protect the officers doing their job so that justice can finally be served," he said.

Ultimately, as pressure mounts on security agencies to look into the firearm threats, the unfolding saga highlights a tense intersection between public office obligations and the absolute sanctity of judicial decrees.

While the senator maintains that his assets were unjustly targeted by political rivals, legal experts and the public continue to demand that the rule of law must prevail without exception.

World.title: Ruto defends IEBC, challenges rivals to present alternative policies
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has launched a scathing attack on opposition leaders over their demands on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), accusing them of attempting to interfere with the electoral agency because they fear losing the 2027 General Election.

The President challenged opposition leaders to allow IEBC to prepare independently for next year's elections, saying they should instead focus on identifying their presidential candidate, developing a manifesto and presenting alternative policies to Kenyans.

Ruto accused his competitors of attempting to play the roles of both contestants and referees by seeking to influence decisions on the procurement of election materials and equipment.

He spoke a day after opposition leaders walked out of a meeting convened by IEBC, alleging bias by the commission.

“Please give IEBC a chance to arrange the elections next year. The people of Kenya will decide. You go and first look for your candidate, find your policies, agenda and plans and sell them to the wananchi. We shall meet at the ballot,” said Ruto.

Speaking during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto questioned why opposition politicians were concentrating on determining how IEBC should procure election materials instead of preparing to face voters.

“How can somebody who is in a competition want to decide where the pitch will be, who the referee will be and where the ball will be placed? Leave IEBC alone. Those who will vote are the citizens, and they are the ones who will decide,” he said.

The President accused his opponents of lacking a clear political agenda and capacity to deliver, claiming their campaigns were centred on slogans and personal attacks against him.

He challenged them to explain what they would do differently in agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment rather than mobilising Kenyans around the slogan 'Kasongo Must Go'.

“The reason why my competitors cannot develop a plan is that they have no capacity. The reason why they have no agenda is that they have no knowledge. The reason why they cannot develop anything is that they know they have no capacity to deliver on anything that they will say,” he said.

His remarks were echoed by Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, who rallied Western Kenya leaders behind his re-election bid and defended IEBC against what they termed unnecessary political pressure. President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [ Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Speaking in Butere, Barasa said the region's political leadership, including Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Wetang'ula and trade unionist Francis Atwoli, was united behind Ruto's development agenda.

“IEBC will conduct the elections according to the law. Opposition leaders should leave IEBC alone and allow it to do its work,” he said.

Wetang'ula maintained that IEBC was independent of both the government and the opposition and should be allowed to conduct its work without interference.

“IEBC is independent of the government and independent of the Opposition. You stand there to do your work fairly, truthfully and equally,” he said.

He added: “Just as Arsenal supporters cannot dictate what uniform the referee should wear, the referee's responsibility is to ensure the game is played fairly and the winner emerges through a legitimate process.”

The exchanges underline the growing political contest over the management of the 2027 elections, with the government side accusing the opposition of undermining the electoral agency before campaigns gather momentum.

Beyond the political exchanges, Ruto used his Western Kenya tour to highlight development projects, saying his administration was committed to correcting years of neglect and unequal distribution of national resources.

He also announced plans for a second phase of the Nyota programme targeting an additional 200,000 young people, each expected to receive Sh50,000 to establish or expand businesses.

The government is also targeting 100,000 college graduates for internships from January, with each expected to receive a monthly stipend of Sh20,000.

Ruto's tour comes amid growing competition for Western Kenya's support ahead of the 2027 General Election, with emerging opposition alliances seeking to challenge his influence.

World.title: Ruto sustains attacks on Gachagua, dares Opposition to name 2027 flagbearer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto launches Matisi-Bokoli-Milani-Teremi road in Webuye West on November 19, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

President William Ruto has challenged Opposition leaders to name their presidential candidate and unveil a clear political agenda, accusing them of wasting time hopping from one hotel to another and holding meetings in private residences in search of a flagbearer and campaign manifesto.

The President said the Opposition was yet to settle on a flagbearer or agree on a common agenda despite the clock ticking towards the 2027 General Election.

He dismissed the rival camps' political engagements as endless consultations and manoeuvres, arguing that their leaders were more preoccupied with political meetings than developing policies to convince Kenyans.

Speaking in Bungoma during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto challenged his opponents to stop what he termed political confusion and present an alternative development agenda, insisting he was ready to face them in the 2027 contest.

"These people do not have a candidate. They are struggling, moving from one hotel to another and from one person's house to another, trying to find an agenda and a manifesto before they can start campaigning. Time is running out, yet they are still struggling to agree on an agenda," he said.

Ruto also launched a fresh attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, accusing him of promoting tribalism and hatred while questioning his remarks about relocating to Texas, United States.

The President mockingly referred to Gachagua as "Mr Chuki wa Texas", questioning why he would allegedly acquire a house in the US while engaging in politics that could divide Kenyans and fuel hostility.

"Mr Chuki wa Texas has gone to buy a house in Texas. He wants to know whether he will flee our country after spreading tribalism and hatred, dividing people and turning them against each other, before boarding a plane to Texas and leaving others to deal with the consequences," Ruto said.

He accused the former Deputy President of attempting to turn communities against one another for political gain, warning that he would not allow anyone to undermine national unity through ethnic mobilisation.

Ruto said he was ready to confront his political opponents directly but insisted that political competition should not become an avenue for spreading hatred and inciting Kenyans against one another.

The President also questioned Gachagua's allies over their reported visit to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) offices in Kizirani, accusing the Opposition of picking unnecessary fights with the electoral agency ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He suggested that politicians who begin questioning the electoral commission before elections could be preparing grounds to reject the results should they lose.

"Whenever you see someone picking a fight with IEBC, that person is already looking for an excuse to fail. Now they are coming up with all sorts of excuses, asking whether it is IEBC that votes. Is IEBC responsible for the votes?" He posed.

Ruto urged politicians to stop harassing the electoral agency, maintaining that the power to elect leaders rests with Kenyans and not the commission.

"I want to tell Kenyans to stop harassing IEBC. IEBC does not have votes. The votes belong to the people of Kenya," he said.

The President maintained that his administration was focused on delivering development, challenging the Opposition to explain its alternative plans on electricity connectivity, education, healthcare and infrastructure.

He questioned what the Opposition considered its development agenda, dismissing what he described as recycled political slogans and simplistic promises.

The President particularly took issue with promises centred on providing porridge to Kenyans, questioning whether such pledges could constitute a credible national development agenda.

He urged voters to interrogate the policies and development track records of politicians seeking their support instead of being swayed by political rhetoric and personal attacks.

The latest attack marks an escalation in political exchanges between Ruto and his rivals as competing camps intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

It also comes amid efforts by Gachagua and other Opposition figures to consolidate their political formations and build a formidable challenge to Ruto's re-election bid, with Western Kenya emerging as a key battleground.

World.title: Ruto lists measures to lower cost of living, put more money in Kenyans' pockets
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his State Of The Nation Address at Parliament, Nairobi. November 18th, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

President William Ruto has outlined a raft of government interventions aimed at reducing the cost of living, increasing household incomes and creating more employment opportunities for Kenyans.

Addressing Parliament during the 2026 State of the Nation Address on Wednesday, Ruto said his administration had prioritised lowering the cost of essential goods and services while increasing earnings across key sectors of the economy.

“Our economic proposition was simple: Reduce the cost for families and increase the income from what they do,” he said.

On food prices, the President cited the government’s fertiliser subsidy programme, which has reduced the price of a 50-kilogramme bag of fertiliser from Sh7,500 in 2022 to Sh2,000 this year.

He said the government had distributed 38.5 million bags of subsidised fertiliser to farmers, contributing to an increase in maize production from 44.3 million bags in 2022 to 71 million bags last year.

Consequently, maize imports declined from 9.9 million bags to 3.3 million bags, while the average price of a two-kilogramme packet of sifted maize flour dropped from a high of Sh230 in September 2022 to Sh152 in September this year.

Ruto also highlighted gains in the tea, coffee, dairy and sugar industries, saying government interventions had helped improve production and increase farmers' earnings.

He said the Cherry Advance Revolving Fund had disbursed Sh15.07 billion to 684,000 coffee farmers, while tea export earnings increased from Sh163 billion in 2022 to Sh187 billion in 2025.

In the dairy sector, milk production rose from 4.5 billion litres to 5.52 billion litres, while average earnings for farmers increased from Sh32 to Sh60 per litre last month.

Sugar production, he added, increased by 60 per cent between January and October, with cane crushing rising by 57 per cent. The industry is projected to produce more than 900,000 tonnes by the end of the year, with Sh1.2 billion in bonuses expected to be paid to sugarcane farmers.

On healthcare, Ruto said the Social Health Authority (SHA) was designed to ease the financial burden of medical expenses on households through a shared health financing system.

In education, he said the government had employed 100,000 teachers and was preparing to recruit an additional 20,000 to address staffing shortages and reduce the burden on parents who pay teachers hired through Boards of Management.

He added that 23,000 classrooms had been constructed, while 1,600 laboratories were being built and equipped.

The President said the annual education allocation had increased from Sh521 billion in the 2022/23 financial year to Sh784 billion in the current financial year.

"These investments improve the quality of education while progressively reducing the need for Kenyans to finance education," he said.

On affordable housing, Ruto said more than 313,000 homes were at different stages of construction across the 47 counties, with over 1.37 million Kenyans registered on the Boma Yangu platform and more than 18,000 homes already allocated.

He said households could work towards homeownership through monthly payments starting at Sh4,000, which he argued would help ease the burden of rent.

The housing programme, according to the President, had also generated more than 1.1 million employment opportunities and reserved orders worth over Sh61 billion for Jua Kali artisans.

On employment, Ruto said 350,000 Kenyans had secured jobs through the digital economy programme, while another 707,000 had obtained employment abroad through international labour mobility initiatives.

He also cited the Hustler Fund, saying more than seven million Kenyans had established credit records through the programme, with cumulative borrowing reaching Sh94 billion.

Under the NYOTA programme, more than 133,000 young entrepreneurs had received training, mentorship and Sh50,000 each in start-up capital, he said.

The President further announced proposed tax measures aimed at increasing disposable incomes, including exempting workers earning Sh32,333 or less per month from Pay As You Earn (PAYE).

Other proposals include scrapping stamp duty on land transactions valued at Sh1 million or less and removing the 25 per cent import duty on mobile phones.

On pending bills, Ruto said the government had approved the settlement of 28,726 verified claims amounting to Sh27.8 billion, covering debts of Sh50 million and below dating back to 2005.

He added that Sh18 billion owed to public universities and another Sh16 billion owed to public and private hospitals under the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) had been approved for payment and were undergoing Treasury processing.

“These are not isolated interventions, but parts of one comprehensive undertaking,” Ruto said.

He maintained that the government's economic strategy was anchored on reducing household expenditure, increasing incomes and expanding opportunities for Kenyans.

World.title: After 22 years of waiting, woman welcomes quadruplet boys
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Samuel Langat speaks to journalists outside St Clare's Kaplong Mission hospital in Sotik Subcounty, Bomet county after his wife Lily Langat gave to quadruplets at the hospital. [Kiprono Kurgat, Standard]

After 22 years of waiting to become a mother, a woman has welcomed quadruplet boys in a rare and joyful birth that has brought immense happiness to her family.

Lily Langat delivered the quadruplets through a Caesarean section at St Clare’s Kaplong Mission Hospital in Sotik Sub-County on November 14, 2026.

The four boys arrived after more than two decades of waiting for a child in what the family described as a double blessing.

The 43-year-old mother could not hide her joy, saying the arrival of the four babies was an answer to years of prayer.

“I am very grateful to God for giving me four babies at once. This is a great blessing to my family. I thank the hospital staff for ensuring I got to see these bundles of joy,” she said.

“I have been praying and waiting upon God to give me double for the trouble. I have been childless for a long time, and God could not have given me a better gift than this,” she added.

She said she had been looking forward to the moment after doctors informed her early in the pregnancy that she could be carrying quadruplets.

Hospital staff celebrated the successful delivery, describing it as a rare occurrence at the facility.

A nurse who spoke with The Standard said the mother and her four newborns were in stable condition.

“We were delighted to deliver the babies. The mother faced some difficulties because of the combined weight of the four babies, but both she and the newborns are now stable,” she said.

The nurse said the babies had been placed in the nursery for observation and were doing well.

“This is a rare case in this hospital. We have had twins before, but this is different. None of the babies has developed complications so far, and we expect them to be discharged once they are fully stable,” she said.

She added that the mother was also recovering well and was expected to be discharged once doctors were satisfied with the condition of the newborns.

Lily's husband, Samuel Langat, appealed to well-wishers to support the family as they prepare to raise the four children.

“Raising four babies at once is no easy task. I am calling on well-wishers to lend a helping hand as we begin this extraordinary journey,” he said.

“Our four precious miracles have arrived safely, and while our hearts are overflowing with gratitude, the reality of caring for four newborns at once has brought challenges,” he added.

Naturally conceived quadruplets are extremely rare, although the likelihood varies depending on several factors, including maternal age and fertility treatment.

The birth marks a remarkable new beginning for the Langat family after 22 years of waiting for a child.

World.title: TSC picks Cheptumo Ayabei as new Chief Executive Officer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Teachers Service Commission headquarters in Nairobi. [File, Standard]

The Teachers Service Commission (TSC) has picked Cheptumo Ayabei as its new Secretary and Chief Executive Officer, making him the first person with a disability to head the commission.

Ayabei emerged top in interviews conducted on Monday, beating four other candidates, including the commission’s acting chief executive, Dr Evaleen Jesang Mitei, to become the country’s top teachers’ employer.

His selection ends a prolonged search for a substantive head of the commission, which has operated under acting leadership since the departure of former CEO Nancy Macharia in June 2025.

Ayabei, who hails from Baringo County, is currently TSC’s Director of Finance, having served at the commission for more than two decades. He joined the institution in 1999 as a Finance Officer before rising through the ranks to become Director of Finance in 2009.

His elevation marks a significant milestone for the representation of persons with disabilities in the country’s public institutions.

Ayabei was the first candidate to face the selection panel at 9am at the commission’s headquarters in Upper Hill, Nairobi. He was followed by Mitei at 10am, Robert Odette at 11am, Lawrence Ngai Kaburu at noon and Farah Abdi Saman at 1pm.

The five candidates were shortlisted from 124 applicants who responded to a fresh  issued on September 29. Applications closed on October 30.

Ayabei holds a Bachelor of Education degree in Mathematics and Economics from Kenyatta University and a Master’s degree in Finance and Banking from the University of Stirling in the United Kingdom. He is also a Certified Public Accountant.

Before joining TSC, he worked at the Ministry of Education between 1990 and 1999.

He takes over at a critical time for the commission, which oversees the employment, deployment, promotion and discipline of teachers across the country. He will inherit mounting pressure over teacher shortages, recruitment, promotions, transfers and the management of the teaching workforce.

The recruitment process had faced legal challenges, with a petition filed at the Employment and Labour Relations Court in Kisii seeking to halt the exercise.

The case, filed by Evans Morara Nyangongo under Cause E038 of 2026, challenged the fresh recruitment and raised questions about Mitei’s participation in the process while serving as acting CEO and seeking the substantive position.

Nyangongo sought to stop the commission from proceeding with the appointment until the issues raised in the petition were determined.

However, the court dismissed both the application and the suit, with no orders as to costs, clearing the way for the interviews.

In its defence, TSC maintained that the decision to advertise the position had been made collectively by the commission’s board and not by the acting CEO.

In a replying affidavit, TSC chairman Jamleck Muturi John maintained that Mitei had neither participated in the board’s deliberations on the recruitment nor influenced the process.

The fresh recruitment followed an earlier court decision that nullified the previous exercise over procedural irregularities, forcing the commission to restart the search for a substantive chief executive.

World.title: Thwake Dam project reaches 94pc completion
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Thwake Multipurpose Dam, which is 94.2 per cent complete, with the government targeting April 2027 for water impoundment.[File,Standard]

Thwake Dam is 94.2 per cent complete, with the government targeting April 2027 for water impoundment as residents seek a review of alleged construction-related damage claims.

Principal Secretary for Water and Sanitation Julius Korir told the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Blue Economy, Water and Irrigation that construction had reached 94.2 per cent.

The dam is being built at the confluence of the Athi and Thwake rivers along the Makueni-Kitui border. It is designed to provide water for domestic use, irrigation and electricity generation.

Martin Kimeu, a resident of Wote, said the project would improve access to water for farming in the region.

“Ukambani is fertile. Water has been the biggest impediment to the realization of our agricultural potential. Thwake Dam water is the clear solution to this,” he said.

Kimeu also defended the compensation process, saying he had followed the project since its inception and believed the exercise had been conducted properly.

Jacob Mwanzia, a resident of Madangi Village, said households in his area had been assessed and compensated. He argued that outstanding complaints should be addressed without delaying the project.

Mariam Mwikali, another resident, said assessments had been conducted on affected properties and residents given an opportunity to raise concerns.

However, some households have complained that construction-related blasting damaged their homes. Residents have reported cracks in walls, windows and foundations as well as dust, noise and ground vibrations.

In August 2026, residents from villages in Mavindini Ward, organised under the Thwake Dam Blasting-Affected Community Committee, sought an independent review by the African Development Bank (AfDB).

The residents alleged that some properties had been left out of assessments and compensation. They also sought access to assessment reports, photographs, measurements, valuation records and estimates for repairs or reconstruction.

A project official said the dam's safety department invited competitive bids for an independent assessment of properties potentially affected by blasting. Agile Consulting was selected to conduct the exercise.

The official said the consultant assessed 330 households within a two-kilometre radius of the construction site and submitted its report to the project implementation team. A large proportion of those assessed were satisfied with the exercise, the official added, without giving a breakdown.

Ben Mwongela, a director at Agile Consulting, said the assessment reviewed blasting records, vibration data and compliance with regulatory standards.

The exercise also involved documenting households, classifying structural defects and preparing bills of quantities and cost estimates for repairs or reconstruction, he said.

The AfDB conducted a field mission to the project between September 21 and 25, with its report published on October 21, 2026.

The bank's team, led by project task manager Nancy Ogal, met residents whose homes had been affected by blasting and identified outstanding health, safety, environmental and social issues, including homeowner grievances.

The bank called for timely compensation and continued monitoring of the project's environmental and social performance.

During a stakeholder engagement visit to Mavindini in October, Korir said the government had secured additional funding after the project experienced cash-flow constraints.
