World.title: Artist Raivo Järvi's cheerful drawings masked a life marked by personal tragedy
World.content:
Generations of Estonians grew up admiring the comics and illustrations of artist Raivo Järvi, better known as onu Raivo (uncle Raivo). Over the course of two decades, he also became a familiar radio voice and later spent nearly a decade in politics.

A new exhibition opening Friday at the Tartu Art Museum, "Pildi ees ja pildi sees" ("In Front of the Picture and Inside the Picture"), sheds light on lesser-known aspects of Järvi's life and work, revealing a more complex and at times deeply tragic personal story.

Born in Pärnu in 1954 as the only child of a violinist father and a ballet master mother, Järvi showed an interest in art from an early age. According to family recollections, he decided to become an artist at around age five after his mother warned him that an actor's life was difficult.

While artists are often associated with bohemian lifestyles, Järvi was known for discipline and meticulousness. From earning top marks in school to refining artistic motifs throughout his career, precision was one of his defining characteristics.

Uus kogumik tõi taas lugejate ette Raivo Järvi 1980. aastate koomiksid Autor/allikas: ERR

"It is a very interesting combination for an artist: meticulousness, a love of order and cleanliness. If you look at his graphic works, you see that same precision and stylistic purity," said his son, Richard-Erik Järvi.

Järvi's television career began almost by accident in 1977 while he was studying graphic arts at the Estonian State Art Institute (ERKI). When singer Voldemar Kuslap was unexpectedly unable to appear on the children's program "Laulujütsid," Järvi volunteered to draw with the children on air.

Over the next two decades, he became a beloved fixture of Estonian children's television, appearing in programs such as "Laupäeval koos isaga" ("Saturday With Dad"), "Kõige suurem sõber" ("The Greatest Friend") and "Jutupliiats" ("Story Pencil"). Viewers were particularly captivated by the drawings he created live on air, often completing elaborate characters before their eyes.

The 1983 children's television program "Kõige suurem sõber". Source: Heidi Maasikmets

Exhibition curator Stella Mõttus said audiences frequently wondered whether the outlines of the drawings had been prepared in advance.

"But no, he simply practiced them an enormous amount beforehand," she said.

Yet behind his public success lay significant personal hardship. Biography author Piret Kooli, who interviewed nearly 40 friends and colleagues while researching Järvi's life, said he endured profound losses. His father died when he was just ten years old. Later, he lost his first great love, dancer and actress Raili, who drowned during a film shoot under circumstances that remained unclear.

Richard-Erik Järvi said his father rarely spoke about her, but it was evident that the loss affected him deeply.

"It was the hardest period of his life," he said.

Järvi's later relationships were also troubled. His relationship with a beauty pageant princess named Signe, the mother of his son Richard-Erik, was short-lived. As a child, Richard-Erik knew little about his mother and was largely raised by his father, with invaluable help from family friend Tiia-Liis Jürgenson.

Jürgenson, whose own son was born just a week before Richard-Erik, helped care for the infant and later became a central figure in his upbringing.

"What began as a few days turned into a lifetime," she said. "For our family, it became completely natural."

Richard-Erik describes her as his guardian angel and says he often refers to her as his mother figure despite maintaining respect and gratitude toward his biological mother.

Raivo Järvi in "Pildi ees ja pildi sees". Source: Toomas Tuul

Despite his fame and productivity as an illustrator, radio host and later politician, Järvi never achieved substantial financial success. One notable example is the redesigned packaging for a popular curd snack introduced in 1996, featuring a cat illustration that became one of the most widely reproduced artworks in Estonia.

"Many people assume that cat earned him money for the rest of his life. In reality, it did not," Kooli noted.

According to those close to him, financial considerations partly motivated Järvi's decision to enter politics with the Reform Party. He served two terms in the Riigikogu, seeking financial stability for himself and his son.

A small room in an outbuilding on Faehlmanni tänav in Tallinn became his refuge when life became overwhelming. By then, his third major relationship, with an Estonia Theatre ballerina named Tatjana, had also deteriorated. Kooli believes Järvi spent much of his life searching for the love he had lost with Raili.

"He was looking for love, approval and himself," she said. "In reality, he was always looking for Raili."

Friends and family say that although Järvi maintained an upbeat public image, he often struggled privately. Kooli reflected that today he might well have been diagnosed with depression.

Despite being diagnosed with cancer, Järvi chose to keep his illness largely private. He continued working in Parliament and hosting radio programs until he was physically no longer able.

"He didn't want many people to know," his son recalled. "He had always felt the hardest way to leave was to slowly fade away in front of others."

Kooli remembered that Järvi continued broadcasting despite severe pain and diminishing strength. During his final broadcasts, medication affected his speech, leading some listeners to mistakenly assume he was intoxicated.

"Those comments were especially painful," Jürgenson said.

Raivo Järvi. Source: Ülo Josing/ERR

Fourteen years after Järvi's death, the Tartu Art Museum launched a public appeal for works to include in a retrospective exhibition. Nearly 500 pieces were identified in private collections and museums, with around 60 selected for display.

Curator Stella Mõttus said the exhibition reveals aspects of Järvi that many people never saw. While known primarily for the cheerful illustrations loved by children, some of his black-and-white graphic works are dark, unsettling and even apocalyptic.

"His life wasn't exactly rosy either," she said.

Richard-Erik Järvi, however, believes the works convey not only sadness and trauma but also resilience.

"We've talked about the tragic moments," he said, "but he always tried to remain positive."

World.title: Nmecha helps Dortmund beat Gladbach to top Bundesliga
World.content:
BERLIN: Felix Nmecha scored with 10 minutes remaining to send Borussia Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table with a 1-0 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday.

Bayern Munich’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday opened up the door for the chasers but Dortmund had few opportunities until Nmecha’s late strike.

Dortmund are now outright first on 24 points, with Bayern and Freiburg, who won 1-0 at Elversberg, locked on 22 points.

Bayern also lost Harry Kane to injury in Friday’s draw, with the Ballon d’Or winner set to miss several months after undergoing surgery on his injured ankle earlier on Saturday.

Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck urged his teammates not to get too far ahead of themselves, despite overtaking Bayern.

“The season is only truly decided from March or April onwards. We need to be in the mix by then,” he told reporters.

Dortmund, who travel to Arsenal on Tuesday, knew victory would send them top but the 2024 Champions League finalists had few chances against a stubborn Gladbach.

Nmecha, who scored twice in Dortmund’s 2-1 win over Elversberg before the international break, looked most likely when his header forced a save from Daniel Batz.

With 17 minutes left, Marcel Sabitzer chipped a free-kick inches wide of the post.

Dortmund continued to push and Nmecha was on hand to knock a rebound through Batz’s fingers and help the visitors snare a crucial three points.

Igor Matanovic’s 68th-minute strike helped Freiburg break down promoted Elversberg and move level with Bayern.

Last season’s Europa League finalists Freiburg stay one point ahead of fourth-placed RB Leipzig, who romped to a 5-1 victory at Union Berlin.

Antonio Nusa, Romulo, Brajan Gruda, Rocco Reitz and Ridle Baku scored for Leipzig, who host Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Gruda was particularly impressive with a goal and an assist, just days after impressing for Jurgen Klopp’s Germany with a goal and two assists versus the Netherlands on the other side of the German capital.

Elsewhere, Afonso Moreira broke his Bundesliga duck with a brace in Bayer Leverkusen’s 4-0 home win over Paderborn.

Moreira had failed to find the net since his summer move from Lyon but scored Leverkusen’s first two goals and laid on one for Ezequiel Fernandez.

Patrik Schick also got a goal to move level with Niclas Fuellkrug atop the league goalscoring charts with nine goals.

In Saturday’s late game, Schalke played out a scoreless home draw with Stuttgart.

Promoted in the summer, Schalke are yet to score a goal in five home matches.

Jonathan Burkardt scored the only goal as Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hoffenheim at home.

Frankfurt goalkeeper Noah Atubolu saved a first-half Andrej Kramaric penalty to keep his remarkable spot-kick record alive.

Atubolu has saved seven out of the 11 penalties he has faced, which is the best save percentage in the Bundesliga’s 64-year history.

World.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for Israeli coalition talks
World.content:
JERUSALEM: Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, has invited the right-wing Likud party of caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu for coalition talks, his party said on Saturday.

Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party said the talks, scheduled to begin on Sunday, reflected a “genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government.”

Former military chief Eisenkot has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu, after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc.

Saturday’s announcement comes as Eisenkot’s wide-ranging camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu’s bloc.

“In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party’s negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow,” the party said in a statement.

Former prime minister Naftali Bennett, an important figure in Eisenkot’s camp, on Saturday called for a “Zionist unity government headed by Eisenkot” and said his party would refuse to join up with Netanyahu or his bloc.

Netanyahu has been pushing hard for a national unity government, which he says is needed to guarantee Israel’s security.

Shortly after Eisenkot’s announcement, Likud laid out its position on forming such a government with Eisenkot’s bloc, including demands to halt “all personal attacks and incitement” as well as political “boycotts” against Netanyahu and the government.

Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud, but has previously ruled out serving in a government led by Netanyahu himself.

Likud also called for a joint declaration committing to a unity government including “all parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people” and without the participation of Arab parties.

Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly criticized leaders of Arab parties for refusing to describe Hamas as a “terror group” following its October 7, 2023 attack on Israel. All leaders of Arab parties have condemned the attack.

Likud proposed a set of guidelines for a unity government including an agreement that Israel is the nation-state of the Jewish people, a rejection of Palestinian statehood, the maintenance of Israel’s “security zones” in Syria, Lebanon and Gaza, and an arrangement on the issue of ultra-Orthodox conscription into the military through a “broad agreement” with the community’s leaders.

On Friday, Eisenkot vowed not to let coalition-building talks drag on and said that he would be prepared to put forward a minority national emergency government for a parliamentary vote should efforts to create a broad-based government fail.

World.title: 24 dead in Nigeria when boat capsizes while carrying people to a funeral
World.content:
ABUJA: A boat carrying people to a funeral has capsized in southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people, emergency services said on Saturday.

The boat was carrying passengers from one community to another for a burial ceremony when it sank on Friday in Bayelsa State in the country’s South South region, Nigeria’s National Emergency Management Agency spokesman Manzo Ezeki said in a statement.

Tragedy As Boat Carrying about 300 Passengers, Including Children, To Ukubie Community In Bayelsa Capsizes, Many Feared Drowned A boat conveying passengers, including children, to Ukubie community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, for a burial has capsized. Many passengers drowned, while others were seen struggling to swim to the riverbank for safety. The incident has raised concerns over the absence of life jackets, as none of the passengers was wearing one. — Esegbona Luis (@esegbonaluis) November 21, 2026

He said that search and rescue operations were ongoing without specifying how many people were missing.

Police spokesman Musa Mohammed said on Friday that another 24 people had been rescued and sought medical assistance.

Authorities haven’t said how many passengers were believed to have been on board.

World.title: Bahrain says Iran struck civilian industrial facility, sparking fire
World.content:
MANAMA: Bahraini authorities said on Saturday that Iran targeted a civilian industrial facility, causing a fire and damage, in the latest attack on the Gulf nation this week.

“As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site. Civil Defense is working to bring the fire under control,” the interior ministry said on X.

“Preliminary reports indicate material damage, with no injuries reported,” it added, without specifying the site’s location.

Bahrain's military said air defense systems dealt with "a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks" on Saturday.

The interceptions led to shrapnel falling and causing "minor material damage" and no human casualties," the General Command of the Bahrain Defense Force said.

The statement accused Tehran of ‌continuing its "systematic hostile approach" toward the kingdom.

The interior ministry had earlier warned residents of a potential threat.

Two residents told an AFP correspondent that they saw smoke rising above Sitra Island, on Bahrain’s east coast, which is home to several industrial facilities including a refinery run by state oil company Bapco.

Bahrain has been targeted several times this month, after a lull in Iranian attacks on Gulf countries since September.

The country, which hosts the US navy’s Fifth Fleet, was heavily targeted earlier in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

World.title: What We Are Reading Today: Scientific Studies by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
World.content:
Goethe’s scientific work may be less familiar to the reading public than his poetry, yet his understanding of natural phenomena displays the same sensitivity and brilliance as his depictions of human relationships.

Based on Goethe’s research in anatomy, botany, physics, chemistry, zoology, meteorology, and geology, these forty selections reflect Goethe’s conviction that scientists must develop their perceptions both inwardly and outwardly in pursuing the continuum of nature in an interconnected and living world.

World.title: PSG lose Doue to knee injury in Ligue 1 win at Nice
World.content:
PARIS: Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue was stretchered off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as the reigning French and European champions beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1 on Saturday.

Doue went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead.

He looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doue to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month.

The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too.

“We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Ligue 1+.

The 21-year-old French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in PSG’s Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns.

He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently.

“This is the life of a professional player at the very highest level,” added Luis Enrique. “You just have to accept it and I am sure he will find a way to recover well and come back even stronger.”

Earlier, Algerian international Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalize with a penalty awarded after a VAR check following a handball in the home box.

Doue — who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break — put PSG ahead a minute after that goal, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions.

His replacement Ferran Torres scored PSG’s third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season — but first in two months.

Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce.

Eight of those wins have come in Ligue 1, in which PSG are now five points clear at the top from Lille, who host Lyon later. Nice are sixth.

World.title: Palestinian authorities say man shot dead by West Bank settler guards
World.content:
RAMALLAH, Palestinian Territories: Palestinian authorities said a man was shot dead by security guards from an Israeli settlement in the central occupied West Bank on Friday, while another was detained during the incident.

The Palestinian health ministry announced the death of 42-year-old Hamza Masoud Salim Abdo, who it said was killed by “Israeli occupation gunfire near the village of Dura Al-Qar” north of Ramallah. It added that his body was being withheld.

A spokesman for the Ramallah-based General Authority of Civil Affairs, which is responsible for coordination between the Palestinian Authority and Israeli authorities, said the fire had come from guards of a nearby settlement.

“According to the information available, guards from the Beit El settlement opened fire on two men who were near a spring in the village of Dura Al-Qar, killing one and arresting the other,” he told AFP.

When contacted by AFP, the Israeli military said it was looking into the incident.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967, where violence has soared since Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack triggered the Gaza war.

Excluding Israeli-annexed east Jerusalem, the territory is home to some three million Palestinians and more than 500,000 Israelis, who live in settlements which are illegal under international law.

Israeli forces and settlers have killed 1,119 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the Gaza war in October 2023, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry.

Palestinian attacks or clashes between Palestinians and Israeli forces have killed at least 51 Israelis during the same period, according to official Israeli figures.

World.title: Arsenal held by Newcastle rally and lose Raya to injury
World.content:
NEWCASTLE: Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday.

The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes.

But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle.

Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points.

An important point 🔒 Well fought, lads 👊 https://t.co/s3DD2BLMN9 — Newcastle United (@NUFC) November 21, 2026

However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise.

Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions.

Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James’ Park.

Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defense of their title.

Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on.

Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August.

The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener.

It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek.

Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break.

Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so.

Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level.

Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks.

Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya.

That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell.

But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title.

Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek.

World.title: Iraq qualifies for 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup in Uzbekistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has officially confirmed the final 16-team lineup for the 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup, including Iraq, which topped Group B during the qualifiers in Thailand with 10 points—putting the young Lions of Mesopotamia just three group-stage matches away from securing a berth at the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Under head coach Salam Shaker, Iraq clinched first place in Group B after defeating tournament hosts Thailand 2–1 in their decisive final qualifier in Buriram on Friday, November 20, ending a nine-year continental qualification drought for the national under-17 side.

The finals are scheduled to take place in the Uzbek capital of Tashkent from May 13 to 29, 2027, following the official tournament draw on February 18, 2027.

Per AFC competition regulations, the top eight finishers at the tournament in Uzbekistan—specifically the eight teams that advance out of the group stage into the quarterfinals—will automatically qualify for the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Reaching the World Cup also carries a secondary continental incentive: under AFC rules, all Asian nations that qualify for the global finals earn direct entry into the 2028 AFC U-17 Asian Cup without having to contest the preliminary qualifying rounds.

The 16 participating nations in Tashkent comprise the seven qualifying group winners alongside the nine AFC representatives from the 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup who received automatic entry:

Qualification Route Qualified Nations Qualifying Group Winners Iraq (Group B), Indonesia (Group A), Syria (Group C), Iran (Group D), India (Group E), Yemen (Group F), Lebanon (Group G) Automatic Qualifiers Uzbekistan (Hosts), Australia, China PR, Japan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Tajikistan, Vietnam

Coach Salam Shaker and his squad now shift their focus toward preparing for February’s draw, aiming to replicate the historic success of Iraq’s 2016 U-16 championship generation and re-establish Iraqi youth football on both the Asian and global stages.

World.title: Japanese cyclist killed in highway collision in southern Iraq’s Muthanna Governorate
World.content:
Samawah (IraqiNews.com) – A Japanese bicycle traveler died on Friday, November 20, 2026, following a traffic collision along the Rumaitha–Samawah highway in southern Iraq’s Muthanna Governorate.

According to a security source, the tourist was riding a bicycle along the highway when he collided with a Dodge Charger sedan.

The impact proved fatal for the cyclist and also injured a passenger riding inside the vehicle, identified as a security officer.

Traffic police and forensic investigators conducted an on-site inspection of the crash scene following the incident. Based on their preliminary field assessment, authorities determined that the Japanese cyclist was at fault for the collision.

World.title: Iraqi Energy Police establish 12 checkpoints along Jurf Al Sakhar oil pipelines
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior’s Directorate General of Energy Police continued field operations on Saturday, November 21, 2026, to secure vital oil pipeline corridors across the Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr) subdistrict in northern Babylon Governorate.

Marking the second consecutive day since Baghdad formally inaugurated its new joint command center in the area, Energy Police units established full operational control along a pipeline stretch exceeding five kilometers.

In an official statement, Ministry of Interior Head of Relations and Media Major General Miqdad Miri confirmed that the deployment is being directed on the ground by Energy Police Director-General Lieutenant General Hamid Abdullah Ibrahim.

Executing the mission with a regiment from the Commando Brigade (Liwa al-Maghawir), engineering teams deployed specialized heavy machinery to carve a dedicated patrol road parallel to the pipeline bundles through rugged terrain, enabling rapid troop mobility and sustained field surveillance.

To lock down the corridor against illicit tampering, Energy Police established 12 new security checkpoints spaced roughly every 500 meters along the route, alongside a permanent regimental headquarters.

Major General Miri emphasized that these preventive measures are designed to elevate field command, safeguard crude transport infrastructure, and protect national wealth.

The deployment represents the first concrete operational phase following the expiration of Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi’s Friday ultimatum to Kata’ib Hezbollah.

On Friday, November 20, federal authorities inaugurated the joint control headquarters (Al-Musaytir)—commanded under the Federal Police and uniting Army, Federal Police, Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), and Energy Police formations—initiating a permanent security reorganization in Jurf al-Sakhar that includes securing pipeline networks and reopening closed transit arteries to civilian traffic.

World.title: US dollar steadies near 170,000 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged slightly lower across major domestic parallel markets on Saturday morning, November 21, 2026, hovering right at the 170,000-dinar threshold for retail sales while buying bids settled below that mark across key commercial hubs.

According to morning monitoring figures, physical banknote rates opened across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra as follows:

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 170,000 IQD against buying offers of 169,500 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks quoted retail selling rates slightly higher at 170,050 IQD alongside purchasing bids holding at 170,000 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices matched Baghdad’s selling quote at 170,000 IQD, with buying offers dipping to 169,250 IQD per $100.

Despite the downward drift at the start of the trading week, parallel cash rates maintain a spread of roughly 18,000 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

World.title: Gulf alternatives may save Excelerate Energy’s LNG project in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is witnessing rapid on-site progress amid efforts to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the marine jetty and terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq, Attaqa News reported.

US-based Excelerate Energy, which is carrying out the project, expects the pace of work to accelerate over the coming weeks, with construction activities progressing at the marine terminal and the facility’s infrastructure.

The firm aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the Iranian conflict have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026. As a result, Excelerate Energy has moved the Excelerate Acadia, its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), to Jordan for nine months.

To overcome disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed within the region, eliminating the need to traverse the strategic waterway.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express.

The US firm indicated that it is working to arrange the import of LNG from countries within the Gulf region, a statement that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,706.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,706 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,710 Iraqi dinars and 1,700 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,709.5 and 1,708.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraqi PM orders reopening of closed roads in Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, ordered on Thursday to expedite the reopening of all closed roads in the Jurf al-Sakhar district in the central province of Babil.

During his meeting with security officials, al-Zaidi emphasized that the army and security forces would uphold the authority of the state across all Iraqi territory, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister emphasized that the enforcement of state authority would be carried out in accordance with the constitution and the law. He affirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and interests of citizens across the country and to preventing any violations or assaults on public and private properties.

According to al-Zaidi, the security forces operate as a unified entity, with their numerous branches and units cooperating with one another.

These directives come ahead of the deadline set by the government for Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant faction, to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar—a deadline expiring on Friday—paving the way for security forces to enter and redeploy in the area.

The deadline for the withdrawal from Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, follows an investigation by a government committee, which Baghdad stated uncovered evidence of oil smuggling operations in the area.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China drops to $19.8 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, said on Thursday that the decline in trade exchange with Iraq—which fell to $19.8 billion—is due to the escalating security tensions in the region.

During a press conference in Baghdad, Bo projected that trade between the two countries would recover, reaching $26 billion by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

According to Bo, China is a trusted partner to Iraq. He noted that the two countries share deep historical and cultural ties, dating back thousands of years.

Bo emphasized that bilateral relations have seen significant development, with Iraq serving as a key trade partner. Trade volume between the two countries reached $51 billion in 2025, reflecting the strength of their mutual commitments and relationship.

Bo mentioned earlier that major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in several Iraqi provinces.

World.content:
The remarks come amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. Malik is visiting India for the first time.

As part of the retelling of the approximately 3000-year long history of the site, India showcased nine layers of continuity--among them the standing ramparts built by Sher Shah Suri (1538-1545 CE) after demolishing and re-modeling Dinpanah, a city founded here by Humayun, around 1533 CE.Reflecting on the excavations at the site, Malik said, âDelhi has not been diminished by civilisations and people coming from outside; rather, it has grown strongerâ.During his inaugural speech on Friday Prime Minister Narendra Modi had also reflected on the history of Purana Qila to assert Indiaâs civilisational journey going back thousands of years to the Mahabharata period. He also visited the âMahabharata Pavillion - Anant: A rare 18th century Mahabharata scrollâ and the exhibition âAstitvaâ offering an immersive account of Delhiâs history through archaeological evidence, that have been curated for the leaders from SCO countries to see.Day two of the Fourm saw ministers of all participating nations make statements. Malik who happens to be the Climate Change and Environmental Coordination referring to archaeological remains from different periods discovered during excavations at Purana Qila, said that the fort in which the delegates were seated was, in itself, a story. He appreciated the description of the event as âTehzeeb Ki Guftaguâ, or âDialogue of Civilisationsâ.

World.title: Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren writes to CJI seeking urgent appointment of HC chief justice successor
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

wrote a letter to

Surya Kant and the Supreme Court Collegium, urging them to expedite the appointment of a successor to Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M S Sonak, who is due to retire on November 27.

In his letter to the CJI and Collegium members, Soren warned that the absence of a permanent successor could lead to another interim arrangement, affecting administrative continuity and institutional planning in the high court, as cited by PTI.

âWithout the Collegium's immediate action, the High Court of Jharkhand faces the prospect of yet another interim Acting Chief Justice arrangementâ¦ I hope it (the Collegium) will not disagree with me that the office of the Chief Justice is central to the administrative and judicial functioning of a high court,â he wrote.

Soren also stressed the need for stable judicial leadership to maintain public confidence in the justice delivery system, saying frequent leadership transitions could disrupt the functioning of the institution.

World.title: NGT scanner on waste dumping near J&K’s saffron fields
World.content:
SRINAGAR:

(NGT) has constituted a committee of experts to assess environmental damage and inspect a municipal dumping site in J&Kâs Pampore after an activist filed a petition alleging such waste disposals were threatening the areaâs vast saffron fields.

The NGT division bench of Justice Prakash Shrivastava and Afroz Ahmad directed the committee to submit a report in eight weeks. The order, passed recently, comes at a time when saffron cultivation has fallen nearly 35% over the years, posing serious challenges for farmers. Saffron, locally known as kesar, is believed to have originated in southern Europe but is now widely cultivated in Iran, Spain and Turkey. In India, it is primarily grown in Pampore.



The NGT-formed panel will include representatives of Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), to be nominated by its vice-chancellor, regional director of the Union environment ministry and a nominee of the J&K Pollution Control Committee.

The members visit the Pampore site, in Pulwama district, find out the extent of municipal and plastic waste dumped there and ascertain if necessary clearances have been secured.





âThe committee will also ascertain the effect of dumping of the waste upon the crop,â the order states.

In his NGT plea, environmental activist Raja Muzaffar Bhat has alleged that Pamporeâs municipal body was illegally dumping harmful materials at its solid waste management facility in Patlibagh-Galander area.

Untreated waste was generating leachate that was seeping into underground water sources and flowing through channels into the Jhelum river, located less than 1km away, Bhatâs plea says.

The dumping site is located in a notified saffron-growing area protected under Saffron Act, 2007, attracting rodents and porcupines which further damage crops, Bhatâs plea says. He submitted with his petition a report by the local pollution control officer about âheaps of unsegregated and untreated waste, including single-use plastic items and packaging materialsâ. âApart from this site, they are using saffron fields for dumping municipal waste,â Bhat told TOI.

World.title: NCB busts interstate pharma drugs syndicate
World.content:
The agency seized more than five lakh tablets, capsules and bottles of pharmaceutical preps

SRINAGAR: The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has busted an interstate network involved in supplying pharmaceutical drugs from Delhi to the Kashmir Valley and has arrested four suspects so far.The agency seized more than five lakh tablets, capsules and bottles of pharmaceutical preparations containing tramadol hydrochloride, alprazolam, nitrazepam and codeine.The NCB said the investigation is focused on identifying where codeine-based cough syrup (CBCS) was diverted from the legitimate pharmaceutical supply chain and disrupting the network that moved it into illicit circulation.In a statement, the NCB statement said that acting on specific intelligence, its Jammu unit intercepted a Srinagar-bound passenger bus near a toll plaza in Chenani in Udhampur district on Nov 16. âThe team seized around 7 kg of CBCS from a resident of Doda,â the statement said, adding that follow-up investigation in the Kashmir Valley led to the suspected principal recipient, a resident of Anantnag district, who has been arrested.âPursuing the supply links in Delhi, NCB Jammu and NCB Delhi apprehended persons linked to the Delhi supply operation and recovered 356 bottles of CBCS on Nov 18, 2026,â the statement said.âFurther enquiries led to a clandestine godown operating from rented premises in Sahadara, Delhi. Searches on Nov 18 and 19 yielded more than 5,00,000 tablets, capsules and bottles of pharmaceutical preparations containing tramadol hydrochloride, alprazolam, nitrazepam and codeine,â the NCB said, adding that it has registered a case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

World.title: Ladakh records 70% voting in panchayat polls, 52% in municpal elections
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Ladakh Saturday recorded 70.03% turnout in panchayat elections and 52.4% in municipal council polls, held for the first time since it was declared a Union Territory in 2019.

The young and the elderly, women and men, first-time voters, monks and people from every walk of life exercised their democratic right across villages and towns. The state election commission said the enthusiastic participation reflected the peopleâs deep commitment to grassroots democracy and local self-governance.

The local body polls were held amid protests led by Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) seeking deferment of Dec 4 elections to eight autonomous hill development councils, citing the harsh winter.



The panchayat elections covered 192 Panchayat Halqas across eight districts, comprising 192 sarpanch positions and 1,428 panch seats. Of these, 55 sarpanches and 1,186 panches were elected unopposed, while polling was conducted for the remaining 137 sarpanch and 242 panch seats.

The municipal council elections covered 38 wards, comprising 21 in Leh and 17 in Kargil. Polling was conducted in all 21 wards of Leh, while four wards in Kargil were filled unopposed and polling was held in the remaining 13 wards.





Election authorities had made elaborate arrangements for the smooth conduct of polling. In Zanskar, helicopters were deployed to airlift polling teams to three remote and road-inaccessible polling stations, enabling the conduct of elections in some of the most isolated settlements.

Ladakh lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena described the day as historic for the region, saying the overwhelming participation in the polls âis a powerful testament to peopleâs unshakeable faith in the democratic process and local self-governanceâ.

However, LAB co-chairperson Chering Dorjay Lakrook and member Sonam Wangchuk alleged at a joint press conference in Leh that a âlarge number of peopleâ had been left out of the electoral rolls. âI wanted to go to my own village to vote but I was told that the polling booth there had been shifted to another village. That is why villagers in my village boycotted the polls,â Wangchuk said.

World.title: Humayun, Sher Shah and ‘one fort’: Pakistan minister highlights Purana Quila’s layered history at SCO forum
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Pakistan minister Musadik Malik invoked Mughal emperor Humayun and Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri while addressing the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Delhi's historic Purana Quila on Saturday.

Referring to the fort's layered history, Malik said it reflected how two rival rulers had contributed to the construction of the same monument.

Speaking at the thematic session titled 'Civilisational and Cultural Expressions', chaired by Union culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Malik described Purana Quila as a symbol of multiple historical influences.

"This (Purana) Quila, where we are sitting, is in itself a story.



A fort, whose foundation was laid by Humayun, who had a descent from the Timurid (dynasty) linkage.. came from Central Asia. And Sher Shah Suri further built on it, who was an Afghan. One wall, two rivals, meaning two rulers and one fort, meaning two layers and one trench," the Pakistan minister said.

Malik also shared a video of his address on X and wrote in Urdu that the Quila is a "story".

He further emphasised the importance of dialogue between different identities and cultures, saying, "dialogue is between distinct identities, and between diversity, and, we have come here for that dialogue only".





"Meaning, many voices, many identities, and their dialogues, and free flow of ideas, among them... free flow of identities. The wisdom lies in it, the wisdom lies in embracing it, embellishing it. So, wisdom is there in it, and needs courage too. And, we have gathered here to celebrate these two things," he added.

The remarks come amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. Malik is visiting India for the first time.

Three-day SCO civilisational forum at Purana Quila

India is hosting the three-day SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Quila to highlight the country's rich civilisational heritage and the layers of history spanning thousands of years.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the summit on Friday evening in the presence of delegates from SCO member countries, including Malik.

The choice of venue also draws attention to the fort's historical significance.

Humayun, the second Mughal emperor, laid its foundation, while Sher Shah Suri later expanded it. Humayun's Tomb, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Delhi's Nizamuddin area, is also located nearby.

The tomb is the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent. It marked a major departure from earlier funerary traditions and is considered a pioneering example of Indo-Islamic architecture, according to the culture ministry.

As part of the forum, a special exhibition titled 'Astitva: The Essence of our Existence' has been organised for SCO delegates. It offers an account of Delhi's history through archaeological evidence dating from 1,200 BC to 1200 CE. The exhibition includes excavated remains, artefacts, architectural fragments and other significant discoveries.

World.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to reach Delhi on Sunday for his first foreign bilateral trip - what's on agenda
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Balendra Shah will begin a two-day state visit to India on Sunday, his first overseas bilateral state visit since taking office in March.

"The visit will serve as an important opportunity to review our wide-ranging cooperative partnership with a forward-looking perspective, maximising mutual benefits for the peoples of both countries," Nepal's foreign ministry said in a statement.

Shah, an ex-Kathmandu mayor and a former rapper, will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation comprising finance minister Swarnim Wagle, foreign affairs minister Shishir Khanal, his chief advisor Kumar Byanjankar, and other senior government officials.

Balendra Shah's itinerary in New Delhi

Shah is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday, after which they will jointly inaugurate several energy-related projects.



The two sides will also sign and exchange bilateral agreements covering various areas of cooperation.

The two prime ministers will address a joint press conference, followed by a luncheon hosted by PM Modi in honour of the visiting Nepali leader.

During his visit, Shah will also call on President Droupadi Murmu and pay tributes at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat.

He is also scheduled to attend the Nepal-India Business Forum, which aims to strengthen trade and economic ties between the two countries.





What's likely to be discussed

According to ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, India and Nepal are expected to discuss issues including development cooperation and people-to-people ties.

"All these issues will be discussed: development cooperation, people-to-people ties, energy ties, connectivity, and some of the newer areas of cooperation such as startups, technology, innovation, and sports. Cricket links have also become an important connection between India and Nepal.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

This is a very important visit for us," Jaiswal told reporters at a weekly news briefing in New Delhi on Friday.

Shah is also expected to discuss Indian assistance for the reconstruction of areas affected by the devastating floods in August, Reuters reported, citing Nepalese officials.

The August 26 floods killed 1,500 people, left more than 5,200 missing and destroyed roads, bridges, power plants, farms and homes.

Nepal is also likely to discuss with India an additional route for commercial flights from the west to Bhairahawa, near Lumbini, the birthplace of Gautam Buddha, and the tourist city of Pokhara.

World.title: 'Modi ji should apologise': Congress alleges PM's Lucknow event led to cancellation of four weddings
World.content:

chief

"Modi ji should apologise to the families whose four weddings have been cancelled. They should ask for it and certainly offer an apology," Rai said.
