World.title: 11 killed in burst of violence in northern Mexico after capture of cartel leader Meza Flores
World.content:
A burst of violence in Mexico's Sinaloa state after authorities captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro", left at least 11 people dead, authorities have said.

Meza Flores, one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives, was captured and flown to Mexico City on Saturday (November 21, 2026) after a heavy firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen overnight left residents of the city of Guasave terrorised and trucks and businesses burning.

Mexico's Defense Cabinet on Saturday afternoon (November 21) said seven alleged cartel gunmen and four Mexican soldiers were killed.

Flores climbed the cartel ranks to lead the Beltrán-Leyva cartel and later became the leader of his own group, the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organisation. The United States had a $5 million reward offer for information leading to his arrest, and he was wanted for trafficking drugs to the U.S. and illegally carrying firearms.

Mexico's government said in a report early Saturday (November 21) that intelligence from the Trump administration helped authorities capture him, but provided few details about how authorities in Mexico and the United States coordinated to detain Meza Flores.

He was also a key ally to "Los Mayos", a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, which was designated as a foreign terrorist organisation by the Trump administration last year. His capture represents a blow to the cartel as it fights with another faction for control of the northern Mexican state.

Authorities in the United States and Mexico celebrated the arrest as a security win. U.S. President Donald Trump has pressured Mexico's government to go after criminal groups.

As a fierce firefight settled into a tense calm Saturday, experts warned that picking off capos could set off another wave of violence in a region already caught up in a power struggle between warring cartel factions.

Mexican forces’ move against cartel fuels violence

The capture of Meza Flores and his number 2 in the city of Guasave, Sinaloa, set off a wave of violence when a firefight broke out around 7 p.m. on Friday (November 20), according to residents of the 290,000-person municipality. Soon, military helicopters and drones were flying overhead and opened fire on key locations across the city.

Videos show screaming civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, burning cars and businesses, and circling helicopters shooting at people below. Such shows of force by cartels are common following the capture or killing of leaders.

"The fighting was happening all over Guasave," said Alma Camacho, a Guasave resident and local journalist. "It spread throughout the city."

Mexican authorities said they used "stealth and surprise" to arrest Meza Flores, establishing a security perimeter around the building where he was located. After coming under attack with guns and explosives from suspected cartel operatives, armed forces personnel entered a home and detained him. He was later taken by aircraft to Mexico City to appear before prosecutors.

Video shared by authorities shows heavily armed men in camouflage escorting a man through a dimly lit house and putting him in the back of a truck. No casualties have been reported so far as a result of the operation.

Because of the violence, the Mexican army and National Guard special forces were unable to extract Meza Flores from Guasave until 4 a.m. on Saturday (November 21), said a federal official who spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorised to discuss the case.

"Getting him [Meza Flores] out was extraordinary," the official said, describing an intense response by members of the criminal group who maintained at least "10 roadblocks" with burning vehicles on Guasave's streets.

Terror in Sinaloa

Guasave resident and firefighter Paola Sánchez said thousands of people were terrorised late Friday as they took shelter from intense gunfire in grocery stores and other locations.

"Last night, many businesses were burned ... along with cars and trucks," Mr. Sánchez told The Associated Press.

She said the city's firefighters had to take shelter at their station and wait until Saturday morning (November 21) for orders from their superiors to dispatch the first crews to check whether any businesses or vehicles were still burning.

An uneasy calm seemed to settle over the city on Saturday (November 21). Mexican Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch wrote on X on Saturday morning (November 21) that armed forces would remain deployed in Sinaloa state to protect civilians. Authorities didn't provide details on how many people were wounded or killed in the clashes.

Burned out trucks continued to line the freeway leading into the town, blocking roadways on Saturday (November 21). "The aftermath of last night's war still lingers. Burned cars in the streets, several Oxxo stores completely burned down," Mr. Camacho said, referring to a chain of convenience stores in Mexico.

Guasave residents remained "very afraid" because security forces were absent from the streets, Mr. Camacho said.

Capture prompts celebration and warnings

Meza Flores' detention marks another high-profile capture of a cartel leader as Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum faces pressure from Trump to crack down on cartels. Sheinbaum has gone after illegal groups more aggressively than her predecessors, and homicides have dipped significantly in her two years in office.

The U.S. and Mexican governments celebrated the capture on Saturday (November 21), with the DEA commending Mexican authorities.

"Results like these don't happen overnight. They are built on sustained cooperation and trust. This is what partners can accomplish together," U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson said in an X post. "We will continue the hunt."

Mexican Security Secretary García Harfuch called the detention "an important step in pacifying Sinaloa". Sheinbaum's government has targeted a number of cartel kingpins, including Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, known as "El Mencho", who was killed by the military in February.

Mexican security analyst David Saucedo said the capture of Meza Flores marked another case of the governments of Mexico and the U.S. increasingly falling back on a longstanding security strategy that critics warn could fuel more violence in the long run.

The so-called kingpin strategy relies on zeroing in on capos like Meza Flores as a way to combat cartels. But experts say it often triggers violent power disputes among groups, like the one under way in Sinaloa.

"What is evident is this is a product of pressure from the United States," Mr. Saucedo said. "What they do is capture high-profile kingpins — the leaders — but they don't dismantle the entire organisation. They arrested the number 1 and number 2, but the entire network of hit men, street-level drug dealers, businesses and political and police connections remains intact."

World.title: Amid cold wave, students’ indefinite strike against J&K recruitment board scam gathers steam
World.content:
Protesting government job aspirants on Saturday (November 21, 2026) launched an indefinite strike in Srinagar amid a cold wave over the government’s failure to act against the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB), the main recruitment agency of J&K that has become mired in a cheating scam that has led to 16 arrests so far.

While former Member of Parliament (MP) Aga Syed Ruhullah joined the protesters in Srinagar, other regional parties also demanded the cancellation of all examinations held by the Board and called for “fixing the responsibility”.

The peaceful sit-in was forcibly broken up by police on Saturday night (November 21), said the protesters. “Students and Aga sahib were removed from the site against their will. The demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA [Finance Accounts Assistant] rigging. This fight isn’t over,” said one protester.

Speaking at the Sher-i-Kashmir Park earlier, Mr. Ruhullah said the protest is a “rare effort to open up space where youth could fight for their rights”.

“We demand that heads must roll. We have the elected government and an unelected government ruling J&K. Both share responsibility for it. Unfortunately, there is a sense of complacency. The examinations should be postponed, responsibility for the irregularities fixed and reforms carried out. The administration should engage students and address their concerns,” said Mr. Ruhullah.

Mr. Ruhullah joined scores of students and aspirants who held a sit-in all day in Srinagar. With evening temperature dipping, a spokesman of Mr. Ruhullah said, “There was no food or blankets. No entry. Students on a peaceful sit-in are being frozen out on a bitter Srinagar night. Their only crime is asking for justice over the alleged Finance Accounts Assistant recruitment rigging.”

The night temperature has dipped to around zero degrees Celsius in Srinagar amid a severe cold wave.

On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts.

Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. Besides 16 arrests made in the case, the police said it filed three First Information Reports (FIRs) and recovered eight wireless devices, 22 mobile phones and four vehicles of the accused.

However, Board chairman Shrikant Balasaheb Suse said the “examination was not compromised by a paper leak or mass malpractice” and announced that the upcoming exams will be held “as per the schedule”.

Facing a growing public outcry, J&K Education Minister Shamim Firdous said strict action should be taken “if any irregularities or rigging are found”.

“Students, who have worked hard, deserve justice. We have already ordered an inquiry to identify the irregularities, and action will follow if evidence is found,” said Ms. Firdous.

In spite of assurances of action by Ms. Firdous, there was no let-up in demands of regional parties to postpone all examinations.

“We demand a thorough investigation into all lapses. It is very imperative. The syndicate must be exposed and dismantled. There should be no further recruitment until the mafia is identified and held accountable,” said Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti.

PDP legislator Muntazir Mehdi wrote a letter to J&K Chief Secretary Sajjan Singh Yadav and sought his intervention into “the concerns surrounding the FAA examination and the growing distrust among aspirants”.

“Elected representatives must be heard, and their concerns addressed. That is how people’s faith in democratic institutions is strengthened,” said Mr. Mehdi in the letter.

Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq said such frequent recruitment scams “amount to playing with the futures of thousands of educated young people”.

“Employment opportunities for young people are extremely limited in J&K. When even these few limited employment opportunities fall prey to allegations of scams, fraud and irregularities, it is a grave injustice to the students and young candidates who spend years preparing for these examinations and pin their hopes for a better future on them,” said the Mirwaiz.

J&K Peoples Conference legislator Sajad Gani Lone said, “I don’t understand why cheating happens more in Jammu. The Chief Minister was backing away from the issue by saying the JKSSB was not under his domain. In the last five years, the Board’s record was bad. I think this institution needs a complete overhaul.”

World.title: Vasan urges political parties to fight for Cauvery water rights
World.content:
Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Saturday urged the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) to direct the Karnataka government to release water due to Tamil Nadu. He also sought the cooperation of political parties in Tamil Nadu in securing the State’s rights by setting aside their differences.

In a statement, Mr. Vasan expressed shock over the Supreme Court dismissing Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking the release of 11 thousand million cubic feet of Cauvery water by Karnataka.

He said that, in the past, the Karnataka government had not complied with the directions of the CWMA and had acted in a step-motherly manner.

Farmers in the Cauvery delta are under severe economic distress due to an acute shortage of water for irrigation. The Karnataka government should understand that the Cauvery water-sharing issue and the Mekedatu issue are not only river water disputes, but also the lifelines of the people of Tamil Nadu, Mr. Vasan added.

World.title: Municipal staff transfers to move online by Tamil Nadu govt., with vacancies displayed on portal
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government has introduced online counselling for transfers and postings of employees in municipal corporations, municipal councils and town panchayats, covering employees in the lower and middle levels of the government pay structure, including posts such as assistants, junior assistants and superintendents. The guidelines were issued through two Government Orders (G.O.s) by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department dated November 19, 2026.

The counselling will be based on vacancies and station seniority. The online portal is being developed by the respective heads of departments and will be introduced shortly, an official said.

Regarding whether employees would be able to raise grievances relating to seniority or other issues through the portal, the official said the department would be asked to incorporate a provision for submitting representations online. The portal would also provide details of vacancies and the procedure for applying for transfers, he said.

According to the guidelines, general transfers will ordinarily be conducted between April 1 and May 31 every year. Applications will be received through the online portal between March 1 and 31. Employees who have completed three years of service in a post or station will be liable for transfer during this period, subject to the availability of vacancies.

Transfers during the non-transfer period, between June 1 and March 31, will be permitted only on administrative grounds, including promotions, disciplinary reasons, complaints, long leave arrangements and other administrative exigencies.

All transfers, including those sought by employees, during the transfer period will be processed through the online portal. The guidelines also provide for a maximum of three alternative station preferences in transfer applications.

The official said counselling for Executive Officers of town panchayats had already been conducted and postings issued based on it.

World.title: T.N. to set up Statewide online registry of voluntary donors with rare blood groups
World.content:
To ensure timely availability of compatible blood for patients with rare blood groups during medical emergencies, the “Tamil Nadu Rare Blood Group Donor Registry” will be established under the Tamil Nadu State Blood Transfusion Council (TNSBTC).

In an order issued recently, the State government permitted the Project Director of the TNSBTC to establish the registry.

The TNSBTC will develop, maintain, and periodically update the Statewide online database of voluntary donors with rare blood groups.

The order directed all licensed blood centres in Tamil Nadu to identify eligible rare blood group donors and facilitate their enrolment in the registry with due consent.

The council is authorised to prescribe appropriate operational guidelines, standard procedures, and mechanisms for registration, verification, updating, utilisation and confidentiality of the registry.

The Project Director had said that rare blood groups posed a significant challenge in managing patients requiring urgent blood transfusion. Timely identification and mobilisation of compatible blood donors are essential to ensure uninterrupted transfusion support in times of emergency, and it is for this that the registry had been proposed.

At present, information regarding donors with rare blood groups is maintained at different blood centres and is not available through a unified State-level mechanism. This may result in delays in identifying and mobilising suitable donors during critical situations.

Blood Donor Clubs

In addition, the government also permitted the TNSBTC to establish “Blood Donor Clubs” in colleges having functional Red Ribbon Clubs (RRC) in the State. Currently, 2,379 RRCs function across the State. Each blood donor club will have a faculty coordinator and a student coordinator. Each club will be linked to a nearby licensed blood centre, and regular voluntary blood donation camps should be organised.

The order noted that voluntary blood donation is an essential component of safe and adequate blood supply. Sustaining an adequate blood supply requires continuous mobilisation of voluntary non-remunerated blood donors, particularly among the youth and student population.

RRCs have an established a network of student members, faculty coordinators and institutional support. The RRCs can provide an effective platform for introducing a dedicated Blood Donor Club in colleges without creating a new institutional mechanism, it said.

Both these initiatives were among the announcements made by the Health Minister in the Assembly early this year.

World.title: Chennai Corporation relaxes road tender rules
World.content:
The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has relaxed the conditions for its 2026-27 road relaying contracts and will generate road work orders through the Tamil Nadu government’s e-procurement portal hosted by the Union government’s National Informatics Centre.

These changes are aimed at widening contractor participation and curbing cartelisation of bidders, according to a GCC official.

Online work orders

The new procedure will enable work orders to be generated online after the financial bids are opened, negotiations are completed and letters of acceptance are issued. Contractors will no longer have to approach officials separately to obtain work orders, a crucial document required to commence execution, an official said.

The GCC has also brought in other changes to its 2026-27 road contract conditions.

It has changed the conditions governing the submission of additional security deposits. Only the lowest bidder will now have to furnish the deposit, within two days of the first negotiation, through NEFT, RTGS or an electronic bank guarantee. Earlier, the requirement applied at the tender-opening stage.

The change is intended to protect the confidentiality of financial bids, the official said.

The Corporation has also permitted bidders to use either owned or registered leased centralised hot mix plants, subject to a valid consent to operate certificate from the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board. The plant must be located within 40 km of the GCC boundary.

Bidders can participate in more than one package, subject to fulfilling the eligibility conditions.

The proposed works cover 753 roads across all 15 zones of the GCC, including 66 bus route roads (BRRs). The works span a total length of 167.55 km, of which 43.86 km comprises BRRs. The estimated cost is ₹149.12 crore, including ₹68.31 crore for BRR works. The tenders have been scheduled for November 27, December 3 and 7, 2026, according to the project details.

Safety deposit

The official said the GCC will retain 2.5% of the contract amount during the three-year defect liability period, as a safeguard against any defects in the work. This amount will be withheld for three years, during which contractors will be responsible for rectifying defects. They can replace the withheld amount with an e-bank guarantee after completing the work. This provision is to safeguard the GCC against contractors quoting steep discounts and failing to complete the works, he said.

The official said GCC tenders had generally attracted bids quoting rates higher than the estimated cost in the past. However, the Chennai Corporation had recently been receiving bids quoting substantial discounts, sometimes as much as 20% to 30% below the estimated cost.

The GCC rejected the request to relax the pollution consent requirement, citing National Green Tribunal directions, but permitted the use of registered leased plants subject to the prescribed conditions.

World.title: AIPC Tamil Nadu to support MSMEs through professional network
World.content:
The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Tamil Nadu chapter should function as a professional support network for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), helping them access legal, financial and technical expertise, said its national chairman Madhu Goud Yaskhi at the organisation’s annual summit in Chennai on Saturday.

Mr. Yaskhi proposed that chartered accountants, lawyers, engineers and IT professionals associated with the AIPC volunteer their time to help MSMEs with taxation, regulatory compliance, financial management and delayed payments.

He said over ₹7 lakh crore owed to small enterprises across India remained stuck in delayed payments, with large companies often taking more than 120 days to clear dues despite the statutory 45-day limit.

The AIPC could also take up delayed payments by State public sector undertakings with the Tamil Nadu government, he said. Lawyers could help MSMEs pursue their dues through legal notices, while chartered accountants could assist with invoice discounting and compliance.

Outgoing AIPC chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty said Congress needed to reconnect with professionals in major urban centres, where it had lost electoral ground since 2014, he said.

He also urged professionals to help implement and promote the Tamil Nadu government’s policies, including the Private University Bill, startup initiatives and tourism projects, saying the Congress’s participation in the coalition government brought responsibilities beyond its share in the Cabinet.

After the event, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan told reporters that the Private University Bill passed by the Assembly had received the Governor’s assent.

The government would prepare a standard operating procedure and issue guidelines for its implementation, he said. The legislation aimed to attract foreign universities to Tamil Nadu and provide students access to international-standard educational facilities within the State.

Lok Sabha MP C. Robert Bruce and Rajya Sabha MP Christopher Tilak were present.

World.title: Gandhi is the core ideological enemy of the Sangh Parivar: Ramachandra Guha
World.content:
While early years after Independence in India saw excessive veneration of Gandhi, the recent trends have shifted to a “venomous detestation” of the man by the right-wing ecosystem led by the Sangh Parivar, historian Ramachandra Guha said here on Saturday while discussing his latest book Arguments with Gandhi.

“When I was young, the ethos in India was excessive veneration of Gandhi. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. That should be very evident from whatever they say about Gandhi. Actually, Gandhi is their core ideological enemy, as he has once been of the Left.” Dr. Guha averred. Citing an analogy, he said that Prime Minister Modi, in his article on Gandhi in the New York Times on his 150th birth anniversary, “praised him for everything except Hindu-Muslim harmony”. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan.

Elaborating on the reasons for such attacks on Gandhi, Dr. Guha emphasised that Gandhi had come to represent the feminine in the eyes of the “macho Right”, what with his non-violent policy, inter-faith harmony, his scepticism of the State, or his scepticism of progress.

“Gandhi raises almost all the important questions of human existence today. You can think of no other thinker; he catches so many vital aspects of our lives,” Dr. Guha observed, as the conversation veered towards his ideas of non-violent science which influenced several scientists, including J.B.S. Haldane and Laurie Baker. Gandhi, he said, derived his principles from all traditions and belief systems – Jainism, Vaishnavism, Christianity, and even communism. His attitude to gender, religion, or non-violence evolved through his engagements with various philosophies.

“I do not see him as a quintessentially Hindu thinker, quintessentially Indian thinker, [or] quintessentially traditional thinker. He transcends these lanes. Or Leftist, Rightist, Conservative; he is all three,” Dr. Guha added.

On the question of caste and the equations with the Ambedkarite principles, Dr. Guha said that Gandhi was a guilt-ridden upper caste while Ambedkar was a dalit without emancipation and they could only take those paths. From the perspective of history and the future of India, the paths are converging. Asked if Gandhi’s methods are lost in the era of social media, he said the “cockroaches showed that they have it”. If the book came out a few months later, he said he would have added a few paragraphs on the Cockroach Janata Party movement.

World.title: ﻿Cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal joins BJP, appointed as special invitee member of party’s OBC Morcha’s NEC
World.content:
Cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal has joined the BJP and the party has named him special invitee member in its OBC Morcha’s national executive committee announced on Saturday. He has been named from Delhi.

The leg-spinner who has played International cricket for India and has been part of various IPL teams had recently met Rajya Sabha member and BJP’s OBC morcha national president Amar Pal Maurya recently in Delhi.

Confirming that Chahal has joined the party, Amar Pal Maurya told The Indian Express, “He had shown interest in politics and expressed a wish to work with BJP. He has been named in the national executive committee,”.

World.title: Interactive: How Mexico captured El Chapo Isidro, FBI’s most wanted cartel boss
World.content:
Mexican military forces captured one of the most wanted suspected drug lords, Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” as well as two other leaders of his drug-trafficking organisation on Friday night following a major operation in the state of Sinaloa, Mexico’s security chief said on Saturday ⁠morning.

Chapo ​Isidro was one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives. For over 20 years, according to the US State Department, he and his criminal organisation smuggled vast amounts of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, and marijuana into the United ​States.

His arrest set off gunfire across the city of Guasave. Open the case file to follow how the night unfolded, who he is, and how four decades of Mexico’s cartel wars led here.

World.title: I’m just happy to play great tennis in the tie-break when it matters: Alcaraz after beating Shelton
World.content:
Carlos Alcaraz felt “a little problem” in his hamstring while facing Daniil Medvedev at the ATP Finals. He beat Medvedev in straight sets anyway. Alcaraz minimized his movement in the next match against Flavio Cobolli, having his left thigh and right wrist strapped, and right knee taped. He routed Cobolli too.

Less than 24 hours later, an in-form Ben Shelton — who had bested him in a Flushing Meadows epic in September — awaited. The world No.4 was not going to offer him loose serves or shallow strokes to pounce on. Alcaraz won anyway.

Rather than worsening (due to the niggle), the Spaniard’s mobility and shotmaking improved through the course of an absorbing semi-final. He brushed aside an early setback to emerge victor 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7-1) in Turin. It was Alcaraz’s 13th consecutive win on Tour, and on indoor courts.



Shelton started the match with a double fault but firmed up to hold serve confidently, first up. The Alcaraz serve, in sharp contrast to the three group-stage matches, looked shaky right away. The hamstring came into play; it wasn’t the Alcaraz we’d been seeing since his comeback at the US Open.

His movement hindered and strokes patchy, the No.3 was suddenly vulnerable. Shelton swatted an unaesthetic but supremely effective forehand return to break the No.3. It was the first time Alcaraz’s serve was broken this campaign — he had claimed 26 straight service games in the group phase.

‘Carlito’ did not give in to the niggle. He let out a bellow and goaded himself on. His next service game was better, and the following one even more so. But the damage was done by then.

Alcaraz was now serving more tightly and staving off Shelton’s potent returns of serve. He just wasn’t gliding fast enough across court when at the receiving end. Shelton, with his big serve and vigorous net play, capitalised. There were no more surprises in the first set, and an ace down the centre sealed it for the southpaw.



The second set was a different story. As great players tend to do, Alcaraz found a way. Walking the tightrope between playing full tilt and aggravating his hamstring trouble, the seven-time Grand Slam winner began nailing his groundstrokes again. He kept challenging Shelton’s service and eventually dismantled it in Game 8. Alcaraz dealt the killer blow in the next game with a precise backhand pass. A decider was on.

The third set entailed cat-and-mouse stuff. Shelton’s serve was put to the test again at 3-3, as Alcaraz foraged for his first break. The American hung on at 30-30 with a world-class drop shot that floated over the net, cross-court. With neither player ceding service, the set headed to an inevitable tie-break.

That is when Alcaraz stamped his authority on the match. After three back-to-back aces — one from Shelton and two from Alcaraz — the 23-year-old earned the first mini-break. Two forehand misfires handed Alcaraz a 5-1 lead. He finished off in style, with a backhand return down the line that landed inches off the baseline corner.

“I’m just really happy. I was frustrated at the beginning, I didn’t start the match how I wanted to,” Alcaraz said courtside after the fighting win. “Ben pushes you to the limit everytime. I didn’t start well, with the early break, but I’m happy I came back in the second set, playing great tennis, step-by-step.”



Alcaraz said Shelton “raised his level in the third set”, and so did he. “I’m just happy to play great tennis in the tie-break when it matters. I’m excited for (the final) tomorrow and happy for today.”

World.title: Vintage Beetle, private pool and Rs 1.75 lakh Mahabharata chessboard: Inside PV Sindhu’s hilltop home
World.content:

From a private swimming pool to a photo wall, a vintage Volkswagen Beetle to an iconic Mahabharata chessboard, the power couple took the guest through their 3-storey hilltop home inside a gated community.

World.title: FIDE slams Carlsen over “lack of respect,” refers him to Ethics Panel for Total Chess forfeits
World.content:
“FIDE considers such conduct unacceptable and inconsistent with the standards of professional behavior expected of participants in official competitions,” the federation added, confirming the matter has been sent to the EDC “for an independent assessment of potential violations of the FIDE Ethics and Disciplinary Code”.

While FIDE noted that several players, including Carlsen, also forfeited games in matches that had already been mathematically decided, it drew a sharp line at his conduct against Artemiev. Carlsen skipped both Rapid games on Day 1 and the Fast Classic game on Day 2 of their 17th-place match before winning an Armageddon tiebreaker.

❗️FIDE Statement on the Conclusion of the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot 2026❗️

Following the conclusion of the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot 2026 in Budapest, the International Chess Federation (FIDE) congratulates the medalists, GM Alireza Firouzja, GM Anish Giri, and GM Fabiano Caruana. FIDE also extends its thanks to Kjell Madland, the entire Total Chess team, and the Hungarian hosts for organizing this important pilot event ahead of the inaugural full season of the Tour in 2027.

At the same time, FIDE expresses serious concern over several instances of players forfeiting scheduled games during the tournament. Some of these forfeits, including those by GM Magnus Carlsen, occurred in matches whose outcomes had already been mathematically decided. Although such actions breached the tournament regulations requiring all scheduled games to be played, they did not affect the results of the respective matches.

However, GM Magnus Carlsen also forfeited three scheduled games over two days of his match against GM Vladislav Artemiev while the outcomes of the respective contests were still undecided. Such conduct undermines the principles of fair play and the fairness of the competition and is unprecedented at the highest level of professional chess. These forfeited games had a significant meaning, seriously impacting the very top of the rating standings.

FIDE considers such conduct unacceptable and inconsistent with the standards of professional behavior expected of participants in official competitions. Given GM Carlsen’s stature and his significant role in promoting chess, such actions are particularly concerning, as they may damage the reputation of competitions and demonstrate a lack of respect for opponents, spectators, and tournament partners.

Accordingly, FIDE will refer the relevant materials to the FIDE Ethics and Disciplinary Commission (EDC) for an independent assessment of potential violations of the FIDE Ethics and Disciplinary Code.

Furthermore, the officiating during the event fell short of fundamental standards, as the arbiters effectively abdicated their responsibility to uphold the FIDE Laws of Chess and tournament regulations. Accordingly, the actions of the arbiters involved will be referred to the FIDE Arbiters’ Commission (ARB) and its Disciplinary Sub-Committee (DSC) for thorough examination and assessment.

As the Budapest event was intended to test the competition format and regulations ahead of the 2027 season, FIDE will continue working closely with Total Chess to refine the rules governing player forfeits and their consequences in order to prevent similar incidents in the future.

FIDE reaffirms its commitment to ensuring that all official competitions are conducted in accordance with the principles of fairness, sporting integrity, and respect for all participants.

Timur Turlov

FIDE President

Viswanathan Anand

FIDE Deputy President

📷 Total Chess / Michal Walusza
